The husband-and-wife duo will attend the ceremony at the legendary Grand Ole Opry on Sunday, September 20, in Nashville.

Listeners are invited to celebrate this milestone by streaming "Hey God, It's Me Again" at https://ffm.to/hey-god-its-me-again and following their journey to the awards.

The Swansons received nominations in four distinct categories:

  • Album of the Year — Seven
  • Song of the Year — "Pray"
  • Song of the Year — "Stick & Stones"
  • Duo of the Year

These nominations underscore a meaningful chapter for The Swansons, whose music consistently reflects their shared journey, faith, marriage, and dedication to connecting with listeners through honest, heartfelt songwriting.

Their latest release, "Hey God, It's Me Again," continues this tradition. The song presents a deeply personal message, exploring the everyday conversations people have with God—moments of uncertainty, gratitude, hope, and the universal need for connection.

For The Swansons, their musical endeavor extends beyond song creation. It centers on sharing stories, offering encouragement, and forging connections with audiences through their unique perspective as life and music partners.

The Swansons state, "We're incredibly grateful for this season. Having four nominations alongside the release of our new single makes this a very special time for us. We're honored to be recognized among so many talented independent artists, and we're excited to head to Nashville, celebrate with our fellow musicians, and enjoy the experience together."

The Josie Music Awards annually recognize independent music artists and industry professionals, bringing together musicians from across the country to celebrate independent music.

With four nominations, a brand-new single, and another chapter unfolding in their musical story, The Swansons head to Nashville with grateful hearts and a song to share.

About 

The Swansons are a husband-and-wife music duo bringing heart, harmony, and a shared love of music to every performance. Blending soulful vocals, heartfelt songwriting, and undeniable chemistry, the duo creates a sound that feels both intimate and timeless.

Built on a genuine partnership both on and off the stage, The Swansons connect with audiences through songs that tell stories of love, life, faith, family, and the experiences that shape us. Their performances combine warm vocal harmonies with an engaging, down-to-earth presence that makes every room feel a little more personal.

Whether performing an intimate acoustic set, a full evening of live music, or an original song, The Swansons bring authenticity and emotion to everything they do.

Two voices. One story. A lifetime of music together.

releases.title: Lainey Wilson, Jelly Roll and Lukas Nelson Share Their Songs and Stories at All for the Hall Los Angeles with Special Guest John Mayer
releases.body:
Gala fundraiser concert supports Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum education programs

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "It's gonna be a good night, I feel it in my bones," Lainey Wilson told the audience gathered at All for the Hall Los Angeles right at the start of the show. "We've got a few surprises up our sleeve."

The intimate, guitar pull-style concert, presented Thursday night (Sept.18) at The Novo featured Wilson alongside Jelly Roll and Lukas Nelson taking turns and sharing songs in the classic Nashville songwriter tradition as part of a fundraiser for the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's education programs. It was a night of stories, laughter and, true to Wilson's word, musical surprises.

Before the music began, the museum's CEO Kyle Young touched on the ongoing importance of the institution's mission as a place of education and study as country music continues to grow. "The artists, writers and musicians who have come before and are sure to come after us are worthy of study celebration and honor," he said.

The three performers assembled for All for the Hall Los Angeles were excellent examples of the breadth of country music in the present, each working in a distinct lane but appreciative of one another's contributions. Wilson served as the affable and gracious host, calling Jelly Roll and Nelson her "brothers in country music" and thanking them for coming. "I've got some of the best friends in the world," she said. "Every time I holler at y'all to be somewhere, y'all show up. That's a real friend."

For his part, Nelson demonstrated that he's a twin threat as a soulful singer and a masterful guitar player who performs with intensity. His performances included "Just Outside of Austin" about the place where he grew up, "Forget About Georgia" and "More Than Friends," for which Wilson hopped off her stool and swayed to the rhythm as she added harmony vocals. The pair also paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton by performing a portion of the 2013 Kenny Rogers and Parton duet "You Can't Make Old Friends."

Nelson wrapped up with a searing rendition of "Find Yourself," which he wrote while working on the music for the 2018 film "A Star Is Born." The song first appeared on his album Lukas Nelson & Promise of the Real, and it got an immediate endorsement from the film's female lead, Lady Gaga. "She loved it so much," he said. "She sang on the actual recording of the song."

Jelly Roll was quick to show his appreciation of Nelson's talents. "You're so good, it's almost hard to like you," he quipped. His banter kept the audience laughing appreciatively throughout the night, whether he was adding playful asides about Wilson's wedding to Devlin Hodges ("That wedding was fancy. Everything was free!") or his colorful past on the wrong side of the law. The Nashville native effortlessly blended humor with the sincerity of his songs, which were inspired by the struggle, doubt and redemption that have marked his journey, performing his hits "Liar," "I Am Not Okay," "Need a Favor" and "Save Me," which featured powerful vocal accompaniment from Wilson. 

"Thank you for wearing your heart on your sleeve," Wilson said to Jelly Roll.

Wilson was brimming with down-home charm and in fine voice as she talked about her life and journey. As she introduced "4X4XU," she noted that she had married a man who goes by the nickname of "Duck."

"I thought I couldn't get any more redneck, and God's like, 'I've got jokes!'" Wilson talked about her family's history taming horses before launching into "Wildflowers and Wild Horses," and belted the high note of "Heart Like a Truck" with gusto, earning enthusiastic applause as she did it. "I have to sing that note for the rest of my life," she said. "Every time I come up on it, I'm like, 'Lord Jesus, you better be with me now!"

To cap things off, Wilson had a special guest waiting in the wings and brought out John Mayer to the audience's delight. The pair gave the debut live performance of their recently recorded collaboration "Phone, Keys, Wallet," with Mayer adding harmonies and his fluid electric guitar licks. Wilson recalled recording the song and thinking out loud that she wanted Mayer to be a part of it. They managed to catch him in a Los Angeles studio and played the track over a tinny cellphone speaker, but it was more than enough to get him on board. "I said, 'Let's go,'" Mayer recalled.

The spirit of being game and loving the music shone through with each artist's selections throughout the evening, which Wilson described as a nourishing experience. "My heart is so full," Wilson said. "If y'all keep having me, I'll keep being here."

All for the Hall Los Angeles also featured a performance from the museum's flagship education program, Words & Music, which instructs young people on the craft of writing songs. Students from Manual Arts High School in Los Angeles took the stage with acclaimed country songwriters Liz Rose and Phil Barton to perform an original song created through Words & Music, "I'll Overcome," that offered a message of strength and resilience.

Festivities for All for the Hall kicked off Wednesday (Sept. 17) with a reception for invited attendees at the Los Angeles home of Sarah and Neil Moritz. Songwriters Hillary Lindsey, Lori McKenna and Liz Rose — known collectively as the Love Junkies — were joined by Phil Barton to give a backyard serenade of hits including such award-winning songs as "Humble and Kind," "Blue Ain't Your Color," "You Belong with Me" and "Girl Crush."

All for the Hall was envisioned in 2005 by Country Music Hall of Fame member and board president Vince Gill, who proposed the idea of donating proceeds from one annual performance to the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. In the two decades since, All for the Hall concerts have raised more than $8 million in support of the museum's educational initiatives. Funds raised from the concerts support the museum's educational initiatives, which directly served more than 125,000 people last year through in-person and virtual programs.

About All for the Hall

Launched in 2007, the All for the Hall campaign began with Country Music Hall of Fame member and Museum Board President Vince Gill challenging himself and his fellow artists to donate proceeds of one annual performance to the nonprofit museum. The concert series has rotated between New York, Los Angeles and Dallas. Keith Urban has hosted recurring All for the Hall benefit concerts in Nashville since 2009. In 2024, Blake Shelton hosted an All for the Hall benefit concert in Oklahoma. Funds raised from the events support the museum's educational initiatives, which directly served more than 125,000 people last year through in-person and virtual programs.

About Words & Music

Words & Music® is the Museum's flagship education program that teaches people how to write original songs and connects them to Nashville's professional songwriting community through interactive workshops. For nearly 50 years, Words & Music has served nearly 200,000 participants and currently engages more than 14,000 participants each year — locally, nationally and internationally. Words & Music empowers people to express themselves and share their stories through songwriting. Songwriting builds essential academic skills and supports overall well-being for people of all ages.

About the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum:

The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum collects, preserves and interprets country music and its history for the education and entertainment of diverse audiences. In exhibitions, publications, digital media and educational programs, the museum explores the cultural importance and enduring beauty of the art form. Among the most-visited history museums in the United States, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum was awarded the country's highest honor in the arts, the National Medal of Arts, in 2024. Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the museum is operated by the Country Music Foundation, a not-for-profit 501(c)(3) educational organization chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964. The Country Music Foundation operates Historic RCA Studio B®, Hatch Show Print® poster shop, Haley Gallery, CMA Theater, CMF Records, the Frist Library and Archive and CMF Press. Museum programs are supported in part by the Tennessee Arts Commission.

More information about the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is available at www.countrymusichalloffame.org or by calling (615) 416-2001.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- It's time for a new doll in the dollhouse. MGA Entertainment (MGA), the company behind Bratz®, Rainbow High® and L.O.L. Surprise!®, today released Mirror Mi's first original single and cinematic music video, bringing the brand's six emotion-inspired characters to life through music and live-action storytelling. With the fashion dolls already available at major retailers nationwide, the debut invites fans deeper into Mirror Mi, a connected world where dolls, original music, fashion and emotional storytelling come together.

At the heart of Mirror Mi are six fashion dolls, each embodying a signature emotion through her own distinct personality, point of view and style. Highly detailed fashions, striking silhouettes, long rooted hair, premium styling, 15 points of articulation and collectible accessories make each doll as expressive as the character she represents, giving fans a tangible way to connect with her story and explore the feelings that make her unique.

The cinematic music video takes those personalities and emotions beyond the dollhouse and into an elite performing arts academy, where the characters pursue their creative passions while navigating friendship, self-expression and change. As their feelings evolve and their auras shift, they discover the unique power within every emotion. For the first time, fans can experience the characters' individual styles and relationships unfolding together on screen.

Produced in partnership with London Alley Entertainment, the award-winning creative studio behind some of today's biggest music videos, the release marks the first doll-based project directed by Grammy-nominated filmmaker Colin Tilley, whose distinctive visual storytelling has helped shape some of today's biggest artists.

"With Mirror Mi, we set out to create a world as layered and expressive as the fans it was created for," said Josh Hackbarth, Chief Marketing Officer at MGA Entertainment. "The dolls are the first point of connection, but music and storytelling allow us to reveal so much more about who these characters are and the emotions that shape them. Every look, lyric and storyline uncovers another side of their personalities, giving fans another opportunity to connect and see themselves reflected in these characters."

Meet the six core characters of Mirror Mi:

  • Blaze Maxx™ (Electric): She's tough, outspoken, and brave. Her rockstar energy amps up her friends and fans. She's fiercely loyal and will always have your back.
  • Amora Valentina™ (Love): When she is not crushing, she is gushing about her love for her friends! She has the biggest heart and always sees the good in people.
  • Luna Skye™ (Dreamy): People say she has her head in the clouds, but that's only so she can whisper to the moon. She's full of whimsical ideas, always dream journaling and perfecting her night-time skin care routine.
  • Akiko Kittyama™ (Cozy): She adores all things comfy and cozy! Whether she's planning the perfect chill day or giving a big, warm hug, she knows how to make everyone feel right at home.
  • Shai Meadows™ (Sheepish): Sweet, quiet, and gentle, Shai may not always say what's on her mind, but her kindness and creativity speak for itself. She can make her friends smile without saying a peep!
  • Suki Goldpetal™ (Fragile): Soft-spoken and sensitive, she feels everything deeply. She might appear delicate, but she dances like nobody's watching. When she embraces who she is, she shines like gold. 

The debut music video marks the beginning of Mirror Mi's next chapter across product and entertainment. The story will continue through stylized stop-motion films and an animated short-form series launching later this year, giving fans more ways to follow the characters, their relationships and their emotional journeys.

The brand will also expand its product lineup with Mirror Mi Mini Dolls, small reflections with supercharged emotions. Rather than miniature replicas of the fashion dolls, each four-inch Mini Mi reimagines a character's signature feeling as a heightened collectible expression all its own, designed to be customized, posed, displayed and taken on the go.

Mirror Mi fashion dolls are available now at major retailers nationwide. The debut music video is streaming now on YouTube. Mini Mis launch in October, with select styles available for preorder at MGAE Shop beginning September 23.

For more information and updates on upcoming releases, follow @MirrorMiOfficial on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Spotify.

MGA Entertainment is on a mission to inspire imagination and creativity through innovative toys, entertainment, and experiences that transform play into limitless possibilities. As the largest privately held toy and entertainment company in the U.S., MGA is a global leader in designing and delivering world-class consumer products that spark wonder and drive play forward. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices worldwide, MGA's portfolio spans a dynamic range of original and licensed brands — from toys, dolls, games, and electronics to fashion, home décor, and entertainment content including hit movies and TV series. The company is recognized for its bold approach to storytelling, trendsetting design, and deep commitment to quality. The award-winning MGA family includes fan-favorite brands such as L.O.L. Surprise!™,Little Tikes®, Rainbow High™, Bratz®, MGA's Miniverse™, Yummiland™, CarTuned™, Mirror Mi™, Ninjombie™,  DohKins™,  BABY born®, and Zapf Creation®.  To learn more, visit www.mgae.com and follow MGA on LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram and Facebook.

Promotional products are branded items such as apparel, drinkware, bags and tech accessories used by companies and organizations for marketing. ASI connects tens of thousands of promotional product distributors and suppliers through ESP+, its flagship technology platform for product discovery, sourcing, presentations, quotes and orders.

Gilliland brings more than 18 years of product and technology experience, including 12 years at Zillow, where he most recently served as vice president of product. He will lead the ASI product organization, help shape the future of ESP+ and accelerate development of AI-powered tools designed to make it faster and easier for promotional product professionals to develop campaigns, sell branded merchandise and serve customers.

"Promo is moving too fast for incremental thinking," said ASI CEO Ashish Mittal. "Matt knows how to take complex technology and turn it into products people want to use every day. We're building the technology our members will need next and Matt is exactly the kind of leader who can help us get there faster."

Gilliland's experience at Zillow includes developing technology for a large marketplace connecting real estate professionals, buyers and sellers. At ASI, ESP+ connects distributors with more than 3,000 suppliers and provides access to more than 1.2 million promotional products.

"ASI has spent decades building something technology alone can't create: deep industry expertise, trusted relationships and a thriving community of distributors and suppliers," Gilliland said. "I'm excited to combine that foundation with modern technology that takes work off our members' plates and gives them more time for relationships, creativity and their customers."

ASI is already expanding its use of artificial intelligence. In July, the company launched the AI-powered Inspire Design Studio in ESP+, allowing distributors to create realistic product lifestyle images, find company logos and generate original visual assets within the platform.

About ASI

The Advertising Specialty Institute® (ASI, asicentral.com) is a technology, marketing and information provider serving the $27.7 billion promotional products industry. Founded in 1950, ASI provides technology, research, news, education and events to a network of promotional product suppliers and distributors.

releases.title: Z Squared Inc. CEO David Halabu Discusses AI Data Center Strategy on Two Investor Podcasts
releases.body:
Both Interviews Are Live Now and Available Through the Company's Website and Major Podcast Platforms

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Z Squared Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSQR) ("Z Squared" or the "Company"), a computing infrastructure company expanding into AI infrastructure, today announced that David Halabu, Chief Executive Officer, was recently featured on two investor podcasts: The Wall Street Resource, hosted by Jeff Kone, and The Nano Cap Podcast, hosted by Will Tjernlund. Both interviews are live now.

Speaking with Jeff Kone on The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu outlined how Z Squared acquires existing powered sites - former crypto mining and manufacturing facilities - and retrofits them for AI and high-performance computing use. He described the Company's role as a triple-net landlord, positioned the Union County Campus in Arkansas as its flagship asset, and reiterated the two measures he has asked shareholders to hold the Company to over the next 12 to 18 months: megawatts under management and signed leases.

Speaking with Will Tjernlund on The Nano Cap Podcast, Mr. Halabu traced his background in trading and real estate and the Company's path to the public markets, and detailed the criteria Z Squared applies to a prospective site - price, power and time to power, redundant fiber, water, and county and municipal support. He also addressed the expanding role of behind-the-meter generation as utility interconnection timelines lengthen, and why he expects land and power to remain scarce as AI compute demand grows.

"These conversations were a chance to be direct about what we are building and how it generates revenue," said David Halabu, Chief Executive Officer of Z Squared. "We find power, deliver a shell an AI tenant can use, and grow the site behind it. Over the next 12 to 18 months, measure us on megawatts and leases."

The full interviews can be found via the following links:

The Wall Street Resource (Jeff Kone): Here

The Nano Cap Podcast (Will Tjernlund): Here

Both interviews touched on the Company's previously announced acquisition of Paradox Data, LLC and the Union County Campus it brought with it. Set out below are the questions investors have most frequently raised about that transaction.

What did Z Squared acquire?

Z Squared acquired 100% of the membership interests of Paradox Data, LLC, whose flagship asset is the Union County Campus in El Dorado, Arkansas. The transaction closed on an all-stock basis - no cash at closing and no debt financing.

How much power does the Union County Campus have today, and how does it scale?

The campus has an existing arrangement with Entergy Arkansas for energy service of up to 8.0 MW, plus an executed contract for adjacent land. On The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu described roughly eight megawatts of total capacity and six megawatts of critical capacity available today. The development pathway targets up to 150 MW over time through a combination of utility power and on-site generation, added in phases as utility timelines and customer demand allow.

How does Z Squared expect to generate revenue from the campus?

Z Squared intends to operate as a triple-net landlord, not a compute provider: it expects to lease the land, the building and access to power to tenants - primarily "neocloud" and enterprise AI users - with power treated as a pass-through, and does not intend to buy or lease GPUs. Mr. Halabu said he is hopeful the first six to eight megawatts can be monetized in the early-to-mid 2027 timeframe, subject to the factors described under "Forward-Looking Statements" below.

About Z Squared Inc.

Z Squared Inc. is a computing infrastructure company operating advanced computing equipment and expanding into AI infrastructure. The Company's strategy is built on three principles: lead with power by acquiring operating sites where power is already flowing; build for AI workloads by converting that capacity into AI-ready colocation where the customer brings the compute and runs what they need; and scale with discipline by deploying conversion capital site by site, against signed contracts and operational readiness. Z Squared's common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol "ZSQR" in April 2026.

For more information, visit www.zsquaredinc.com.

releases.title: The live music industry still largely runs on spreadsheets and email threads. ABOSS is the operating system.
releases.body:
AMSTERDAM, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Let's be honest. The live music industry still runs its operations across email threads and spreadsheets at large. Booking agencies, artists, managers and crews coordinate deals, contracts, logistics, and money through systems that were never designed to connect.

ABOSS spent the past decade building an operating system for live music, to solve this problem from a place of deep industry experience. Booking agencies, artists, and crews can manage their shows in one structured environment; from the back-office to center-stage. However, while the hustle is real and the front-end often catches the spotlight, the adoption of new technology in the back-end can move like a slow jam on a Sunday afternoon.

"After all those years, deals are still made on relationships, and they're still being executed in chaos," said Arvid Silos, founder of ABOSS. "If your data lives in inboxes and spreadsheets, you're leaving margins on the table."

ABOSS is built with structured collaboration, dealmaking and business logistics in mind across two environments on the same record. The Agency Platform is where booking agencies run deals, contracts, financial tracking, planning, and pre-production. Artist Pro is where artists and their teams access, review, and work on the same data. A true single source of truth solution.

That split is also the platform's position on who owns the data. Operational information in live music has long sat with the agency, or been scattered across inboxes and spreadsheets. Agencies running on ABOSS are already offering artists a record they can own, access and control, while the agency continues to run the operation. The infrastructure has been there for a decade. However, hardly any artist or manager claims it: of the roughly $1 billion in deal value moving through ABOSS this year, artist-owned records cover about 4%.

A mobile application extends that record onto the road: schedules, travel, and ops, available offline, with summaries. Records are exposed through an open API to empower a new layer of specialized workflows and integrations to improve the live music stack.

SAPPS AI, offering platform-agnostic AI-native micro-apps for live music, is one of those layers that recognizes the power of ABOSS as a system of data supply. AI Models need data that is substantial, owned, structured, secure, and current, contextualized to specific business cases. AI does not replace architecture. That's where ABOSS turns admin into a commercial opportunity in the age of AI.

It's one thing to jump on the AI hypetrain, it's another thing to diligently navigate it, nurturing trust and strongholding this promise ABOSS built the operating system for live music on; to elevate the way we all work in music.

About ABOSS: ABOSS is the operating system for live music. Booking agencies, artists, managers and crews use it to collaboratively manage deals, contracts, finances, logistics and more in a shared environment. https://abossmusic.com

About SAPPS: SAPPS is a platform-agnostic AI-native intelligence layer for the live music industry: specialized applications that connect across systems music businesses already run. https://sapps.ai

releases.title: PBS Western Reserve & Ideastream Public Media Announce Merger to Strengthen the Future of Public Media Across Northeast Ohio and Western Pennsylvania
releases.body:
Long-time partners join forces, retaining staff and sustaining programming across the region

KENT, Ohio and CLEVELAND, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PBS Western Reserve and Ideastream Public Media today announced that their boards have approved an agreement to merge, creating a combined public media organization serving more than 4 million people across Northeast Ohio and Western Pennsylvania.

"At a time of growing pressures for public media organizations nationwide, this is about taking action now to protect something that matters deeply to the communities we serve," said Kevin Martin, President & CEO, Ideastream Public Media. "Despite losing a combined $4 million in annual federal funds, both PBS Western Reserve and Ideastream Public Media are strong today. We believe we can be even stronger together in the future."

This agreement follows a comprehensive due diligence process, undertaken by both organizations in the wake of the July 2025 federal elimination of Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB) funding, reductions in state-level public media funding, rising operating costs, and broader uncertainty around future public funding priorities. That process led to today's determination that coming together now is the best way to ensure long-term effectiveness of public media across every part of the region.

Continuity Across the Combined Organization

PBS Western Reserve and Ideastream Public Media bring a long history of collaboration to the merger, sharing a commitment to local and national news, educational programming, and cultural content.

"For years, our organizations have worked alongside one another with a common belief in the value of public media and the responsibility to serve the people and places that count on us," said Natalie Pillsbury, President & CEO, PBS Western Reserve. "This merger builds on that history and gives us an opportunity to bring our people, experience, and resources together to make our work even stronger."

That commitment to strength and stability extends across the organization. No layoffs are planned as a result of the merger, and the organizations intend to retain all existing staff. The two existing boards will join, ensuring consistent representation from across the region.

Moving forward, Pillsbury will become Chief Content Officer at Ideastream Public Media, succeeding the organization's retiring Chief Content Officer. The role's responsibilities will expand under the combined organization to include strategic oversight of programming and content. Pillsbury brings more than a decade of experience in public media to the position, including prior roles at Ideastream Public Media and WKSU. Martin will remain President & CEO of Ideastream Public Media, a role he has held since 2017.

On the programming side, local and cultural programming, local news coverage, and educational services will continue without interruption across the organizations' NPR and PBS affiliations, including three television stations, WVIZ, WNEO, and WEAO, along with NPR programming on WKSU and classical and jazz music on WCLV and JazzNEO.

A Stronger Future for Public Media

The merger creates a public media footprint spanning Cleveland, Akron, Canton, Youngstown, and Western Pennsylvania, from the region's largest urban population centers to its small, rural communities. Over time, the combined organization's greater capacity could create opportunities to expand educational offerings and locally relevant storytelling, invest in new technologies, and find new ways to connect with audiences throughout the region.

Both organizations are working collaboratively to finalize the transaction, starting with filing for the license transfer with the FCC and completing a merger filing with the State of Ohio. Existing licenses, branding, call letters, and locations will remain in place throughout the closing period. Once the transaction is complete, it is anticipated that the combined organization will operate under the Ideastream Public Media name.

Additional information about the merger, including FAQs, can be found on the websites for www.ideastream.org/merger and www.pbswesternreserve.org/merger.

About PBS Western Reserve

PBS Western Reserve is a community organization that empowers Northeast Ohio and Western Pennsylvania through the impact of accessible public media and educational services to foster connection and lifelong learning. PBS Western Reserve presents cultural, scientific and artistic programming for awareness and enjoyment; local storytelling and access to trusted regional, state and national public affairs; experiential opportunities and community outreach for people of all ages; and educational initiatives that support the healthy development of youth. 

PBS Western Reserve is made up of two separately licensed public television stations (WNEO and WEAO) and an Educational Services division operating under one 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation, Northeastern Educational Television of Ohio Inc. (NETO). WNEO was established in 1971, is licensed to the city of Alliance and serves the Youngstown designated television market. WEAO went on the air in 1975, is licensed to the city of Akron and serves the Cleveland-Akron-Canton designated television market. All programming is simulcast on both stations.

About Ideastream Public Media

Ideastream Public Media serves as Ohio's largest independent, publicly supported media organization. Ideastream is the home of Northeast Ohio's PBS, NPR, and classical and jazz music public broadcasting stations: WVIZ, WKSU, WCLV and JazzNEO. Free programs and services are made available to 3.6 million people in 22 counties across radio, TV, and digital platforms, meeting the communities we serve where and when they need us.

releases.title: Dunamis Woman™ Enterprise Expands Into Original Media With Launch of Dunamis Woman™ TV Network
releases.body:
Inc. 5000-ranked faith-based enterprise unveils new television and podcast slate led by original docuseries, "House of Healing." Private Atlanta upfront and premiere screening set for Thursday, October 8.

ATLANTA, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dunamis Woman™ Enterprise has announced they are expanding their transformational work into television and digital media with the launch of the Dunamis Woman™ TV Network, a new streaming platform featuring original programming centered on healing, faith, identity, relationships, leadership and personal transformation. The initial slate will include the flagship docuseries, House of Healing, the Dunamis Woman Today TV show and original podcasts from Dunamis Woman™ Visionary Founder, Dr. Davetta "Dunamis Dee" Mallory, and her daughter COO and Visionary Builder, Ariel "Professor Ari" Fuller.

The expansion marks the next chapter for the mother-daughter-led enterprise, whose story began with Dr. Dee and Professor Ari doing the deeply personal work to heal their own relationship before helping other women do the same. What began as a calling has since grown into a multimillion-dollar faith-based enterprise serving more than 125,000 women globally and, most recently, earning the company the No. 3,465 spot on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list following 82% three-year revenue growth.

"When Dunamis Woman began, healing was personal. My daughter and I had to confront things in our own relationship before we could authentically help other women confront what was broken in theirs," said Dr. Dunamis Dee. "Since then, we have had the privilege of watching women do the courageous work of healing, reclaiming their identity and changing the trajectory of their families. I am incredibly proud of how far this vision has come, and I believe we are ready for this next chapter. Dunamis Woman TV gives us an opportunity to open the doors and let the world see what real healing looks like, and what becomes possible on the other side of it."

"We reached a point where we knew the transformation happening within Dunamis Woman could no longer be limited by how many people we could bring into a room," added Ariel. "My mother is the Visionary Leader, and I am the Visionary Builder, so my responsibility was to determine how we could translate what she created into media without losing the integrity of what makes it powerful. That required us to think beyond simply filming content and intentionally develop programming that could carry these stories, conversations and experiences to a much larger audience. Dunamis Woman TV is the result of that planning, and the beginning of how we take this impact to the world." 

To extend that impact, the Dunamis Woman™ TV Network will serve as the centralized home for the organization's original television, transformational storytelling and podcasts, bringing its growing body of programming together across digital and streaming platforms. The network's slate includes:

Dunamis Woman Today — Premieres Wednesday, October 5: A transformational, story-driven series highlighting real women and men from the Dunamis Woman™ community and their journeys through healing, faith, relationships and personal transformation. Hosted by Professor Ari, the series pairs personal storytelling with insight from Dr. Dee, who helps viewers understand the lessons behind each journey and apply them to their own lives.

House of Healing — Premieres Thursday, October 10: The network's flagship unscripted transformational docu-series follows real women, not actors, as they enter an immersive healing retreat to confront the wounds, mindsets, relationships and life experiences that have kept them bound. Led by Dr. Dunamis Dee, each retreat takes viewers inside the raw conversations, challenging exercises, therapeutic coaching and deeply personal breakthroughs that unfold as women uncover what lies beneath the problems they thought they came to solve, revealing that sometimes, the problem you walk in talking about isn't the real problem at all.

The Professor Ari Podcast — Premieres Sunday, October 11: A thought-leadership podcast for ambitious women building what they believe God has called them to carry. Through conversations about identity, leadership, faith, endurance, income and impact, Fuller draws from her experience as a young executive and entrepreneur to explore what it takes to build with both purpose and capacity.

The Dr. Dunamis Dee Podcast — Premieres Sunday, October 11: Filmed from the stylish setting of Dr. Dee's' Dunamis Woman Boutique, the podcast introduces audiences to another side of the Visionary Founder through candid conversations about confidence, relationships, self-esteem, wisdom and the freedom to become unapologetically who they were created to be.

Dunamis Woman™ will formally introduce its new media chapter to the entertainment industry on Thursday, October 8, 2026, with the Dunamis Woman™ TV Network Upfront & Premiere in Atlanta. The invitation-only event will bring together entertainment executives, producers, media, creators, influencers, cultural tastemakers and business leaders for an exclusive "first look" at the network's inaugural programming slate. Guests will experience programming previews and trailers, a premiere screening of House of Healing, and a moderated conversation with Dr. Dee, Professor Ari and select participants from the series, followed by an industry networking reception.

Dunamis Woman™ TV Network programming is available for streaming on Roku, Amazon and Android TV as well as through the Dunamis Woman TV Network App on iPhone and Android. To subscribe, visit https://www.dunamiswomantv.com/checkout/subscribe/signup.

For press inquiries, or to schedule interviews with Dr. Dee and Professor Ari, contact dunamis@cnbettermedia.com.

Media interested in attending and covering the Dunamis Woman™ TV Network Upfront & Premiere may apply for credentials here: https://bit.ly/DunamisUpfrontCredentials 

ABOUT DUNAMIS WOMAN™

Dunamis Woman™ is a global transformational movement committed to helping women heal emotionally, grow spiritually and walk boldly in their God-given authority. Rooted in the Greek word "dunamis," meaning miraculous power, the organization equips women to restore identity, strengthen faith, build legacy and live whole from the inside out through transformational teaching, leadership development, educational resources, community experiences and live events. With a growing international community of more than 125,000 women, Dunamis Woman™ continues to inspire a generation of women determined to move beyond survival and into purposeful, legacy-driven living. For more information, visit www.dunamis-woman.com and follow @DunamisWoman on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X.

releases.title: Toronto Sauna Festival Transforms Evergreen Brick Works into a Three-Day Celebration of Sauna, Cold, Music and Movement
releases.body:
Following a sold-out debut, Toronto's sauna culture gets a major expansion with 20+ saunas, international sauna masters, immersive rituals, bigger music acts and triple the amount of wellness programming

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- Sauna culture has exploded beyond the traditional spa--and Toronto is getting a three-day festival built around it.

Produced by Unbounded, this year's festival will transform Evergreen Brick Works into a sprawling wellness playground, occupying more than three times the footprint of its debut, bringing together hundreds of sauna rituals, world-class Aufguss masters and practitioners from across Canada and Europe, alongside movement classes, cold plunges, live music, DJs, breathwork, sound experiences, recovery treatments, food and more.

The result is less a traditional wellness event and more a three-day social and cultural experience built around the rituals of heat and cold.

"Last year showed us that people are looking for something much bigger than simply going to a sauna," says Nick McNaught, founder of Unbounded. "We saw 1,500 people come together to sweat, plunge, move, listen to music and connect with each other. That response gave us the confidence to completely rethink what this event could become. This year, we've tripled the space, expanded to three days and brought together sauna traditions and talent from around the world, while creating a place where people can spend hours exploring, whether they step into a sauna or not."

Sauna Culture from around the world meets Festival Culture 

At the center of the festival will be a constantly changing program of guided rituals and free-flow experiences within the sauna village. 

International sauna masters and practitioners from Germany, Poland, Romania and Estonia will join Canadian talent to showcase the breadth of global sauna culture--from highly performative Aufguss ceremonies and herbal infusions to body scrubs and traditional Banya-inspired rituals.

Cold immersion will run throughout the festival, with both guided and free-flow plunges giving guests the opportunity to move between heat and cold at their own pace.

But the festival is designed to be about more than what happens inside a sauna.

Guests can move through an expanded wellness landscape featuring yoga and Pilates, breathwork and sound baths, meditation, recovery and longevity experiences, skin and herbal treatments, live music and DJs, as well as food, tea and non-alcoholic beverages. Interactive installations and unexpected activations will be woven throughout the Evergreen Brick Works site. 

KC Roberts, Meagan Delima [performed for Barack Obama], The Coffee Party and more will take over different elements of the festival's entertainment programming. 

A New Immersive Opening Night: October 2

Toronto Sauna Festival will kick off its 2026 edition with A Journey Through the Elements, a signature opening-night celebration on October 2 that invites guests into an immersive world, culminating into a one-night only artistic centrepiece.

Guests will begin their journey into the festival by cycling through four elemental zones: Earth, Air, Water and Fire. At the heart of the evening is a large-scale performance inspired by these elements, transforming the main space into a theatre for one-night only. Each element will be interpreted through a different wellness and artistic practice, from Aufguss to Cymatics, fire breathing to live music, this night marks the beginning of a weekend designed to blur the lines between wellness, nightlife and culture.

A Festival You Can Make Your Own

Rather than following a traditional festival schedule, Toronto Sauna Festival is designed around choice and discovery.

Saturday and Sunday programming will include a variety of sessions, each with their own atmosphere and lineup. Guests can move between saunas, cold plunges, guided rituals, movement classes, recovery spaces, music, food and other activities at their own pace.

The festival reflects the growing evolution of sauna and cold culture: practices that were once primarily associated with health and recovery are increasingly becoming social spaces--places to gather, meet people, listen to music, move, relax and experience something together.

Toronto Sauna Festival 2026

October 2–4, 2026

Evergreen Brick Works

Toronto, Ontario

In partnership with Therme Group.

Tickets and festival information are available at torontosaunafestival.com.

About Unbounded

Unbounded creates social wellness experiences built around sauna, cold immersion and community. Through these experiences, Unbounded is helping introduce a new generation to sauna culture in Toronto.

Leveraged ETFs are notoriously inefficient and cannot be held for long. Banks that supply leverage are constrained by hedging costs, and these charges are passed on to holders — compounding against performance year after year. Which is why leverage has been limited to short-term use. 2factor structurally eliminates this cost onchain, making leverage viable for the dominant capital base in finance: the $112 trillion population of buy-and-hold investors.

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 2factor.finance announced today its launch on Base for Coinbase's tokenized stocks, giving long-term investors moderate leverage they can hold indefinitely, at a fraction of what a leveraged ETF costs to carry. It is a rare case of an onchain product beating its traditional counterpart on performance rather than on access.

Tokenized equities may turn out to be an even larger development than people think. When Coinbase listed real equities onchain, the assets were the smaller half of the announcement. The larger half was opening them: any developer can now compose a listed stock with any other asset or protocol built onchain. What that unlocks is still mostly unknown. 2factor is an early answer, and not one anybody was forecasting. If structured products can be built better onchain than off, the question is how much else can be.

LEVERAGED ETFS CANNOT BE HELD, LIMITING THEM TO SHORT-TERM USE

Beta slippage, or beta decay, is the gap between the multiple on the label and what a holder actually earns. Hold a 3x fund for a year and you do not get 3x. Hold it for several and you often do worse than the stock itself.

This decay decomposes into two costs that compound against holders. Volatility drag is mathematical — the gap between arithmetic and compound returns — and cannot be engineered away. Financing drag is a charge: leveraged ETFs buy their exposure from banks that must hedge it, and the price of that hedging is passed through to the holder. Across the roughly $250 billion held in leveraged ETFs, investors pay an estimated $10 billion annually in financing above the risk-free rate.

Only about a third of single-stock leveraged ETFs have beaten simply holding the stock. No crypto leveraged ETF has ever beaten spot over its own lifetime.

2FACTOR CUTS THE COST OF LEVERAGE BY 75 PERCENT

The obstacle has always been structural. Leverage has to come from somewhere. Traditionally it comes from an intermediary who takes the other side and hedges it, and whose price reflects what short exposure costs to carry. Shorts are expensive. So the cost of being long has always been set by the cost of being short.

How expensive depends on how deep the hedging market is, not on how risky the asset is. In the big equity indices, where dealers hedge cheaply, leverage runs 4 to 5 percent a year. On a single stock it runs 8 to 86 percent. Competition does not compress it, because the price is set by the dealer's hedging cost rather than the issuer's margin.

2factor breaks that link. It sources leverage from investors seeking stable yield rather than from investors willing to be short. Stable yield is far cheaper than short exposure, and the savings are passed to holders — roughly a 75 percent reduction in the all-in cost of holding a leveraged single-stock position.

AND GROWS ITS ADDRESSABLE MARKET BY 750 PERCENT

A 3x position destroys capital over long horizons regardless of what it costs, because volatility drag scales with the square of leverage. So 2factor sets leverage targets that compound in favor of long-term holders — Kelly-optimal multiples that account for drag, roughly 1.33x for cbBTC, rather than the 2x and 3x the industry applies to every asset alike.

The difference shows up on the hardest asset there is. Over the past decade, one dollar in 3x Bitcoin went to zero. One dollar at 1.33x grew to approximately $506, against $281 for spot. Equities are far less volatile, which makes the range where leverage helps wider for a listed stock, not narrower.

The idea is not new. More than half a century of portfolio theory holds that moderate leverage maximizes growth for long-duration capital — at current equity volatilities, somewhere between 1.5x and 2x. Traditional finance has never disagreed. It has never been able to build the instrument.

Cheap financing and correct sizing together produce leverage that can be held like a spot position. Approximately 88 percent of investable capital — roughly $112 trillion — buys and holds; only about $15 trillion trades on shorter horizons. Leverage priced and sized for traders serves the smaller number. Leverage built to be held serves both — a 750 percent increase in the capital that can use it.

"I want to own moderately leveraged Google for exactly the same reason I want to own moderately leveraged Bitcoin. I don't know what path it will take, but I think the position will simply be worth more in five years," said Evan Kuo, co-founder of 2factor. "That is not an exotic wish. It is the most ordinary thing an investor can want, and until now there was no way to act on it that survived a bad quarter."

ON-CHAIN SOLUTIONS NOW OUTPERFORM THEIR TRADITIONAL ALTERNATIVES

This is not a workaround for investors who cannot reach traditional markets. Onchain products have generally won where access was the binding constraint; this one does not need that. It is a better instrument than the traditional alternative, for an investor with full access to both — and against a single-stock leveraged ETF held for years, the margin is not close.

Every structure traditional finance cannot assemble — programmable collateral, counterparties who never meet, terms that adjust without an administrator — is now buildable on a listed stock. And now there is proof they can be built better.

"Listing the assets was the first step, but opening them was the more important one," said Brian Armstrong, co-founder and CEO of Coinbase. "Putting a stock onchain is only interesting if it lets people do something they could not do before — otherwise we have rebuilt the same brokerage with extra steps. 2factor clears that bar, and it is exactly the kind of thing we opened these assets up for."

releases.title: United Teams Up with DISH to Broadcast Professional and College Football Games Live on Starlink-Enabled Seatback Screens
releases.body:
United flyers won't miss a play this football season, with live broadcasts from ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX, FS1, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network and TNF on Prime Video on Starlink-enabled seatback screens starting this week through the big game in February

Starlink is the fastest, most reliable WiFi in the sky and live TV streaming on seatback screens is now on board more than 220 mainline aircraft for customers in every class of service – up to 700 flights per day – with plans to reach 700 mainline planes early next year

United sponsors nine NFL teams and expects to operate 200+ team charter flights this season for 11 teams.

CHICAGO, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- United Airlines customers won't miss a play this football season, thanks to a new agreement between the airline and DISH. Starting this week, travelers can catch live professional and college football games right on their Starlink-enabled seatback screen.

Starlink is the fastest, most reliable Wi-Fi in the sky and United is installing Starlink at a rapid rate - and, fans can now watch live broadcasts from ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX, FS1, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network and TNF on Prime Video on more than 200 Starlink-equipped airplanes – about 700 of flights per day. The service will be available on domestic flights through the big game in February, and United expects to have Starlink on nearly 700 airplanes by then.

Starlink is free for MileagePlus members in every class of service, and the airline expects to complete installations before the end of 2027.

This new entertainment offering builds on the airline's long history of supporting professional football, sponsoring nine professional football teams in New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Houston, Washington D.C., Denver, Kansas City, Cleveland and Nashville and operating more than 200 team charter flights for 11 teams this season.

"Starlink opens a whole new world of features and benefits for our customers, regardless of where they sit on the plane – now football fans don't have to schedule their flights around game day," said Andrew Nocella, United's Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer. "Instead, they can watch their favorite team on seatback and also make changes to their fantasy roster, text or live chat with friends, or even stream different games on their phone, laptop or tablet, just like they would do at home."

United's new agreement represents a collaborative effort with DISH, utilizing its OnStream platform, to deliver content to next-generation aviation environments.

"With United, we are helping to rewrite the inflight playbook," said Amir Ahmed, Executive Vice President, Video Services, DISH. "Whether you're sitting on your couch or cruising at 35,000 feet, you should be able to watch your favorite teams play. By pairing DISH's OnStream platform with United's Starlink connectivity, we're keeping fans connected to the moments that matter most."

Starlink Sets a New Standard for Live Entertainment in Flight

This new service is just the latest example of how United is using Starlink to redefine the inflight entertainment experience. Last month, United partnered with ESPN to host a first-of-its kind live Fantasy Football Draft from 30,000 feet where ESPN analyst Tyler Fulghum made his picks live from the sky during the two-hour broadcast. And earlier this summer, United customers could stream the biggest soccer tournament in the world onboard Starlink-powered domestic flights.

Starlink is now active on more than 560 United mainline and United Express® aircraft and the airline has already flown more than 31 million passengers on Starlink-powered aircraft across more than 464,000 flights, powering 14.2 million devices.

Starlink is just one way United is investing nose to tail in its customer experience. The airline continues to install seatback screens across its fleet – up to 1,000 aircraft before the end of 2027 – and is rolling out new airplanes with 27-inch, 4K OLED seatback screens, the largest among U.S. carriers. Passengers can now access more than 2,500 hours of premium entertainment content including Apple TV, HBO Max, A24 and Spotify.

Football Flies United

Separately, for the second year in a row, United is celebrating the intersection of football, fashion and travel for its Football Flies United advertising campaign. Featuring New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh, Giants players Abdul Carter and Arvell Reese, and Chicago Bears players Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland, the campaign is built around a simple idea: how you arrive matters. Whether stepping off a plane for game day or arriving for an important business meeting, traveling well can help people feel refreshed, confident and ready to work – no matter what comes next.

"When our players step off the plane, we want them to feel rested, confident and ready to compete. Football Flies United celebrates the idea that when you travel well and feel your best, you're going to perform at your best," said Coach Harbaugh. "And for football fans traveling this season, they can bring that same game-day energy with them knowing they won't have to miss a play – they can watch their favorite teams live on United flights all season long."

The campaign is featured across prominent out-of-home locations in Chicago and New York, including Wrigleyville and Penn Station, with additional content rolling out across social media throughout the NFL season. The teams and locations were chosen to highlight United's roots as Chicago's hometown airline, and its global reach with Newark as a gateway to more than 90 international destinations.

The airline will also charter flights for the Washington Commanders, New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers for their international games in London, Paris and Mexico City.

About United

At United, Good Leads The Way. With U.S. hubs in Chicago, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, New York/Newark, San Francisco and Washington, D.C., United operates the most comprehensive global route network among North American carriers and is now the largest airline in the world as measured by available seat miles. For more about how to join the United team, please visit www.united.com/careers and more information about the company is at www.united.com. United Airlines Holdings, Inc., the parent company of United Airlines, Inc., is traded on the Nasdaq under the symbol "UAL".

NEW YORK, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As the Christmas season approaches, Great American Media is launching a new nationwide initiative celebrating the important role local churches play in caring for their communities and keeping faith at the heart of Christmas.

Know a small-town church making a difference this Christmas? Nominate here: https://GreatAmericanChristmasChurch.com.

Great American Christmas: Small-Town Churches invites Americans to nominate a small-town church they love and share how that church serves its community at Christmas and how additional support from Great American Media could help make an even greater difference.

Churches often meet some of the most immediate needs in their communities, providing food, coats, gifts, Bibles and support to families who need a helping hand. But their impact goes far beyond tangible needs. They offer a place for people to find faith, encouragement, belonging and hope, and to reconnect with the true meaning of Christmas.

"Churches are at the heart of so many communities, and that becomes especially meaningful at Christmas," said Kaitlyn Haubrich, Chief Brand Officer and Chief of Staff at Great American Media. "They're caring for families, supporting their neighbors and helping people stay connected to their faith and to what Christmas is about. Christmas As It's Meant To Be has always been about faith, family and taking care of the people around us."

Support will be shaped around the needs of each selected church and the community it serves. That could include helping with Christmas outreach, food or gift ministries, children's and family programs, worship or music programs, transportation, decorations or another need identified by the church.

Great American Media is asking church members, pastors, ministry leaders, neighbors and viewers to help identify churches that are taking care of those around them and making Christmas meaningful in their communities.

Know a church that deserves to be recognized this Christmas?

Nominate it.

Tell us its story.

Tell us how we can help.

Nominations will be accepted through October 15 at Great American Christmas: Small-Town Churches. Selected churches will be announced on October 27 and celebrated across Great American Media's social and digital platforms.

For families looking to continue celebrating the season together, Great American Pure Flix offers a collection of faith- and family-centered Christmas movies and stories throughout the holiday season. Explore Great American Pure Flix.

We can't wait to hear about your small-town church and how we can help make Christmas a little brighter this year. 

For nomination details, visit https://greatamericanchristmaschurch.com.

ABOUT GREAT AMERICAN MEDIA

Great American Media is the leader in faith and family entertainment, and one of the fastest-growing entertainment networks on television. Great American Media is home to a portfolio of entertainment  brands that celebrate faith, family, and country, including Great American Family, the flagship linear network featuring original Christmas movies, rom-coms, and beloved series; Great American Pure Flix, the leading faith and family streaming service; Great American Faith & Living, the unscripted companion network; and GFam+, an app that lets viewers watch anytime, anywhere. Great America Media, established in June 2021 by Bill Abbott and a group of US-based family offices, is available via cable, streaming on Pure Flix and YouTube TV, and on the GFam+ app.

releases.title: Regal Delivers Its Biggest Domestic Summer at the Box Office Since 2018
releases.body:
Revenues up 35.3% thanks to strong performance with the biggest movies of the summer

KNOXVILLE, Tenn., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Regal's gross domestic box office revenues grew more than 35% year-over-year this summer, marking the company's biggest summer in eight years.

Performance in the period (May 1-Sept. 7) was driven by outstanding delivery across all movies with particular strength on the biggest films of the summer, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey. The company took 18.2% of share on Spider-Man and 19.5% of The Odyssey, both well ahead of its 16.5% share of the market as a whole.

"A summer like this starts with filmmakers and studios making films that people really want to see on a big screen, and there have been a lot of them already this year," said Eduardo Acuña, Chief Executive Officer of Regal Global Entertainment. "The slate had real depth and range to it, and audiences kept coming back to share it with family and friends. I'm grateful to Regal's theatre teams who worked so hard to look after moviegoers, and to the staff in our offices who set the summer up so well. Our partners are putting money into films worth seeing, and we're putting money into the experience of watching them—moviegoers get the benefit of both."

The depth of the movie slate this summer played a key part in the success of the season. Alongside the summer's two biggest releases, Toy Story 5, Michael, The Mandalorian and Grogu, Obsession, The Devil Wears Prada 2, Backrooms, and Minions & Monsters each brought a different audience into theatres. The strength of the schedule was consistent from the first weekend in May through Labor Day rather than being concentrated in a handful of dates.

Premium large formats continue to contribute to ongoing growth through company investment in renovating theatres with expanded premium offerings including the recently opened Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria in Los Angeles. Regal's premium format box office rose 63% year over year and represented 22% of the circuit's summer revenue in the period, up from 18% a year ago, and contributing a third of the company's total increase. IMAX revenue at Regal more than doubled, RPX grew 80%, ScreenX grew 45%, and 4DX grew 13%. Premium formats made up more than 60% of Regal's gross on The Odyssey, a third on The Mandalorian and Grogu, and a quarter on Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Standard format revenue grew 29% over the same period, showing that the increase came from across the circuit rather than from premium alone.

About Regal Global Entertainment

Regal Global Entertainment operates the second-largest theatrical exhibition business in the world with 7,648 screens across 629 locations. Through its Cinema City, Cineworld, Picturehouse, Planet, and Regal brands, the company is committed to delivering exceptional moviegoing experiences through premium large formats, innovative loyalty and subscription programs, enhanced food and beverage offerings, and outstanding guest service.

Media Contact

Kevan Kerr

Senior Communications Manager

(865) 925-9539

Note to Editors

The 2026 summer season runs from Friday, May 1 to Labor Day, Monday, September 7. The 2025 summer season ran from Friday, May 2 to Labor Day, Monday, September 1.

releases.title: New Retirement in America Podcast: Rising Healthcare Costs Put Retirement Security Under Pressure
releases.body:
Segal Board Chair David Blumenstein Examines the Changing Benefits Landscape, the Enduring Value of Pensions and the Future of Retirement

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 5 of its Retirement in America podcast, "The New Reality of Retirement and Workplace Benefits."

The new episode features David Blumenstein, board chair and immediate past president and CEO of Segal, and podcast host Dan Doonan in a wide-ranging conversation about the forces reshaping employee benefits and retirement security. They examine rising healthcare costs, the shift of retirement responsibility to individuals, the continuing value of pensions, changing expectations for workplace benefits, and how technology and artificial intelligence could transform the field.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube, and all major podcast platforms.

"Healthcare and retirement benefits do not exist in separate silos," Doonan said. "When healthcare costs consume a larger share of compensation, there is less room for wages and retirement contributions. David brings decades of experience working with employers and plan sponsors, and this conversation helps explain why strengthening retirement security requires looking at the entire benefits landscape."

Blumenstein says the pace of change confronting employers and plan sponsors has accelerated significantly. On the retirement side, advances in computing have enabled more sophisticated risk modeling. On the healthcare side, employers are navigating rapidly evolving treatments, telehealth and other new approaches to care. At the same time, workers increasingly expect benefits information and tools to be as immediate and easy to use as other digital services.

The conversation also explores the broader shift toward placing more responsibility for saving for retirement on individual workers. Blumenstein says that while defined contribution plans are an important part of the retirement system, many workers cannot simply save more when their income is already consumed by basic necessities. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss the role defined benefit pensions can play by providing lifetime income workers can count on, as well as the need for personal savings to supplement retirement income.

Blumenstein also offers an optimistic view of technology and artificial intelligence. He expects new tools to make benefits analysis faster and more responsive while allowing employers and workers to model decisions more easily. But he emphasizes that critical thinking, problem solving and judgment will remain essential as the benefits field continues to evolve.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Rising healthcare costs and retirement security. Healthcare inflation puts pressure on employer compensation budgets, potentially leaving less available for wages and retirement benefits while workers and retirees face higher medical expenses.
  • The changing employee benefits landscape. Employers and plan sponsors are adapting to faster technological change, new healthcare treatments and rising expectations for easy, real-time access to benefits information.
  • The growing burden on individuals. Workers are increasingly responsible for saving for their own retirement, even as affordability pressures can make it difficult to maximize 401(k) or IRA contributions.
  • The enduring value of pensions. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss how defined benefit plans provide lifetime income and reduce some of the complex financial decisions and risks individuals otherwise must manage on their own.
  • Technology and AI. Blumenstein sees technology as a force that can improve modeling, communication and decision-making, while increasing the importance of critical thinking and problem solving.
  • A collective approach to retirement security. The episode closes with a discussion of the need for employers, policymakers and other stakeholders to work together on challenges that cannot be solved by individuals alone.

Retirement in America is a podcast from NIRS examining the economic, workforce and policy trends influencing retirement security. Combining expert insight with real-world experiences, the podcast helps listeners better understand one of the most important financial issues facing American workers and families today.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

releases.title: Notes.fm Raises $5 Million to Unify Royalties, Publishing, and Distribution for Independent Artists
releases.body:
New funding from leading artists and music industry executives—including Zach Bryan, Benny Blanco, Tainy, Ari Emanuel, Julie Greenwald, Sam Hendel, and others—supports the next phase of growth as Notes.fm builds a new financial layer for the music economy

Download Image Assets Here

NEW YORK, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Notes.fm, the music royalty collection platform helping musicians and music companies identify and collect 100% of their royalties, announces it has raised $5 million from leading artists, managers, executives and strategic partners across the music industry. Notes is the latest venture from Stem co-founder Tim Luckow, on a mission to support independent artists with the best-in-class technology for distribution and publishing under one roof so they can have full control over their earnings and stop missing out on money that is rightfully theirs.

The round includes participation from a range of influential artists and music industry leaders from Benny Blanco, Zach Bryan and his managers Stefan Max and Danny Kang, Tainy, Blake Slatkin, and Mt. Joy frontman Matt Quinn, WME Group Executive Chairman Ari Emanuel, Chord Music founder Sam Hendel, longtime Atlantic Records chief and 26.2 founder Julie Greenwald, as well as many of the industry's leading companies including Foundations, Mick Management, Twenty Ten Management, Triple 8, KMGMT, Good Boy, Mexican Summer, and Breakaway. The funding will support continued platform development and scaled marketing efforts as Notes expands its offering to artists globally.

Notes recently debuted a new feature "Releases" and unveiled its new partnership with Stripe, to streamline distribution, publishing admin and money management into one simplified release flow for musicians. This allows artists to use Notes.fm as the home for both distribution and royalty collection, making it easy for artists and their teams to take simultaneous ownership of their creative output and the income it generates. Notes is founded on the principle that every artist should receive all of their royalties. That's why they take 0% participation in distribution and publishing royalties, charging a flat monthly subscription fee instead. It's the same ethos behind their catalog royalty review technology, which helps rights owners identify missing royalties across their catalog and fix the issues so they can claim all of the royalties they've earned while they can.

This isn't new for Notes. Since launch, they've rolled out capabilities that allow artists and rights holders to more seamlessly manage their earnings, including integrated financial accounts designed to give users more flexibility in how they collect, store, and transfer, and earn on income. These updates are part of a broader effort to build a more complete financial layer for the modern music ecosystem.

Prior to Releases, Notes also announced  Credits.fm, a free and open music credits database indexing more than 150 million song codes and credits to help the music industry organize, verify, and connect the data powering royalties and artist compensation in the age of AI.

"Music is evolving quickly, and the finance systems around it need to evolve at a faster rate," said Tim Luckow, CEO and co-founder of Notes.fm. "Between all of the actions required to properly release, credit and collect on music, there are a lot of places where money falls through the cracks. We built Notes to bring all of that into one platform — so artists can release music and collect every royalty from day one, and recover what's historically been missed."

"Having spent our careers working with artists at every level, we've seen firsthand how much value gets lost to fragmented, unnecessarily complex systems," adds co-founder Derek Davies. "The response to Notes from the music community has been incredibly meaningful, and we're proud to announce a raise funded almost exclusively by artists, managers and music industry strategics who have a native understanding of these issues firsthand. This raise gives us the resources to keep building the infrastructure and applications that we believe the next generation of artists deserves."

Notes has created an artist-friendly, automated process to simplify a notoriously complex and outdated system that has historically led to hundreds of millions of dollars in royalties going unclaimed by artists every year. Notes brings clarity to the complexity, requiring only a musician name and list of songs to start reviewing streaming services, collection societies, and registries like the MLC and SoundExchange. The platform not only identifies missing royalties, but it also helps an artist fix issues and directly claim the royalties that result from those corrections while ensuring future income flows correctly.

Following its public launch last year, Notes has already demonstrated strong early traction, identifying more than $10 million in previously unclaimed royalties across a broad range of artists and catalogs including James Blake, Zach Bryan, Mt. Joy, Girl In Red and more. The platform continues to grow across both emerging and established artists, reflecting a shared demand for greater clarity and access in how music earnings are tracked and distributed.

By bringing together royalty discovery, payments infrastructure, and music-centric financial management into a single experience, Notes.fm is helping to create a new system that better supports artists as their careers and audiences grow.

About Notes.fm

Notes.fm is a music royalty collection platform built to help independent musicians, artists and music companies collect all of their royalties in one easy-to-use place. Founded by Stem co-founder Tim Luckow, Notes brings distribution, publishing, and financial tools under one roof, giving musicians and companies the technology to release music, verify song credits, manage their catalogs, and collect every royalty they're owed. Music Royalties, Simplified.

Learn more at www.notes.fm.

The Untold: Chelsey Northern (cn@wearetheuntold.com), Chloé Snyder (cs@wearetheuntold.com), Cory Councill (cc@wearetheuntold.com)
