releases.title: Sonilo Takes AI Music to the World Stage at the Venice Film Festival
releases.body:
The Silicon Valley company showcases its music and sound-effects models in a completed cinematic soundtrack, marking a milestone in its expansion into professional filmmaking.

SILICON VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sonilo, a U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI, brought its AI music and sound effects to the 2026 Venice International Film Festival. The company's technology contributed to the soundtrack of the PRIMORDIA trailer, which premiered during the opening program of an industry forum organized by TapNow at Venice Production Bridge. The presentation placed Sonilo's audio technology in front of an international film-industry audience through a finished cinematic work.

For Sonilo, the showcase represents a significant step into professional cinema. Its technology contributed to the musical identities, emotional progression and physical world of a production presented at Venice, demonstrating how AI-powered music and sound effects can move beyond standalone generation into the demands of cinematic storytelling.

The significance extends beyond visibility. A completed soundtrack gives filmmakers and production partners a tangible basis for evaluating the technology: how it works with the picture, supports the narrative and contributes to the experience audiences ultimately see and hear.

"Bringing Sonilo's AI-powered music to Venice is a milestone in our push into professional filmmaking," said Trista Hong, Chief Marketing Officer of Sonilo. "Cinema demands more than an impressive track or a realistic sound. It demands emotion, timing and a world the audience can believe in. We are building audio technology powerful enough to support ambitious productions and intelligent enough to serve the story."

Technology That Understands What the Story Needs

Sonilo is developing its Sound World Model, a multimodal AI system designed to connect video understanding, audio generation and temporal alignment. Rather than treating music and sound effects as isolated assets, the company is building technology that understands visual stories and generates audio in relation to the action, environment and narrative.

The production presented at Venice illustrated that approach across both music and sound effects.

For the score, Sonilo helped the production team explore contrasting instrumental textures within a character-driven musical framework. The finished soundtrack progressed from restrained elements beneath dialogue to deeper bass and additional layers as conflict approached. Rhythm and intensity increased with the action, culminating in a combination of synthesizers, orchestral elements and percussion. The result demonstrated how generated material can be developed into music with narrative structure, rather than simply placed beneath a sequence of images.

For sound effects, Sonilo analyzed scene content, movement, materials and narrative context before generating audio. Sound creators then reviewed and refined the results, corrected mismatches and added further creative direction. This scene-aware approach connects generation to a central requirement of filmmaking: sounds must belong to the world on screen, not merely sound convincing on their own.

"Film music is not everywhere in the film," said Shawn Song, CEO of Sonilo. "The model has to know when to start, when to stop, and when to leave room for the dialogue."

That is the technical ambition behind Sonilo's approach: audio generation that responds to what a scene means, not only what it contains.

Turning Generation Speed Into Creative Capability

The production also demonstrated how Sonilo's performance can expand creative exploration. According to the workflow presented at Venice, Sonilo reduced one initial music-exploration stage from approximately 10 hours to around 20 seconds. The comparison applies to that specific exploration stage, not to completion of the entire soundtrack.

The team used Sonilo to generate multiple musical and sound-effect directions, evaluate their emotional and narrative fit, and develop the strongest material through selection, combination, editing and professional post-production. This gave the project's composer and creative team a broader range of material to work with while preserving the decisions that shaped the final soundtrack.

For Sonilo, the opportunity is larger than making an existing task faster. The company aims to put more creative possibilities within reach: more musical directions to test, more sound palettes to explore and more opportunities to discover an approach that strengthens the film. Generation speed becomes valuable when it expands what a production can attempt and accomplish.

Building a Lasting Place for AI-Powered Music in Cinema

Sonilo's approach pairs technical ambition with respect for intellectual property and creative labor. "We respect knowledge, we respect IP, we respect effort. It should be common sense," Song said during the forum.

The company sees responsible development and professional collaboration as essential to building a lasting place in the film industry. Its goal is to advance audio technology that fits the realities of production, supports demanding creative work and develops alongside the filmmakers, composers and sound professionals who use it.

The Venice presentation offers a concrete example of that direction: Sonilo's generation capabilities working within a production process that combined composition, sound design and post-production to deliver a finished soundtrack.

For Sonilo, this is a foundation for a broader ambition: to make AI music and sound effects a meaningful part of professional filmmaking, with the capability to support increasingly ambitious stories. Its presence at Venice marks a step toward that future, demonstrated through the work itself.

About Sonilo

Sonilo is a Silicon Valley-based U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI for visual storytelling. The company is building the Sound World Model, designed to connect video understanding, music and sound-effects generation, and temporal alignment. Its technology supports filmmakers, creators and creative platforms across film, video, gaming and generative media.

About 10000 Parallel Universes

10000 Parallel Universes is TapNow's long-term international AI-native IP incubation initiative, designed to connect emerging creators with creative development, production support, international collaboration and distribution opportunities.

The initiative aims to explore how technology can amplify culturally diverse voices, expand access to filmmaking and help meaningful stories reach international audiences.

releases.title: 5 Creator Economy Trends That Will Change How Creators Make Money in 2027
releases.body:
RM11 identifies the rise of owned audiences, diversified monetization, paid traffic, AI automation and creator wellness as forces reshaping the creator business model.

DALLAS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The creator economy is growing up. Building a large following is no longer enough to build a sustainable creator business as creators increasingly seek greater control over their audiences, revenue, workload and long-term careers.

RM11, a creator-first platform built around direct audience relationships and multiple monetization tools, has identified five trends it believes will reshape how creators build businesses and generate revenue in 2027.

Recent industry research supports that shift. CreatorIQ's 2026 State of Creators study, based on 5,095 creators, found that 67% earned less than $10,000 from content creation over the prior year and that content creation was not the primary source of income for 62% of respondents. Meanwhile, Epidemic Sound's Future of the Creator Economy Report 2026 found that 72% of creators are actively developing owned audiences, while 41% want to build a sustainable independent business or grow into a media brand or creator studio.

"The next evolution of the creator economy isn't about producing more content or accumulating more followers," said Olivier David, Chief Growth Officer of RM11. "It's about giving creators the infrastructure to operate like businesses — own their audience relationships, diversify revenue, acquire customers and protect their most valuable resource: their time."

RM11 identifies five shifts that will define the next era of creator monetization:

1. Owned audiences will become more valuable than follower counts.

Creators are increasingly looking beyond algorithm-dependent reach toward direct relationships with their audiences. Memberships, private communities, messaging and direct-to-fan experiences can give creators greater control over how they engage and monetize their most loyal followers. Epidemic Sound's 2026 research found 72% of creators are already developing audiences away from core platforms through channels such as newsletters and Discord.

2. Creator platforms will evolve beyond the paywall.

The next generation of creator platforms will function more like business operating systems. Rather than relying on subscriptions alone, creators will increasingly combine memberships, pay-per-view content, livestreams, messaging, video calls and other revenue streams while using integrated tools to manage customer relationships, content and day-to-day operations.

3. Creators will start thinking about customer acquisition — not just followers.

As the industry matures, creators will increasingly apply traditional business metrics such as customer acquisition cost, conversion and return on advertising spend to audience growth. RM11 is developing promotion tools designed to make paid traffic and measurable customer acquisition more accessible to eligible creators, moving growth beyond the traditional "post and hope" model.

4. AI will shift from content generation to workload reduction.

AI adoption is becoming mainstream, but creator control remains critical. Adobe's 2026 Creators' Toolkit Report found that 93% of surveyed creators say creative AI helps them produce content faster, while 85% say the final creative decision should always remain with the creator. RM11 believes the next opportunity lies in using AI to reduce repetitive work and expand creator capacity without sacrificing authenticity, ownership or human oversight.

5. Creator wellness will become business infrastructure.

Creator-first economics cannot stop at revenue share. As creators operate increasingly complex businesses, platforms will be expected to help address the workload, stress and burnout that can accompany always-on digital careers. RM11 is investing in this area through integrated human account-management support and relationships with creator wellness and mental health organizations, including Creators for Mental Health, Revive Health Therapy and Pineapple Support.

"At RM11, 'creator-first' has to mean more than a revenue split," David added. "It means asking what creators actually need to build sustainable businesses — and then building the technology, services and partnerships around them."

RM11's growing ecosystem combines direct monetization, creator CRM capabilities, human account-management support, audience-growth initiatives and creator wellness resources as the company works toward a broader vision: giving creators the infrastructure to build businesses, not simply profiles.

For more information, visit RM11.com.

For media inquiries, please email media@rm11.com

About RM11

RM11 is a creator-first platform designed to give creators greater control over their audience, earnings and digital businesses. Through memberships, exclusive content, messaging, livestreaming, native video calls, integrated creator tools, account-management support, and a free CRM for agencies, RM11 provides multiple ways for creators to monetize direct relationships with their audiences. Female-founded and led, RM11 is building a more sustainable, creator-first model for the next generation of the creator economy.

releases.title: Clear Channel Outdoor Selected to Lead Advertising Program at Pensacola International Airport
releases.body:
New Concession Will Modernize Airport Media Network and Support Long-Term Growth Strategy

PENSACOLA, Fla., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, today announced it has been selected to manage the advertising concession at Pensacola International Airport (PNS). The agreement gives Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO) responsibility for delivering a refreshed airport media program that connects brands with more than 3.1 million annual passengers and strengthens the airport's position as a key commercial gateway for the Gulf Coast region.

Following a competitive selection process, PNS selected CCO to lead its advertising program, which has been managed in-house since 2018. Having previously served as the airport advertising concessionaire until 2012, CCO will return with a major investment in upgraded infrastructure and new sponsorship inventory. The program is designed to modernize the terminal environment, enhance revenue opportunities, and introduce more dynamic, technology-enabled advertising formats across high-traffic passenger areas.

"Pensacola International Airport is experiencing remarkable growth, and we're proud to partner with the airport at such a pivotal moment in its development," said Morten Gotterup, President, Clear Channel Outdoor Airports Division. "This agreement enables us to bring a new level of innovation to the airport environment, creating high-impact opportunities for brands to engage travelers through modern, technology-driven media while enhancing the overall experience for the millions of passengers who move through PNS each year."

PNS is the busiest airport along the Interstate 10 corridor between Jacksonville and New Orleans, serving a broad mix of business, leisure, and military travelers. The airport offers 28 nonstop destinations and is served by major carriers including American, Delta, United, Southwest, Breeze, Frontier, and Contour.

Modernizing the Passenger Environment

The new advertising program aligns with PNS's broader capital investment strategy, including a $165 million terminal expansion and new concourse scheduled for completion in the first half of 2028, which will add five gates to the existing 12-gate facility.

"Pensacola International Airport is in the midst of one of the most transformative periods in our history, and every investment we make should reflect the future we're building," said Matt Coughlin, Executive Director of Pensacola International Airport. "Clear Channel Outdoor shares that vision by bringing innovative, technology-driven advertising solutions that will elevate the passenger experience while creating meaningful opportunities for businesses to connect with millions of travelers each year. We're excited to partner with them as we continue shaping the next chapter for PNS."

CCO's Airports Division will introduce a modernized advertising program across key passenger touchpoints, including:

  • Branded LED video walls across entryways, security checkpoints, and baggage claim – Large-format digital displays placed at key passenger touchpoints, delivering high-impact brand storytelling throughout the airport journey.
  • Digital concourse advertising network – A connected network of screens throughout the concourse, reaching travelers as they move between gates, dining, and retail areas.
  • Reimagined branded environments – Immersive media opportunities that transform high-visibility terminal spaces into memorable brand experiences while reinforcing the airport's identity.
  • Corner tension fabric displays – Architecturally integrated, large-format displays designed to maximize visibility while complementing the terminal environment.
  • New charging station sponsorship opportunities – A premium sponsorship platform that aligns brands with a high-demand passenger amenity, creating sustained engagement throughout dwell times.

The partnership reinforces CCO's commitment to helping airports modernize passenger environments through innovative, technology-driven advertising solutions while supporting long-term growth and investment across the aviation network.

To learn more about Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division, visit https://clearchanneloutdoor.com/airport-advertising/.

About Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc.

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CCO) is at the forefront of driving innovation in the out-of-home advertising industry. Our dynamic advertising platform is broadening the pool of advertisers using its medium through the expansion of digital billboards and displays and the integration of data analytics and programmatic capabilities that deliver measurable campaigns that are simpler to buy. By leveraging the scale, reach and flexibility of our diverse portfolio of assets, we connect advertisers with millions of consumers every month.

releases.title: SiriusXM's SXM-11 Satellite Successfully Completes In-Orbit Testing and Enters Operational Service
releases.body:
Most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's fleet is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America

NEW YORK, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SiriusXM today announced that the Company's SXM-11 satellite is now operational, following successful in-orbit testing and handover by Intuitive Machines. SXM-11 is the most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's high-powered fleet and is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America.

"Bringing SXM-11 into service strengthens our next-generation satellite fleet and reinforces the long-term resilience of our network," said Sean Gibbons, Chief Product and Technology Officer at SiriusXM. "For listeners, that means a premium in-car experience with broad, reliable coverage, including where cellular service may be limited. Through SiriusXM with 360L, we combine that reach with the choice, personalization and interactivity of streaming, to bring the best of both technologies together in millions of vehicles."

210 million SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America are on the road today and rely on the proprietary satellite infrastructure supporting SiriusXM's in-vehicle listening experience. Built on the Intuitive Machines IM 1300™ satellite platform, SXM-11 weighed more than 15,000 pounds, or nearly 6,950 kilograms at launch. The satellite stands 28 feet tall and spans more than 106 feet with its solar panels deployed. Orbiting 22,000 miles above Earth, SXM-11 features a large, unfurlable 30-foot (9 meter) main beam antenna that broadcasts audio and data to users on the ground, with an estimated eight million square miles of broadcast coverage.

"SXM-11 marks another milestone in our longstanding partnership with SiriusXM. Over the course of our relationship, we have built 13 spacecraft together," said Chris Johnson, President, Intuitive Machines. "This handover reflects our shared commitment to mission success and the confidence SiriusXM continues to place in our team to deliver high-performance, reliable space systems. We continue to demonstrate our ability to design, build, and deliver satellite systems that meet the demanding requirements of today's commercial space market with robust, scalable high-power platforms."

SiriusXM also offers satellite-delivered Marine and Aviation services that provide pilots and boaters with weather data and other important information directly in their cockpits. SXM-11 carries an additional communications payload that will be used to deliver expanded WCS-band coverage.

SXM-11 launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 10:25 p.m. ET on June 28. SiriusXM and Intuitive Machines subsequently completed the commissioning and testing required to verify that the spacecraft and its communications systems were ready for operational service.

SXM-11 is the 15th satellite launched for SiriusXM and will replace XM-5. It is part of SiriusXM's ongoing satellite fleet-refresh program. SXM-9 and SXM-10 commenced service in 2025, and SXM-12 is currently scheduled for launch in 2027.

SXM-11 by the numbers

  • More than 15,000 pounds: SXM-11's launch weight, approximately the weight of a school bus.
  • Nearly 60%: The portion of the satellite's launch weight made up of fuel supporting its journey and in-orbit operations.
  • 28 feet: The height of the satellite.
  • 22,000 miles: The satellite's orbiting distance above Earth.
  • 8 million square miles: The satellite's approximate broadcast coverage footprint.
  • More than 106 feet: The satellite's span with its solar panels deployed - approximately the height of a 10-story building laid on its side.
  • 30 feet: The diameter of SXM-11's large, unfurlable S-band reflector (9 meters).
  • 210 million: The estimated number of SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America supported by SiriusXM's proprietary satellite network.
  • 15th satellite: SXM-11 is the 15th spacecraft launched for Sirius, XM and SiriusXM.

About Sirius XM Holdings Inc.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a complete ecosystem of advertising solutions through SiriusXM Media and AdsWizz. SiriusXM offers live, on-demand, and human-curated programming across music, talk, news, sports, and podcasts, and the company reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its platforms. With deep automotive manufacturer relationships and unique spectrum assets, SiriusXM is built to reach listeners wherever they are. The company connects fans to the voices, creators, and moments they love - creating communities where listeners engage, participate, and belong. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: https://www.siriusxm.com/

About Intuitive Machines

Intuitive Machines is a leading space infrastructure company that builds spacecraft, connects networks and operates infrastructure-as-a-service for commercial, civil and national-security customers. With a proven track record across the space domain, the company, through organic growth and portfolio expansion, has built more than 300 spacecraft, delivered more than 260 kilograms of payload to the lunar surface and provided precision-navigation expertise that has guided spacecraft across the solar system. These capabilities form an integrated Build-Connect-Operate infrastructure service company, enabling customers to achieve mission and campaign outcomes through a single prime solution. Intuitive Machines' technology has been demonstrated across the space domain and is engineered to support the next century of opportunity in space.

releases.body:
HANGZHOU, China, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On September 15, Adam Fan's new album SKYFALL makes exclusive debut on NetEase Cloud Music. Meticulously crafted by top international production teams and Grammy-nominated producers, SKYFALL features 10 tracks spanning melodic rap, rage rap, trap, rock-infused rage rap, and other styles. With every track refined to meet world-class production standards, the album showcases Fan's musical versatility and creative edge, marking a dramatic transformation in his global music career.

The album's title track, SKYFALL, has been released as an advance single on September 8 and reached No.1 on NetEase Cloud Music's Rising Chart (飙升榜), Popular Recommendations Chart (全民热推榜), and Heartbeat Chart (心动榜) that same day. To date, the song has received more than 300,000 comments from listeners. This song was produced jointly by Fan and Lawson, a leading American hitmaker who has produced for superstars such as The Weeknd and Playboi Carti. The song seamlessly blends ethereal, hazy, atmospheric melodies with deep self-examination. Through its lyrics and composition, Fan delves into his inner world—confronting the high-pressure pace behind his success, his inner struggles, and the loneliness at the very top. SKYFALL demonstrates Fan's evolution from a C-POP idol into an avant-garde, internationally oriented musician.

Fan has successfully crossed over from C-POP and acting, making a striking impression with SKYFALL, an internationally oriented urban rap album. The album boasts a stellar songwriting and production lineup: it was crafted entirely by leading hitmaking teams who have worked with global icons such as Drake, The Weeknd, Playboi Carti, Beyoncé, Yeat, and Trippie Redd. The album moves from late-night uncertainty, loneliness and intense introspection (SKYFALL and CHANCES) into the dark aesthetic of raw, industrial rage rap (TTTM, ERROR, and MAKE IT ROCK), ultimately arriving at a celebration party with cinematic trap and lush-flowing (GO GIRL, HEARD OF US, MAKE IT MAKE SENSE, and PINK).

NetEase Cloud Music has more than 200 million monthly active users, with over 90% of its active users born in the 1990s or 2000s. The platform's large community of young music fans is precisely the target audience for a new generation of singers, including Fan. In 2020, EMERGING, Fan's concept EP marking his 20th birthday, sold more than 250,000 copies within six minutes of its release on NetEase Cloud Music and surpassed 400,000 copies within 24 hours. In 2021, Yi? (咦？), his concept EP celebrating his 21st birthday, sold more than 150,000 copies within five minutes of its release on the platform, topping both NetEase Cloud Music's daily and weekly digital album sales charts. Its lead track, Born to Lose, reached No.1 on the platform's Rising Chart and New Songs Chart. The newly released SKYFALL surprises and delights music fans with its musicality, sincerity, and innovation. The album shows that Fan is continually pushing his own boundaries and gradually evolving into an all-around musician.

NetEase Cloud Music and Fan have collaborated on multiple EPs and albums, all of which have earned both widespread attention and positive word of mouth. As of this new release, Fan describes SKYFALL as the color of black, because the album represents his journey from late-night introspection to a fresh start. "I hope we all stay clear-headed and confident, and I'd like to thank NetEase Cloud Music for helping this album reach more listeners."

Wei Yuan, Vice President of Copyright at NetEase Cloud Music, said, "We are delighted to partner with Adam Fan once again. NetEase Cloud Music offers a wealth of high-quality rap music and brings together a large community of young rap fans. We hope the platform will help Adam Fan's new album build a more direct and deeper connection with music fans."

NetEase Cloud Music is the leading music community in China, where users can listen for free to hundreds of millions of music tracks and other audio titles. Since the start of 2026, NetEase Cloud Music has continued to significantly expand its licensed music catalog, adding a large collection of classic film and television soundtracks from TVB, as well as officially licensed music from the Chinese-style martial arts game JX3, and exclusively premiering new works by renowned artists such as Ren Jialun (Allen Ren) and Mariah Carey.

At the same time, NetEase Cloud Music has continued to deepen its commitment to HIP-POP, launching the Chinese HIP-POP Music Awards (中文说唱音乐奖), along with semiannual charts, monthly and weekly charts, to identify outstanding work from multiple perspectives and highlight trends in Chinese HIP-POP. The platform also provides systematic support for the development of HIP-POP in China through initiatives including BeatSoul, its one-stop beat marketplace, income support programs, and rap projects. Going forward, NetEase Cloud Music will partner with more musicians to continue bringing users high-quality, officially licensed music.

ST. LOUIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly 40 years after Illinois alternative rock trio Lucky Mary Blonde disbanded, the band's long-lost 1988 live recording is being released worldwide today on major streaming services as the album Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! — completing one of the most unlikely journeys in the history of the group's music.
releases.title: Two Forgotten Cassettes, One Musical Miracle: Lucky Mary Blonde Releases Lost 1988 Live Album Today
releases.body:
Nearly 40 years after the band disbanded, an extraordinary discovery, a second forgotten cassette and advances in AI-assisted audio technology brought one of the group's last performances back to life

ST. LOUIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly 40 years after Illinois alternative rock trio Lucky Mary Blonde disbanded, the band's long-lost 1988 live recording is being released worldwide today on major streaming services as the album Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! — completing one of the most unlikely journeys in the history of the group's music.

Lucky Mary Blonde emerged from the fertile Midwest alternative and college rock scene of the late 1980s. The trio's album Let the Moonlight Burn was released in December 1987 and climbed Midwest college radio charts the following year. The band performed at venues from Chicago to Memphis and opened for national acts before unexpectedly breaking up in late 1988.

The recordings that would eventually become the new live album began as private cassette tapes made directly from the sound board and stage microphones during one of the band's final performances in Carbondale, Illinois in 1988. They were never released publicly, never intended to become an album and, after the show, were immediately forgotten.

Nearly four decades later, one cassette was discovered by a friend of the band and ultimately sent to drummer John Baldus, based in St. Louis, Missouri. Baldus began experimenting with modern AI-assisted audio technology to clean up the recordings. AI technology made it possible to break down the aging two-track recording into multiple, individual vocal and instrumental stems. Separating the stems was only the beginning, some instruments and vocals were still stubbornly intertwined, and Baldus spent months repairing and working through the recordings piece by piece.

Baldus eventually moved the restoration into professional recording studios with engineers in St. Louis and Richmond, Virginia. The project ultimately became a year-long effort.

As the first cassette was processed in St. Louis, however, a serious problem emerged. Elements of the performance were missing, including portions of the guitar, backing vocals and the audience microphones that originally captured the energy of the concert.

"It was frustrating," Baldus recalled. "We knew there was something special in the performance, but important pieces were simply gone. I remember lamenting to the guys how difficult the audio was to work with and wished there was somehow another better copy of the tape."

That prompted bassist Jerry Tilk, based in Virginia, to scour hundreds of old cassettes sitting in storage for decades. After a painstaking search, he hit the jackpot: another missing cassette from the same 1988 show.

Tilk immediately sent it to the Richmond studio to be digitized. What happened next bordered on miraculous. The Richmond engineer reported that the second cassette was in good condition, but it seemed to contain only backing vocals, audience microphones and portions of the guitar.

For the band, it was a jaw-dropping revelation. The missing elements from the first cassette were not missing at all, they had been recorded on the second cassette. The two recordings contained complementary channels from the same performance. By digitally combining them, the restoration team could reconstruct the complete recorded show.

"At that moment, we realized this coincidence and chain of events were far too great to ignore.  We were on a mission now to complete this project.  After four decades, it really was amazing to put lost pieces of a puzzle back together," said Baldus.

Tilk long remembered that some of Lucky Mary Blonde's best songwriting came after the release of its first album. "I regretted that our post-album writing was never recorded. When we found and heard the tapes, we realized those songs actually had been recorded, they were just lost. It simply became a matter of restoring the recording to original concert quality. This is one positive aspect of AI. We had an opportunity to resurrect these great songs."

The result is a 16-song live album featuring 11 previously unreleased songs alongside five songs originally recorded for Let the Moonlight Burn .

For guitarist and songwriter Todd Baxter, hearing the performances again was about more than recovering old recordings. Now based in Florida, Baxter commented, "I hadn't heard these songs in 40 years. They capture a period of life of youth, tremendous energy and zeal, and listening to how well we performed them live, I just want to go back and pat these young guys on the back and tell them 'well done boys.'" Baxter wrote all of the songs on the live album and remains a prolific songwriter today.

Sometimes a lost recording is found. Sometimes it is found twice. And nearly 40 years later, the technology finally exists to hear what was there all along.

The complete Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! album is being released worldwide today on Apple Music, Spotify, Amazon Music and other major digital music services.

www.luckymaryblonde.com

Website: www.luckymaryblonde.com

About Lucky Mary Blonde

Lucky Mary Blonde was an Illinois-based alternative rock trio that gained a loyal following throughout the Midwest college music circuit during the late 1980s. Following the release of Let the Moonlight Burn in 1987, the band toured extensively before disbanding in late 1988. The Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! album documents one of the group's final performances and preserves a chapter in independent college rock history.

releases.title: Storyteller Overland Announces STO Fest: Where Overlanding Meets Live Music
releases.body:
Four days of live music, vehicles, and desert adventure in the high desert of Johnson Valley, October 15–18, 2026.

BIRMINGHAM, Ala., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- There's a reason a campfire and a concert feel like the same instinct. Gather. Listen. Connect. Stay longer than you planned. Storyteller Overland has built an entire festival around that overlap.

STO Fest is a four-day gathering in Johnson Valley, California, built around overlanding, live music, and the outdoors. It grew out of the brand's community of vehicle owners, but the gate swings both ways — STO Fest welcomes anyone ready to say yes to their next grand adventure, whether they show up in a fully kitted rig or have never set foot off-pavement.

Overlanding and live music pull from the same crowd: people who go find it instead of waiting for it to come to them. STO Fest puts them in the same place, at the same time, for the first time.

Presented by Gibson Guitars and Mercedes-Benz, the festival features two bands each night on the Gibson Stage, Thursday through Saturday, with headline sets from Ozomatli, Blackberry Smoke, and The Struts, plus a special appearance from The Dusty Bunch, a musical collective made up of Storyteller Overland's own team members — including CEO, Neil Grimmer.

Thursday, October 15

Headliner Ozomatli brings three decades of Grammy-winning genre fusion blending Latin, hip-hop, funk, and reggae, rooted in Los Angeles. Opening the night is The Western States, a rising force in the LA country scene built for high-energy sets that span classic country, honky-tonk, and alt-country.

Friday, October 16

Southern rock mainstays Blackberry Smoke headline, fresh off their latest album Be Right Here and a #1 Billboard Americana/Folk chart debut. Blues-rock guitarist Jared James Nichols opens, pick-less playing style and all.

Saturday, October 17

Glam-rock powerhouse The Struts close out the weekend known for arena-sized hits like "Could Have Been Me" and "Body Talks." All-female Black Sabbath tribute act Black Sabbitch opens, fresh off their live album Unrest in the West.

"Our community has always known how to gather around a campfire, a trailhead, a hot meal after a long adventure," said Josh Ehren, Chief Marketing Officer of Storyteller Overland. "STO Fest just gives those connections a stage and a lineup. It's the same incredible people, the same reason we all got into this in the first place, we just added the live music."

Beyond the music, STO Fest runs full days of programming. Learning Labs give guests hands-on skills sessions all weekend. Vendor Village showcases gear, mods, and makers. Attendees can get behind the wheel with demo drives in Storyteller vehicles and LiveWire electric motorcycles, or meet the Mojave mini donkeys who call the high desert home. Food, water, showers, and restroom facilities are on-site all weekend. Campfires and conversations round out each night, the space where the community connections really happen.

STO Fest 2026 runs October 15–18 at Lasertown in Johnson Valley, California. Tickets and full event details are available at stofest.com.

About Storyteller:

Storyteller Overland is widely regarded as the world's most all-encompassing and highest quality overland vehicle manufacturer. Launched in 2018 by a dedicated group of automotive and outdoor enthusiasts, Storyteller has always believed that capability is only half the story — what matters most is how that capability lets its community live and experience life exactly the way they want to. That belief drives the mission: to inspire and equip a growing community of adventurers with the proper gear, resources, and mindset to "live free, explore endlessly and tell better stories." Storyteller is honored to serve its STORYTELLERS owners group, a diverse, kind, helpful, and inclusive gathering of rugged individualists drawn together by a shared belief that life's greatest luxury is saying "yes" to the next grand adventure. Based in Birmingham, Alabama, the Soul of Storyteller is the unique connection that exists between the stellar group of people who design, engineer, and build our vehicles and gear, and the incredible people who experience them.

releases.title: Amuze Acquires Sweet Attractions, Strengthening California Operations and Family Entertainment Capabilities
releases.body:
Acquisition brings together local customer relationships, regional service expertise and national equipment and merchandise resources

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Amuze, a national amusement equipment and route-services platform, today announced the acquisition of the operations of Sweet Attractions, a California-based amusement operator serving family entertainment centers, restaurants, bars and other entertainment venues. The transaction also brings affiliated Paramount Amusement Group operations into Amuze. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Sweet Attractions provides equipment installation, operation and ongoing service across arcade games, cranes, redemption attractions and photo booths. The business is growing throughout California and expanding into markets outside the state.

Amuze plans to build its coordinated California operations around a Fresno-based hub while maintaining local field-service coverage. Integration will prioritize customer and employee continuity, shared resources and support for Sweet Attractions' expansion.

Amuze's vertically integrated platform includes Pipeline Games, which designs and manufactures redemption, crane and merchandiser games, and Quality Plush, a supplier of licensed and generic plush merchandise. These businesses will provide Sweet Attractions with equipment, plush and merchandising support, helping venues deliver engaging entertainment experiences.

"Sweet Attractions has always been about taking care of our customers and finding the right entertainment mix for each location," said Mark Knepper, President of Sweet Attractions. "Joining Amuze gives us more equipment choices and deeper service support while preserving the relationships and personal attention our customers value."

"Sweet Attractions is a strong fit with our broader California growth plans," said Stephen Lahti, co-CEO, Finance + M&A. "Mark and his team bring valuable customer relationships, hands-on operating knowledge and a commitment to service. Bringing those strengths together with Amuze's equipment, sourcing and regional support capabilities will help us serve customers more effectively and grow with them."

Knepper will continue working with the business, supporting customer relationships, the team's transition and continued growth.

About Amuze

Amuze combines venue-based entertainment operations with equipment development, sourcing and distribution.

About Sweet Attractions

Sweet Attractions installs, operates and services amusement equipment for family entertainment centers, restaurants, bars and other venues.

releases.title: Hisense Unveils New C3 Projector Family for Immersive Home Entertainment
releases.body:
QINGDAO, China, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hisense, a leading brand in global consumer electronics and home appliances, is expanding its home entertainment portfolio with the new C3 projector family, designed to bring cinema-sized entertainment into everyday life. Showcased at IFA 2026, the C3 Ultra and C3 Ultra Max are launching across global markets this September, with the C3 Pro set to follow.

From movie nights and live sports to gaming with friends, the C3 family is designed around the moments people want to make bigger. With projection sizes of up to 300 inches, powerful brightness and immersive sound, it transforms living rooms, bedrooms and other spaces into flexible entertainment destinations, giving users more freedom to enjoy the big-screen experience at home.

The C3 Ultra delivers 4,000 ANSI lumens and a 5,000:1 contrast ratio with an IRIS Lens, combining vivid visuals with gaming-enhanced performance. Its Devialet-tuned audio system, featuring co-engineered hardware and a built-in subwoofer, delivers deep bass and immersive surround sound for a more engaging entertainment experience.

For users seeking greater visual power and responsiveness, the C3 Ultra Max delivers 5,000 ANSI lumens, 5,000:1 contrast with an IRIS Lens and 1ms ultra-low latency, supporting dynamic entertainment across movies, sports and gaming. Enhanced by Devialet audio, it completes the experience with rich, immersive sound that matches its high-performance visuals.

The C3 Pro brings the C3 experience to more users with 3,000 ANSI lumens, 5,000:1 contrast with an IRIS Lens and Devialet-tuned audio with a built-in subwoofer, offering a compelling balance of performance and value.

Together, the C3 Ultra, C3 Ultra Max and C3 Pro further enrich the C3 family, offering consumers a broader range of choices to suit different entertainment needs and spaces. Earlier this year, the C3 has undergone Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) verification by SGS, supporting transparent evaluation of environmental impact across the product lifecycle and reflecting Hisense's commitment to transparent product-level environmental assessment.

releases.body:
BEIJING, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Orange Lion Sports, founded by Alibaba Group, has unveiled Smartshot 2.0, the upgraded version of its AI sports solution, at the Sports Services exhibition during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), held September 9-13 in Beijing.

From six-camera Hawk-Eye electronic line calling and AI-powered auto-directing to the debut of a voice-interactive smart ball machine, the company is advancing a cost-effective approach to inclusive sports technology, bridging the gap between professional competition and mass participation to "make sports simple."

At CIFTIS 2026, Orange Lion Sports' replica tennis court became a focal point. Smartshot 2.0 introduced an upgraded electronic line calling system designed to address long-standing disputes over line calls at amateur tennis events. As soon as the ball lands, a large screen provides instant in/out calls and can announce "IN/OUT" at adjustable volumes. The system supports smoother, fairer amateur competitions at a low marginal cost without requiring additional labor.

AI commentary and auto-directing cut broadcasting costs of up to hundreds of thousands of yuan, making high-quality broadcasts more accessible. AI-powered robots are becoming a valuable complement to traditional sports coaching.

In Orange Lion Sports' roadmap, Smartshot will work with the smart ball machine to interact with trainees through natural language, instantly adjusting ball settings, placement and speed to create personalized training programs and help beginners improve more efficiently.

Leveraging Alibaba's technology capabilities, Smartshot has integrated the Tongyi Qwen large language model to launch what it describes as the industry's first "AI Tournament Assistant" in the first half of 2026. The assistant understands natural-language instructions and parses PDF regulations, enabling scheduling and registration to be completed in minutes. Smartshot now offers pricing at one-tenth that of comparable offerings.

"Our goal is to find the optimal balance between precision and cost control, consistent with our long-standing technical philosophy. We reject expensive professional premiums and pursue cost-effective, inclusive technology," said Peng Wei, CTO of Orange Lion Sports.

Since its launch, Smartshot has been deployed across more than 500 courts and expanded into overseas markets, with installations in Europe, Australia, Hong Kong SAR, and Taiwan region. Looking ahead, as AI advances in sports, Orange Lion Sports' approach to balancing commercial value with accessibility aims to make professional-grade smart equipment more affordable and accessible worldwide.

releases.title: Gold House Honors the 2026 Multicultural Emmy® Nominees at the One House Toast to the Emmys®
releases.body:
Red Carpet Photos (Credit: Andrew Ge)

Party Photos (Credit: Duke Winn)

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Gold House, the cultural platform shaping global opportunity, honored the multicultural nominees of the 78th Emmy® Awards at its annual One House Toast to the Emmys® on Thursday, September 10, at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills. The One House Toast is a celebration of multicultural excellence in television and media, convening over 200 creatives and artists, including Emmy-nominees from BEEF, Bridgerton, The Pitt, Abbott Elementary, and others, as well as industry leaders and creators. This year's event was made possible by presenting sponsor Chase Sapphire Reserve for BusinessSM, exclusive automotive partner Genesis Motor America, lead media partner Variety, Asian entertainment streamer Viki, and WME.

Netflix's BEEF had another historic awards season with 16 nominations, including nods for executive producer, writer, and director Lee Sung Jin, Charles Melton, and Youn Yuh-jung. Their nominations are joined by Sepideh Moafi (The Pitt), who became the first Iranian woman nominated for an Emmy, and members of The Pitt's cast, including Kristin Villanueva and Amielynn Abellera.

Notable guests included Lee Sung Jin, The Pitt's executive producer Simran Baidwan, Street Fighter director Kitao Sakurai, Creative Arts Emmy winner Sang Kim, Seoyeon Jang, Dante Basco, Dolly de Leon, Will Yun Lee, Leah Lewis, Monica Padman, Tal Anderson, Gurinder Chadha, Albert Cheng, Justin Chien, Hanelle M. Culpepper, Percy Daggs IV, Fiona Dourif, Edwin Lee Gibson, Chin Han, Ryan Alexander Holmes, Scott and Mark Hoying, Madison Hu, Gia Kim, Ken Kirby, Hiro Koda, Raymond Lee, Michelle Mao, Dana Ledoux Miller, Minnie Mills, Daniella Monet, Yoko Okumura, Monica Padman, Brandon Perea, Huma Qureshi, Salli Richardson-Whitfield, Saagar Shaikh, Joanna Sotomora, Regan To, Kristin Villanueva, Cole Walliser, Janet Yang, Hanbit Yi, Phinehas Yoon, and many others.

Throughout the evening, guests enjoyed a custom portrait studio presented by Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business, an exclusive photo experience featuring the all-new Genesis GV90 from Genesis Motor America, and a custom BEEF-themed food-and-beverage experience presented by WME. Variety returns as the Toast's lead media partner for the third year.

"Gold House has meant a lot to my journey and BEEF's journey. These events are fun, but it's also a place of true community. Having people here to support makes a difference; you never know who you'll run into or what conversation turns into what. I'm really grateful that we get to do this and do it together," said Lee.

"In a week when several whistleblowers are warning that new technologies can decimate our species by the end of the decade, it is hybridized, undefinable-by-a-single-genre art like BEEF that reminds us of what most makes us human, of our fallacies, and our right to exist. On platforms and spaces, when people try to flatten us into one thing, it is polymathical, multi-skilled creators who don't just write, who don't just produce, who don't just direct, but do it all to create historic pieces of art that remind us what it takes to get this far. And it is in our own lives that we're reminded that when things get toughest, we take our broken hearts and turn them into art. That reminds us why we are still here—and why we must stay." said Bing Chen, Executive Chairman and CEO of Gold House.

Jazz Tangcay, Senior Artisans Editor at Variety, ended the remarks by urging the crowd to "[p]lease keep telling your stories because… it means so much to see our faces on [television]."

The One House Toast continues Gold House's commitment to advancing Asian Pacific representation in entertainment. This year's celebration builds on the organization's Gold List for Film and Gold List for TV honoring Asian Pacific excellence, and its ongoing industry-leading consultation, investment, and marketing partnerships across film and television to ensure opening weekend success. Its platform now includes the recently launched Gold House Studios, which provides development and financing for Asian Pacific-led films, series, and IP. Through these initiatives, Gold House continues to empower and enable affirming and authentic portrayals of Asian Pacific and multicultural voices in front of and behind the camera.

For further inquiries, please contact goldhouse@havasformula.com.

Gold House is the cultural platform shaping global opportunity. We foster spaces where established and emerging makers gather to amplify their impact. We shape public perceptions by consulting on, investing in, and marketing society-defining media properties. We create new economies by backing the boldest entrepreneurs and scaling them internationally.

By fueling unity, visibility, and economic mobility, success becomes our shared world. With roots in Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Singapore, Gold House operates with the heart of a nonprofit and the reach of a world-class enterprise.

We don't just change culture—we make it.

releases.body:
APJ raises over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /CNW/ -- Board Chair Natasha Koifman and powerhouse board members George Stroumboulopoulos, Kardinal Offishall, Amanda Brugel and more, hosted the 18th annual Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) Gala this evening at the Windsor Arms Hotel, the landmark venue that hosted the organization's first Toronto gala. Recognized as one of the city's most anticipated philanthropic events, the gala raised over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti.

Since its founding, APJ has raised over $37 million and supported more than 32,000 students through access to quality education, healthcare, and opportunity.

The evening honoured three remarkable women whose careers and philanthropy embody the spirit of Artists for Peace and Justice: Andrea Martin, Emily Hampshire and Jann Arden.

Natasha Koifman, Chair of the Board, opened the evening with remarks on APJ's evolving mission, from rebuilding after the 2010 earthquake to using education as a lifeline for children caught in Haiti's escalating gang crisis today. "Believing in a better future is no longer enough. We have to be the lifeline that helps pull these children out of danger. The situation in Haiti has changed dramatically since APJ was founded, and while we haven't been able to return to the country because of the ongoing crisis, our commitment to the children we serve has never wavered. Today, education is not just about preparing young Haitians to rebuild their country in the future - it is a lifeline in the present, giving children a safe place to learn, hope, and build a path beyond the violence. The humanitarian crisis and the daily struggle to survive are unimaginable, and that makes our work more urgent than ever."

Evening Highlights

  • Setting the tone for the night, a buzzy red carpet welcomed a special group of guests: adoptable puppies from Project Paws, who posed for photos with talent and guests to help spotlight pets in need of a home.
  • APJ Board Members George Stroumboulopoulos and Kardinal Offishall returned as emcees for the evening, welcoming guests and expressing gratitude for the continued generosity that fuels APJ's mission.
  • Rick Mercer, a past APJ Award recipient, presented Emily Hampshire with the Canadian Artists for Peace and Justice Changemaker Award, celebrating her work using her platform to raise awareness around mental health and queer experiences. Hampshire's Schitt's Creek co-star Noah Reid took the stage after to perform a special song in her honour.
  • Amanda Brugel, last year's Changemaker Award recipient and a new APJ board member, presented Jann Arden with the Artists for Peace and Justice Impact Award, in recognition of her decades-long commitment to philanthropy, humanitarian causes and giving back to communities in need.
  • George Stroumboulopoulos presented Andrea Martin with the Global Artists for Peace and Justice Award, honouring her longstanding commitment to humanitarian causes and her dedication to creating positive change. Martin surprised the room with an impromptu rap after accepting the honour.
  • Norman Gaudet, former head of the Toronto French School, took the stage to announce an extraordinary milestone: inspired by Wes Hall, he created a full international scholarship after discovering APJ's mission last year. He proudly shared that Schnaider, the Academy's scholarship recipient, has officially arrived in Canada and is settling in with his host family, a testament to the importance of giving these children new opportunities outside of Haiti.
  • The live auction, led by The Auctionista, was one of the night's most electric moments, as guests bid fast and furiously on an extraordinary collection of art. Celebrated artists Russell Young, Tyler Shields and Mr. Brainwash, courtesy of Taglialatella Gallery, along with Anthony Ricciardi, saw their work draw serious heat in the room. Young, in attendance for the evening, unveiled a truly one-of-a-kind charitable commission: a family portrait shot by CAFA winner Renata Kaveh and rendered in his signature diamond dust technique, destined to become a cherished heirloom for its new owner.
  • The energy hit a fever pitch over a rare Birkin, courtesy of Carly Jordan, sparking a spirited bidding war between guests determined not to leave empty-handed. Also up for grabs: travel packages from Air Canada, a culinary evening at Michelin-starred Enigma Yorkville, and two once-in-a-lifetime experiences, the Bautista Impact Summit in the Bahamas and a getaway to Hightail Ranch in Montana.
  • Mandy Rennehan and Lauren Ferraro led a lively final Fund the Need moment, courtesy of Dean Davidson, with guests raising their hands to purchase 20 special bracelets to support some of the highest-need areas of APJ's Academy for Peace and Justice.
  • Haitian music icon and long-time APJ supporter Paul Beaubrun closed the night with an emotional performance.

Generous sponsors for this year's event include: Air Canada, 2Fifteen by DBS Developments, Audi, and Forest Hill Group.

Download Images here –  Credit Shutterstock Images (Photographers: Tyler Da Silva/ and Ernesto DiStefano)

ABOUT ARTISTS FOR PEACE AND JUSTICE

Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) is a non-profit organization that encourages peace and social justice and addresses issues of poverty around the world. APJ's immediate goal is to serve the poorest communities in Haiti with programs in education, healthcare, and dignity through the arts. The organization is committed to long-term, sustainable development in direct partnership with the Haitian people. APJ partners with St. Luke's Foundation in Haiti. To learn more, visit www.apjnow.org or follow @artistsforpeace on Instagram and Twitter.

ABOUT NKPR

NKPR was started in 2002 by Natasha Koifman to combine two passions: shining a spotlight on stories of substance and supporting causes that are making a difference around the world. Over the past 24 years, NKPR has established itself as a highly regarded full-service public relations, artist management and digital agency with offices in Toronto, New York and Los Angeles, representing over 40 national and international brands and supporting charitable organizations like Artists for Peace and Justice. For more information, visit NKPR on social media @natashankpr or at www.nkpr.net.

Debuting during the 2026 football season on a streaming service, the new campaign marks 120 years of Coldwell Banker affiliated agents handing families the keys to the places where their lives unfold.

MADISON, N.J., September 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coldwell Banker Real Estate LLC today announced The Letter, a new national advertising campaign premiering on select Thursday evenings this fall during football season on a streaming service. The campaign follows one family across three generations in the same home, celebrating the central role the home played in a family's life in a letter drafted to wish the new owner well. 

As the Coldwell Banker® brand celebrates its 120th anniversary this year, the campaign honors all of the little moments that add up to make a house into a home: the dinner parties, holiday celebrations, graduations, visitors, and new additions. The 60-second spot tells one family's story across more than 30 years, while a series of original 15-second spots highlight individual moments in the family's life – and the home that served as the setting. It's a vantage point Coldwell Banker has held since 1906, across generations of families and the agents who walked them through the door.

"The Letter isn't about the value of a house in dollars, cents or square footage. It's about the value of life that happens inside," said Brandon Newman, Vice President of Marketing, Coldwell Banker Real Estate LLC. "Homes are an ecosystem for your life, so we built our campaign the same way. There is no single hero spot with cut downs. Instead, there's a whole life that takes place in this world we have created, which celebrates the real lives people live in their homes every day." 

Capturing three decades of one family in the same home shaped every production choice, from casting to cameras. The Coldwell Banker team cast the family at multiple ages, spent up to six hours a day on makeup to age or de-age actors, and evolved wardrobe and production design through the decades. Three cameras marked the passage of time, including a 16mm film camera for the earliest era.

"Much of the conversation around real estate today is about technology, listings, transactions and market conditions, but buying or selling a home has always been about more than that," said Mary Lee Blaylock, President of Coldwell Banker Affiliates. "Homes are incredibly emotional, and after 120 years in the business, Coldwell Banker has seen all of it. Coldwell Banker affiliated agents don't just close transactions. They hand people the keys to the places where their lives unfold. The physical letter is a beautiful way to conceptualize the ending of one family's chapter in a home by welcoming another, reminding us what a home really is."

The campaign was created with Siltanen & Partners, directed by Alice Gu. You can view all the spots in The Letter here and find behind the scenes content here to discover the story, inspiration and creative thinking behind The Letter and "120 Years of Home," the full year campaign celebrating the role home plays in shaping our lives.

FREDERICKSBURG, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When it comes to retirement planning, most people focus on how much to save and where to invest it. But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.
releases.title: Your Muscles May Be One of Your Most Valuable Retirement Assets
releases.body:
Fitness & Finance co-founders explain why preserving muscle should be part of the retirement-planning conversation

FREDERICKSBURG, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When it comes to retirement planning, most people focus on how much to save and where to invest it. But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. Maintaining strength and muscle mass as we age can help support mobility, balance and independence—factors that can influence both quality of life and healthcare needs later in life. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.

"We spend decades building a financial portfolio for retirement, but we should be building our physical portfolio at the same time," said Jennifer Scherer, co-founder of the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, registered dietitian, medical exercise specialist, certified personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio. "Muscle is one of the assets that helps protect our ability to move, remain independent and enjoy the life we worked so hard to build. Financial longevity means much less if our physical health doesn't allow us to enjoy it."

While people are focused on building their financial portfolio, they may be overlooking their physical one. Age-related losses in muscle and strength can affect mobility, balance and independence and are associated with greater risk of falls and hospitalization. Those health consequences can also create significant expenses during retirement.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), starting at around 30, our bodies naturally begin losing muscle mass. We lose 3-5% of muscle mass every decade, and while that change may happen slowly, it adds up, leaving people with weakened strength. Sarcopenia, the gradual loss of muscle mass, increases the risks of falls, broken bones, and hospitalization. These are all things that are going to dip into the financial savings that someone has accumulated for retirement.

A study published in the Journal of Frailty & Aging reports that the hospitalization costs associated with sarcopenia are around $40 billion. They report that those with the condition are more likely to be hospitalized, with it costing each person an average of over $2,300 per year. Add to that the costs that people incur outside of the hospital due to broken bones, falls, and any hired help they need due to the lack of independence. It adds up to a financial burden that people may have been able to avoid if they had worked on maintaining muscle mass over the years.

The key is to start working on building and maintaining muscle mass, regardless of what age someone is at. It's never too late to take this issue on. According to the NIH, 30% of adults over the age of 70 have trouble walking, getting up from a chair, or climbing stairs. They report that such mobility issues not only lead to a loss of independence, but are also linked to higher rates of falls, chronic diseases, nursing home admissions, and mortality. They report that the big culprit is a loss of muscle mass, and that it can be slowed down by maintaining an active lifestyle.

Here are some tips to keep in mind to help slow the muscle-mass loss problem:

  • Get active no matter what age you are. Know that you can always start slow and build it up as you get stronger. Being physically active is crucial to healthier aging.
  • Ensure that your workout routine has you lifting weights and challenging yourself. It's important to get things in there like resistance exercises. Include progressive resistance training. Muscles need an appropriate challenge to adapt and remain strong. Resistance can come from weights, machines, bands or body weight, and the program should be appropriate for the individual's health, abilities and experience.
  • Be sure to get the right foods in your diet in order to build and maintain muscle. Getting enough protein is a must in order to build and maintain muscle mass over the years. Know how much you need per day and pay attention to ensure you get it. Prioritize adequate nutrition, particularly protein. Protein provides the amino acids needed to support muscle maintenance and repair, but individual needs vary based on age, health status and activity level.
  • If you have one day that you slip or one week where you falter on your new fitness plans, don't give up. Just start again. Too often, people throw in the towel and give up, rather than simply getting back at it. Working with someone, such as a coach or trainer, can help keep you on track.
  • Build a professional team. A qualified fitness or healthcare professional can assess physical function and help create an appropriate plan for maintaining strength and mobility, while a qualified financial professional can help prepare for the financial realities of retirement. Both plans should support the same goal: maintaining independence and quality of life for as long as possible.

"One of the biggest expenses in retirement can be needing help with the things you once did independently," said Jeff Smith, co-founder of Fitness & Finance Radio, financial planning expert, personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of The Retirement Smith. "We can build a strong financial plan, but preserving the physical ability to enjoy those years is equally important. Financial planning and fitness planning have more in common than people realize: both benefit from starting early, being consistent and thinking long-term."

"Never Be," "Grow," "Get Your Money Up," "I'll Fly," "Higher Up" and "We Rise" each landed with their own moment in the spotlight. ALPHA's own story is exactly the kind that makes a debut like this hit harder. Trained and licensed as a lawyer in Zimbabwe, he walked away from a secure, respected career to chase the thing he could never actually let go of, music. It started long before law school, back when he was 13 years old breakdancing with his crew, Blade Squad, at pageants and basketball halftime shows. "I took what I understood from dancing, rhythm and movement, and turned it into rap," he says. "I tapped into my background in English literature and realized, I know how to write poems. I understand rhythm. Maybe I can do this."

'The Future Right Now' is built entirely around that idea: self belief as fuel, motivation as philosophy, the present moment as the only place the future actually gets built. "Everything I do today, everything I did all these years, has brought me here, because my future was always in the present," ALPHA says. "We Rise," was originally written back in 2014 while he was finishing his law degree. "Expect Us" channels real testimony, drawn directly from ALPHA's own experience as a practicing lawyer in Zimbabwe supporting the movement built by activist Evan Mawarire against corruption and injustice. And "Never Be" is a full display of technical firepower, stacking wordplay, literary references and mythology into bars built to be replayed just to catch everything packed inside them.

That live reputation has already put ALPHA on some seriously big stages. He has shared bills with Method Man & Redman, Ja Rule, Chali 2na and Cut Chemist of Jurassic 5, The OBGMs, Moka Only and Tanika Charles, and lit up major festival stages across Western Canada.

"I want people to hear this and see themselves inside the music," ALPHA says.

releases.title: Toronto Artist And Producer LADJI MOUFLET Channels Taino Defiance On New Single "Hatuey"
releases.body:
Spotify I YouTube I Instagram I TikTok

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toronto-based producer, DJ, and beatmaker Ladji Mouflet unveils "Hatuey," a warrior of a single that pulls its title and its spirit from one of Caribbean history's most defiant figures. Built on the hypnotic percussion and rolling low end that have become his signature, the track finds Ladji at his most physical, a record made for the dance floor that carries something much older underneath it.

The name is not incidental. Hatuey was a Taino Indigenous chief who led resistance against the Spanish conquistadors in the sixteenth century and was burned at the stake for it, choosing defiance rather than surrender. Through his mother's lineage, Ladji carries Taino heritage himself, and the parallel is intentional: a song about refusing to bend. The connection runs through the visuals too, with cover art weaving together Taino imagery and the tribal tattoos Ladji and his brother wear in tribute to that history.

Ladji built "Hatuey" the way he builds everything: alone in the studio at first, composing, producing, and arranging every layer himself before bringing in his family, team and label. The result sits at the intersection of baile and the wider electronic sounds he has spent years refining, hypnotic Afro percussion set against sleek, modern production.

That sound was shaped long before Ladji touched a fader. Raised between Harlem, the South Bronx and the Lower East Side of New York, he grew up inside a household built around rhythm. His mother, from the Dominican Republic, danced salsa on stages alongside Tito Puente and Celia Cruz. His father, Senegalese and Martinican, founded a dance and music school blending West African tradition with ballet and jazz.

That sound has already found a massive audience without a major. Ladji's breakout single "Baiana 2022" has passed 35 million streams and became an unofficial anthem of the last World Cup, shared by Tom Brady, Lamine Yamal and Wayne Rooney. "French Bossa Nova" followed with more than 44 million streams. Today Ladji reaches 1.5-2.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify and more than 350,000 followers across social platforms, all built independently through his own label, Alkebulan Records.

"Hatuey" arrives as the first single from Ladji's upcoming album, 'The Pilgrimage,' a journey back to himself, tracing his roots one track at a time and letting that heritage lead the record.

releases.title: As Live Nation Enters Its Busiest Week of the Year, New Global Report Reveals a Return to Real
releases.body:
New research spanning tens of thousands of fans worldwide explores why real-world experiences are gaining value as more of life moves online.

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This week, millions of fans will compare set-list predictions as merch lines wrap around venues and restaurants and bars fill before the show. Once the lights go down, they will share an experience that can only happen live.

In the U.S., it is expected to be the busiest week for Live Nation's fan attendance this year. The milestone reflects a much larger cultural shift playing out around the world. As more of life moves online, people are placing greater value on experiences that feel unmistakably real.

The Return to Real, a new global report from Live Nation for Brands, examines what is driving that shift and what it means for culture, commerce and brands. Drawing on multiple surveys of tens of thousands of fans worldwide, the research found that 93% of fans crave real experiences over digital ones, while 80% would rather spend on experiences than on things. Live music emerged as the world's favorite form of entertainment.

As technology becomes more deeply woven into everyday life, it is getting harder to tell what was made by a person, what was generated and what actually happened. At a concert, there is no question. The artist is on stage. You are in the room. Thousands of other people are experiencing the same thing alongside you.

"People can do almost everything from their phones now," says Russell Wallach, Global President, Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. "That's exactly why the things worth leaving home for matter more than ever. The brands building lasting loyalty are becoming part of those experiences."

For brands, that opportunity comes at an interesting moment for loyalty. While 66% of fans say they engaged with loyalty programs more than a year ago, 64% say they feel less loyal to brands, and 71% say loyalty programs feel the same. More than 9 in 10 say live music benefits would make them sign up for or switch loyalty programs.

Brands across industries are already responding.

Reserved by Spotify is using its digital platform to connect fans with live experiences. "There's just no replacement for the live music experience," says Jon Ostrow, Spotify's Head of Business Development, Live Music. "Obviously, we're a digital platform, and we've got thousands who are thinking deeply daily about how to create a more robust digital environment, but we're starting to see how digital and live can go hand in hand, creating a better experience both offline and online."

Mastercard sees exclusive access becoming a new form of loyalty. "As people place greater value on real-world experiences, access has become one of the most powerful forms of loyalty," says Monica Biagiotti, EVP, Global Consumer Marketing and Sponsorships. "Whether it's traveling to experience a bucket-list concert, discovering a new destination through music, or sharing an unforgettable night with friends and family, these experiences create lasting memories. Through the Priceless Platform and our partnership with Live Nation, we're making those moments more accessible for millions of cardholders around the world."

Lowe's is extending loyalty beyond the store. "Products may bring someone through the door, but experiences are often what make them want to come back," says Amanda Bailey, VP of Customer Marketing and Loyalty. "Music connects people through emotion. Almost everyone has a song, an artist or a concert that means something to them. Live music gives us a chance to surprise and delight our loyalty members with experiences and benefits that make those moments even better."

Across industries, brands are finding new ways to make live experiences part of how they build customer relationships. The Return to Real explores what fans value about experiences they can see, feel and share for themselves, and what that shift means for brands.

Download The Return to Real here.
