releases.title: LIMRA: Many Americans Spend More Time on Social Media in a Week Than on Retirement Planning All Year
releases.body:
Nearly 6 in 10 pre-retirees say they feel highly prepared for retirement. But new LIMRA research finds that confidence often outpaces action — 76% either have no written plan or have spent fewer than five hours on one in the past year. 

WINDSOR, Conn., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Many Americans approaching retirement spend more time scrolling social media in a single week than they spend planning for retirement in an entire year. That is one of the more striking takeaways from new research from LIMRA's 2026 Retirement Income Readiness Report, which finds a wide gap between how prepared Americans feel for retirement and how much they are actually doing to prepare.

Nearly six in ten pre-retirees (59%) — workers age 45 and older who plan to retire within 10 years — rate themselves highly prepared for retirement, and 88% say they have thought about how they'll generate income once they stop working. Yet that confidence and those good intentions are not always reflected in recent planning activity. Half of pre-retirees (50%) either have no written retirement plan or have one they haven't recently updated, and 76% have either no plan or spent fewer than five hours developing, reviewing, or updating one in the past year.

"Most Americans approaching retirement genuinely feel prepared, and that confidence matters," said Tina Beckwith, Chief Marketing Officer, LIMRA. "But confidence and planning activity do not always align. Many people who feel prepared have not put a written plan in place or have not revisited one recently. Thinking about retirement is a good start, but having a plan and actively engaging in the planning process can strengthen people's sense of preparedness for retirement."

A Week of Scrolling vs. a Year of Planning

The scale of the gap comes into focus with a simple comparison. More than a quarter of pre-retirees (26%) spent fewer than five hours in the past year planning for retirement. Meanwhile, Americans age 45 and older spend an estimated 1.5 to 2 hours a day on social media — roughly 10 to 14 hours in a single week, according to DataReportal's Digital 2026 Global Overview. For many people nearing retirement, one week of scrolling outpaces an entire year of retirement planning.

It's not that Americans aren't worried about retirement. Cost-of-living increases, healthcare expenses, inflation, and the fear of outliving their savings weigh heavily on pre-retirees and even those who feel fully prepared report anxiety about whether their money will last. The issue is that concern isn't consistently translating into preparation.

"When people spend more time on social media in a week than they spend planning for retirement in a year, the barrier clearly isn't awareness — it's action," Beckwith said. "The encouraging part is that planning is one of the few retirement variables people can actually control. You can't control the markets or inflation, but you can decide to make a plan — and that single decision changes how prepared people feel and how prepared they actually are."

Planning — Not Just Wealth — Drives Confidence

LIMRA's research shows that retirement preparedness isn't determined by savings alone. Planning behaviors and professional guidance each contribute meaningfully to how prepared consumers feel. Pre-retirees who work with a financial advisor or planner are far more likely to feel highly prepared — 77% versus 47% of those who don't — yet only 40% currently work with one. Consumers with a written retirement plan likewise report significantly higher preparedness than those without.

A Simple Way to Check Your Readiness: The Three "R's"

LIMRA's research highlights several factors that contribute meaningfully to how prepared consumers feel, including their financial resources, having a written plan, actively engaging in the planning process, working with a financial advisor or planner, and understanding how savings will generate income in retirement. Based on these findings, consumers approaching retirement can begin by considering three questions:

Readiness — Do I have the financial resources and a current written plan to support the retirement I envision?

Resilience — Does my plan account for risks such as inflation, market swings, healthcare expenses, and other unexpected costs?

Retirement Income — Do I know how I'll turn my savings into income that lasts?

Consumers who regularly revisit all three areas are more likely to feel confident about their retirement future. The takeaway from the research is ultimately an encouraging one: retirement confidence isn't reserved for the wealthy or the lucky. It's built — through planning, guidance, and a clear picture of where the income will come from. And it can start with an hour that might otherwise be spent scrolling.

About the Research

The Retirement Income Readiness Report is based on a LIMRA survey of 486 pre-retirees (workers age 45 and older who plan to retire within 10 years) and 804 retirees age 45 and older, fielded in April, 2026. Social media usage figures are drawn from DataReportal's Digital 2026 Global Overview Report, which estimates average daily social media use at roughly 1.5 to 2 hours for adults age 45–54 and under 90 minutes for adults age 55 and older.

About LIMRA

Serving the industry since 1916, LIMRA offers industry knowledge, insights, connections, and solutions to help more than 600 financial services member organizations navigate change with confidence. Visit LIMRA at www.limra.com.

releases.title: Reins launches Valuation to help contractors know and grow their business value
releases.body:
New product connects business worth with incentives that help retain the people driving growth

LAS VEGAS, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Reins, which gives contractors the tools to grow what their business is worth and their key people a real stake, announced today the launch of Valuation, a new standalone AI-powered product that gives owner-operators in the trades a clear view of what their company is worth and what they can do to increase that value.

Reins has raised $5.5 million to date from Album, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Torch Capital and Animo Ventures to level the playing field for independent business owners by giving them access to tools traditionally available to larger companies and private equity-backed businesses.

Valuation joins Reins' existing Incentives product, which helps owners create long-term incentives, including phantom stock and stock appreciation rights (SARs), as well as short-term profit-sharing plans that give key employees a real stake in the value they help create.

Reins initially developed this technology to support Incentives but saw a broader need among contractors for greater visibility into their companies' value. Valuation uses carefully developed AI agents to analyze financial and operating data, deliver a current valuation, identify the factors driving it and pinpoint opportunities for improvement.

Valuation gives owners:

  • A clear number for what the business is worth today, built from the owner's own financial and operating data, including QuickBooks and ServiceTitan data.
  • Visibility into what is holding that number back and how the business compares with peers.
  • Guidance on what to do next, including the incentive plans, KPIs and targets that can help move the business forward.

"Independent business owners spend years building companies that support their families, their employees and their communities, but they haven't always had access to the same sophisticated tools larger companies use to understand and grow their value," said Chris Buttenham, co-founder and CEO of Reins. "We want to change that. Valuation gives owners a clear picture of what they have built, shows them where they can create more value and connects that insight to Incentives so they can give key people a real stake in helping the business grow."

Valuation begins with the owner's own books and operating data to establish what the company is worth today. Its agentic analysis then identifies the factors driving that value, benchmarks the business against peers and highlights the levers with the greatest potential impact. Owners can then use Incentives to align key employees with the KPIs and targets that matter most through long- or short-term plans tied to the value they help create.

"Big companies have a CFO, an appraiser and a compensation consultant a phone call away," Buttenham said. "The owner of a 30-person HVAC shop has none of that: no real number on the business, no plan for what comes next. Valuation is how we level that. It gives independent owners the leverage private equity and big corporations have had for decades."

Valuation and Incentives run on the same data and are designed to work in the background of the business an owner already operates, without adding administrative burden or requiring a consultant. Together, they help contractors understand what their business is worth, act on the factors that can increase that value and build a stronger company with more options when the time comes to sell, hand off or step back on their terms.

For more information about Reins, visit myreins.com.

About Reins

Reins is the ownership operating system for independent businesses, giving owners the tools to understand and grow their business value while giving key employees a real stake in the value they help create. Through Valuation and Incentives, Reins helps owners understand what their business is worth, identify opportunities to increase its value and create long- and short-term incentive plans without giving up ownership or control. Reins works with hundreds of owner-operators in the trades, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, restoration and landscaping, who have granted more than $50 million in incentives to key employees through Reins. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Reins is backed by Album, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Torch Capital and Animo Ventures.. Learn more at myreins.com.

releases.body:
Landmark $16.68 billion states settlement prompts Legal Bay to expand lawsuit funding for qualified victims and families pursuing individual claims involving alleged social media-related injuries and deaths.

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Legal Bay LLC, a national leader in pre settlement funding, lawsuit funding, legal funding, and settlement funding, announced today that it is actively considering funding applications from qualified plaintiffs pursuing social media addiction, personal injury, and wrongful death lawsuits following Meta's landmark settlement with 29 U.S. states.

Meta recently agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion to resolve state allegations that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to addict children, misrepresented platform safety, and improperly collected children's personal data. The agreement also requires significant changes intended to protect younger users, including usage restrictions, stronger age-verification measures, and additional safeguards surrounding potentially harmful content. Meta has denied wrongdoing.

The historic settlement represents an important development in the rapidly expanding litigation surrounding social media platforms and alleged harm to children and teenagers.

Thousands of individual personal injury cases remain separate from the states' settlement. These lawsuits allege that addictive platform features contributed to serious injuries among young users, including depression, anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm, suicidal ideation, attempted suicide, and, tragically, suicide deaths. More than 3,300 personal injury claims have already been consolidated in California litigation involving allegations of social media addiction and related harm.

Legal Bay is now providing pre settlement funding for qualified individual plaintiffs and families pursuing these claims, including parents who have filed wrongful death lawsuits following the suicide of a child allegedly associated with social media addiction or harmful online content.

Chris Janish, CEO of Legal Bay, commented, "The size of this settlement demonstrates that allegations surrounding social media addiction and youth safety have become a major area of litigation. Behind these cases are real children and families who have suffered devastating consequences, including self-harm and suicide. Legal Bay is now prepared to evaluate qualified cases for funding and provide financial assistance to victims and families while their attorneys pursue accountability."

If you or your child suffered serious psychological injury, self-harm, attempted suicide, or other damages allegedly related to social media addiction—or if you lost a loved one to suicide and are pursuing a wrongful death claim—Legal Bay is now accepting qualified cases for pre settlement funding. Please visit Legal-Bay HERE or call toll-free at 877.571.0405.

Individual lawsuits may involve allegations that social media companies knowingly incorporated features designed to maximize engagement among young users despite potential risks. Claims have focused on compulsive use and exposure to harmful content, as well as psychological and behavioral injuries. The social media companies have disputed allegations that their platforms caused plaintiffs' injuries and continue to defend individual cases.

Legal Bay believes the latest settlement could become an important benchmark as attorneys evaluate the continuing individual litigation against Meta and other social media companies. While no settlement or verdict guarantees the outcome or value of another case, major resolutions and bellwether verdicts can provide valuable information as mass litigation develops.

However, for families who have already endured severe psychological injury or the unimaginable loss of a child, the prospect of lengthy litigation can add another layer of stress. Drawn-out litigation can create substantial financial pressure if they are facing medical bills, therapy expenses, lost income, and other costs long before their cases reach settlement. If you are involved in an active social media addiction lawsuit and need an immediate cash advance against an anticipated settlement—or if you need assistance finding an attorney—please visit Legal-Bay HERE or call toll-free at 877.571.0405.

Legal Bay offers pre settlement funding, lawsuit funding, legal funding, settlement funding, loans on lawsuits, loans on lawsuit, and loan on lawsuit programs for qualified plaintiffs involved in complex litigation. These non-recourse funding programs provide immediate cash against an anticipated recovery, allowing plaintiffs to address financial needs while giving their attorneys additional time to pursue fair compensation. Legal Bay's funding is non-recourse, meaning repayment is required only when a plaintiff successfully obtains compensation through a settlement or verdict. If there is no recovery, there is no obligation to repay the advance.

releases.body:
A live Zoom event, Thursday, October 1, 2026, 2-3 PM ET

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The American Council of Learned Societies presents "Hashtag Humanities: Scholars, Social Media, and Knowledge for the Public Good," a virtual discussion panel, on Thursday, October 1, 2026, 2-3 PM ET.

As social media continues to play a critical role in how many people receive news and information—in some cases being their primary source—it has become increasingly important for scholars to have a significant voice on popular platforms.

Rigorous training in research and analysis gives today's PhDs in humanistic fields an advantage in the ongoing battle for revealing truth and fact in a crowded multimedia landscape.

This live Zoom panel discussion will feature three popular scholarly influencers on why and how they've built their social media followings and how they hope to change how people access knowledge beyond the academy.

Meet the Panelists:

Dr. Xavier Buck | @historyIn3

Executive Director of the Dr. Huey P. Newton Foundation, founding director of the Black Panther Party Museum in Oakland, CA, and a 2021 ACLS Leading Edge Fellow

Heather Colley | @heathercolleyauthor

PhD student in English Literature at Oxford University, author of The Gilded Butterfly Effect: A Novel (Three Rooms Press)

Dr. Dan McClellan | @maklelan

Public scholar of the Bible and religion

The discussion will be moderated by Dr. Keyanah Nurse, ACLS Senior Program Officer for Intentional Design for an Equitable Academy (IDEA) programs.

This live Zoom event is free to join and registration is required. Learn more at bit.ly/4AciCCo.

Formed over a century ago, the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) is a nonprofit federation of 85 scholarly organizations. As the leading representative of American scholarship in the humanities and interpretive social sciences, ACLS upholds the core principle that knowledge is a public good. In supporting its member organizations, ACLS expands the forms, content, and flow of scholarly knowledge, reflecting our commitment to diversity of identity and experience. ACLS collaborates with institutions, associations, and individuals to strengthen the evolving infrastructure for scholarship.

releases.title: SIRUI Wins "Best of Show", Showcases New Lenses at IBC 2026
releases.body:
LAS VEGAS, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SIRUI, an imaging brand specializing in innovative lens design and technology, showcased its latest lens innovations at IBC 2026. A major highlight of the show was the Aurora 15mm F1.6 full-frame autofocus lens receiving a Best of Show Award on September 13. At Booth 12.D31, SIRUI also featured the newly launched Saturn V2, two upcoming new focal lengths in the Aurora series, and the Swift series, alongside its established Vision Prime, Iron-Star and Astra lineups.

Aurora 15mm F1.6 Receives "Best of Show" Award

SIRUI's upcoming Aurora 15mm F1.6 full-frame autofocus lens received a "Best of Show" Award during IBC 2026 on September 13.

Combining an ultra-wide 15mm focal length with a large F1.6 aperture, the lens features a 0.3m minimum focusing distance, low distortion and a compact, lightweight design. The combination of ultra-wide coverage, large aperture and portability makes it a versatile option for full-frame creators.

The lens also reflects SIRUI's focus on optical design and manufacturing, including the in-house development and production of aspherical lens elements.

New Lens Innovations at IBC 2026

SIRUI's IBC lineup featured several recent additions across anamorphic, autofocus and lightweight imaging solutions.

The Saturn V2 drew attention with its 1.6x anamorphic design, full-frame coverage and horizontal-and-vertical shooting capability, offering greater flexibility across different production formats.

The Aurora series introduced new focal lengths while maintaining a focus on compact design and image quality. The Aurora 24mm, for example, was designed for video creators with low focus breathing and a compact form factor suited to applications including vlogging, handheld video, weddings, events and documentary production.

SIRUI also showcased its upcoming Swift autofocus lens series, developed around the "Daily Carry" concept for users seeking a compact and lightweight solution for everyday shooting. Together with the Vision Prime, Iron-Star and Astra series, the lineup demonstrated SIRUI's expanding portfolio of imaging solutions.

The two new focal lengths in the Aurora series and the Swift series are set to launch progressively over the coming months. For further details, please stay tuned to SIRUI's official store.

Connecting with Creators and the Imaging Industry

Beyond product demonstrations, SIRUI engaged with filmmakers, creators, media and industry professionals throughout the show.

At the show, SIRUI was also joined by creators Sightseeing Stan, Vi-Dan, and INDIE Filmmakers, who took part in on-site talks sharing their experiences working with SIRUI lenses and their perspectives on visual storytelling. International imaging media outlet CineD also conducted an on-site interview with the SIRUI team.

SIRUI also partnered with EVOTO and HOLLYLAND on a joint on-site check-in campaign during the show.

SIRUI's participation at IBC 2026 highlighted its latest lens developments and continued engagement with the global imaging community.

About SIRUI

Founded in 2006, SIRUI is a global brand specializing in optical imaging products and dedicated to providing professional, high-quality optical and imaging solutions for photographers, filmmakers, and imaging enthusiasts. Through continuous innovation in optical technology and product design, SIRUI strives to empower creators with greater freedom to explore, create, and bring their vision to life.

releases.title: Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival
releases.body:
Out of the Ashes receives the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize and Empire at Sea receives the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize; the two projects offer distinct approaches to climate storytelling

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Two projects supported by Agog: The Immersive Media Institute won two of the three prizes awarded today in the Venice Immersive competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Out of the Ashes, co-directed by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña, received the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize. Empire at Sea, created and directed by Peter Flaherty, earned the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize.

The awards celebrate two distinct approaches to climate storytelling. Out of the Ashes is a virtual-reality documentary about loss, memory, resilience, and rebuilding after the January 2025 Los Angeles fires. Empire at Sea is an interactive solarpunk augmented-reality drama that asks audiences to confront questions of sustainability, migration, inclusion, and collective survival.

Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

"Wendy Schmidt and I founded Agog on the belief that immersive media can bring people closer to urgent issues and help them imagine what change could look like," said Chip Giller, co-founder and executive director of Agog. "At Venice, we saw creators expand what these emerging technologies can do—and audiences responded in deeply personal ways. Out of the Ashes brought people from around the world close to the human toll of the Los Angeles fires, and many saw echoes of what their own communities have experienced. Empire at Sea shows new possibilities for filmmaking by pairing cinematic performance and an accomplished cast with the power of immersive media. Seeing both works recognized on a global stage makes us more excited than ever about immersive media's potential to advance storytelling, contribute to social change, and serve the public good."

"Out of the Ashes and Empire at Sea are ambitious, deeply human works that demonstrate the creative range of immersive storytelling," said Liz Rosenthal and Michel Reilhac, curators of Venice Immersive. "Agog made a meaningful contribution to Venice Immersive this year, not only through its support of three projects selected for competition, but also by creating spaces where artists, producers, technologists, and changemakers could experiment, exchange ideas, and form new connections. That combination of supporting individual projects and investing in the wider ecosystem is exactly what an emerging field needs to grow."

About Out of the Ashes

Narrated by award-winning actor Courtney B. Vance, Out of the Ashes places audiences within the events and aftermath of the Los Angeles wildfires. The 26-minute documentary combines first-person storytelling with volumetric reconstructions of participants' homes, created in part from their own family photos and videos. It closes by highlighting community organizations leading recovery efforts, including My Tribe Rise, Evolve Altadena, and the Palisades Recovery Coalition.

The work was created by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña and co-produced by The Mercantile Agency, Emblematic Group, and Arizona State University's MA in Narrative and Emerging Media program, with support from Agog and the MacArthur Foundation.

Out of the Ashes assets: project page | press kit

About Empire at Sea

Empire at Sea is a 22-minute interactive augmented-reality drama about climate scientists building a sustainable community on a remote oil rig after a catastrophe cuts them off from the mainland. Up to 10 audience members experience cinematic holograms around a custom interactive LED table and navigate together a story about science, sustainability, immigration, and community.

The work was created, directed, and produced by Peter Flaherty; commissioned by Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and ASU Gammage; developed with Flaherty Pictures, 4DV.ai, and NightLight Labs; and supported by Agog, the Schwarzman Center at Yale University, and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. It is scheduled to be presented at Lincoln Center in January 2027.

Empire at Sea assets: project page | website | press kit

Agog at Venice Immersive

Agog supported three projects selected for this year's Venice Immersive competition. The third, Solwata, is a mixed-reality documentary that brings audiences into the lives of communities in Solomon Islands confronting rising seas, displacement, and planned relocation. Created by NowHere Media and co-produced by Human Rights Watch and Agog, the experience is narrated and executive produced by Mark Ruffalo. Following its Venice premiere, Solwata is now being presented at the Toronto International Film Festival's Innovation Hub through Sept. 16. It will next appear at the BFI London Film Festival and COP31, the annual United Nations climate change conference.

Beyond its involvement with the three projects, Agog partnered with Venice Immersive on the occasion of the festival's 10th anniversary to shape discussions about what the next decade could hold, with a focus on impact. Throughout the festival, Agog convened creators, nonprofit leaders, funders, technologists, and cultural leaders for programming including a Smart Glasses Petting Zoo offering hands-on access to the latest emerging technology to consider ways it could be harnessed for storytelling and social good, an imagination workshop focused on expanding what is possible in immersive storytelling, and hands-on- conversations about new creative possibilities and the opportunities for immersive media to spur social change.

These activities are part of Agog's broader efforts to champion ambitious work, connect people across the immersive ecosystem, and help immersive media develop with public purpose at its center. Learn more

About Agog: The Immersive Media Institute

Agog: The Immersive Media Institute is a philanthropic organization founded by Chip Giller and Wendy Schmidt that is dedicated to helping creators and nonprofit leaders use immersive media—including virtual, augmented, and mixed reality—to imagine and build a more connected, just, and compassionate world. Agog operates as a field builder and creative partner, supporting immersive storytellers whose work addresses urgent social and environmental challenges. Learn more at agog.org

releases.title: Frank Russo Calls for Florida Crackdown on Addictive Social Media Features Targeting Children
releases.body:
Independent candidate for Governor says protecting children, parents and classrooms must come before Big Tech profits

NEW SMYRNA BEACH, Fla., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Non-party affiliated candidate for Florida Governor Frank Russo today announced that, if elected, he will support and sign legislation restricting addictive social media design features aimed at children under the age of 16.

The proposal comes as California moves forward with new protections limiting addictive features for young users - but Russo said Florida should not wait for another state or Washington to decide how to protect its children.

As a father, Russo said he understands the concerns parents have about what their children are exposed to online – from addictive algorithms designed to keep them scrolling to predatory content and pornography that can be only a few clicks away.

"This isn't about Republicans or Democrats. It's about our kids," Russo said. "Parents are doing everything they can to protect their children, but they are up against some of the largest technology companies in the world designing products to keep kids hooked. At some point, someone has to stand up for Florida families."

Russo also connected online safety directly to his experience listening to Florida educators. Teachers across the state have repeatedly raised concerns about the impact social media and constant phone use are having on student attention, behavior and learning.

"I've been listening to teachers, parents and families across Florida, and they are telling us the same thing – social media is affecting what happens inside our classrooms," Russo said. "If we are serious about improving education, we cannot ignore what is competing for our children's attention every minute of the day."

Russo said Florida should establish clear, enforceable standards for technology companies serving minors while giving parents stronger tools to protect their children.

"Big Tech has had plenty of time to police itself," Russo said. "Our children's safety, their mental well-being and their ability to learn have to come before another click, another view or another dollar in corporate profit. Florida can lead on this - and as Governor, I will."

The Russo campaign will release additional details of its proposed child online safety legislation

releases.title: MAJOR LEAGUE TABLE TENNIS ANNOUNCES LEAGUE'S MOST EXPANSIVE MEDIA DISTRIBUTION LINEUP
releases.body:
Every Season Four match will stream live on MLTT's YouTube channel and DAZN, with select matches airing on SI TV and expanded national and regional coverage

PRINCETON, N.J., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Major League Table Tennis (MLTT), the first professional table tennis league in the United States, today announced its most expansive media distribution lineup for the 2026-27 season, bringing every match live to fans through global streaming and extending selected-match and recap programming across free ad-supported streaming television, national cable, regional cable and local broadcast television.

Every MLTT match will stream live on the league's YouTube channel and DAZN throughout the 2026-27 season, which begins Sept. 11. DAZN will also make every match available on demand across its global footprint of more than 200 countries and territories. Sports Illustrated's SI TV will televise select matches on its free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channel in the United States, while Youku Sports will carry live MLTT matches in China.

Event recap programs will appear nationally on FS1 and AXS TV in the United States and on Game+ across Canada, while Gray Media, NBC Sports Bay Area & California and Angels Broadcast Television will expand MLTT's regional presence across key U.S. markets. The agreements mark the first time MLTT has secured third-party media distribution outside the United States, including live match distribution in China through Youku Sports, as well as the league's first regional recap coverage across key U.S. markets.

"In 2023, MLTT was just an idea on a blank sheet of paper. In just a few years, we've built a professional league from the ground up with a wildly engaging format that fans love and media partners increasingly want to be part of," said Flint Lane, Founder and CEO of Major League Table Tennis. "The demand for MLTT content is a great validation of the quality and excitement of our competition. We couldn't be prouder of how far we've come, and we're even more excited about where we're going. Season four will bring MLTT to more fans, on more platforms, than ever before."

The expanded distribution lineup also provides a broader national and international platform for MLTT's teams, athletes and commercial partners as the league enters its fourth season.

MLTT enters its fourth season with accelerating momentum after generating more than 76 million video views during the 2025-26 season and concluding the campaign with a sold-out Championship Weekend.

MLTT'S 2026-27 MEDIA DISTRIBUTION LINEUP

LIVE AND SELECTED MATCH COVERAGE

MLTT YouTube: Every MLTT match will stream live and free on the league's YouTube channel, with full replays and highlights available on demand.

DAZN: Every MLTT match will stream live and be available on demand across more than 200 countries and territories.

SI TV: Select MLTT matches will air on the network's free U.S. FAST channel.

Youku Sports: Live MLTT matches will be available in China.

UNITED STATES AND CANADA RECAP PROGRAMMING

FS1: Two 30-minute national recap specials will air during the 2026-27 season in the United States.

AXS TV: A slate of 16 one-hour recap shows will air nationally in the United States.

Game+: A slate of 16 one-hour recap shows will air across Canada.

REGIONAL RECAP PROGRAMMING

Gray Media: 16 one-hour recap shows will air across select Gray Media markets in Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, South Carolina and Tennessee.

NBC Sports Bay Area & California: 16 one-hour recap shows will be distributed across Northern California, Nevada and Oregon.

Angels Broadcast Television (ABTV): 16 one-hour recap shows will be distributed across Southern California, Nevada and Hawaii.

"Our media distribution strategy is built around the multiple ways fans discover and follow sports today," said Matt Parker, Senior Vice President, Marketing for Major League Table Tennis. "Every match will be available live on YouTube and DAZN. SI TV will bring select MLTT matches to its U.S. audience, Youku Sports will expand live access in China, national recap programming will introduce MLTT to new audiences, and regional outlets will connect our teams to local fans. Together, these platforms create a strong path from initial exposure to lasting fandom."

Additional broadcast schedules, air times, platform availability and local listings will be announced separately.

MLTT was advised by Range Sports on its 2026-27 media distribution agreements.

ABOUT MAJOR LEAGUE TABLE TENNIS

Major League Table Tennis is the first professional table tennis league in the United States, featuring world-class athletes competing in a fast-paced, city-based team format. Founded in 2023, MLTT is dedicated to growing participation, building fandom and establishing table tennis as a major professional sport in North America. For more information, visit MLTT.com.

FERNDALE, Mich., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lick the Plate, the original culinary, culture and music radio show hosted by David Boylan, is celebrating its 2,000th radio show this week with the legendary Scottville Clown Band, one of Michigan's oldest and most colorful musical traditions. The show was recorded on their tour bus with bandleader George Wilson providing the bands backstory plus interviews with all the band members on hand for their performance at the Cedar Polka Fest.

The milestone episode brings together two distinctly original Michigan-rooted institutions. The Scottville Clown Band has entertained audiences across Michigan since 1903, while Lick the Plate has spent more than 15 years sharing the stories of chefs, restaurateurs, musicians, artists, farmers, surfers, fishermen and unique personalities in San Diego, Detroit, Windsor and Northern Michigan.

The Scottville Clown Band's combination of music, humor, outrageous costumes and community spirit made it an ideal guest for the landmark show. The band's members come from a variety of professions, united by a love of music and entertaining. Their nonprofit organization also supports youth music education through scholarships and grants.

"I couldn't think of a more appropriate guest for our 2,000th show than the Scottville Clown Band," said Lick the Plate host David Boylan. "They are fun, unpredictable, deeply connected to Michigan and completely original. That also describes the lowbrow to highbrow spirit and range of guests we have tried to bring to Lick the Plate from the beginning. Reaching this milestone is both humbling and incredibly gratifying. I'm thankful to every guest who trusted us with their story and to our listeners, sponsors and radio partners who have kept this adventure going for so many years."

Lick the Plate began its radio journey in San Diego on independent adult-alternative station 102.1 KPRI in 2011. The radio program grew out of Boylan's popular Lick the Plate column, which launched in The Coast News in Encinitas in 2007 and is still running today.

From the beginning, Boylan designed Lick the Plate to be different from a traditional restaurant-review program. In addition to the food, the show explores the people behind the restaurants through their tastes in food and music. Guests discuss their cultural influences, favorite meals, musical tastes and interests outside their professions. The integration of music into culinary storytelling was another defining innovation with guests sharing the music that influenced their lives and careers.

The combination of food, culture, music and personal storytelling became the signature Lick the Plate format.

Following its start on the iconic KPRI in San Diego, Lick the Plate joined the Entercom San Diego group of stations, airing on KBZT-FM 94/9, KSON-FM and KXSN-FM Sunny 98.1. The program later aired on San Diego rock station 101.5 KGB, Sunny 98, and expanded its audience on The Mightier 1090 ESPN Radio.

In 2015, Lick the Plate expanded into the Detroit-Windsor market on CIDR-FM 93.9 The River, bringing Boylan back to the region where he grew up.

Lick the Plate also developed a Northern Michigan presence in 2017 through MyNorth.com, then KLT The Rock Station and Fox FM before expanding to Q100/WQON. These outlets enabled the program to showcase the chefs, musicians, growers and distinctive personalities of Traverse City and communities throughout Northwest Michigan.

The show later landed on 100.7 Ferndale Radio, where it can still be heard throughout metro Detroit and streamed worldwide and on the free Audacy and Live365 mobile apps.

Episodes have been recorded in restaurant kitchens, farms, breweries, wineries, fishing boats, circus trains and music venues. The annual "Fish Stories" series expanded the format further by combining Boylan's love of fishing and storytelling. The series has featured charter captains and anglers with shows recorded on the Pacific Ocean, Lake Michigan, Lake St. Clair and the Detroit River. Boylan is also an avid surfer and applied the fish stories concept to feature members of the Great Lakes surfing tribe that has produced many memorable shows as well.

Ferndale Radio Program Director Dave Kim had this to say about the Lick the Plate milestone landing on his station: "I've followed Lick the Plate since they landed on 93.9 The River and always loved the style and originality it brought to commercial radio. It's also a perfect fit for the eclectic mix of programing on Ferndale Radio and I'm stoked for David and this impressive milestone."

Learn more at Lick-the-Plate.com.

releases.body:
Key Takeaways 

  • Melissa Rivers will return to the red carpet for the first time in nearly two decades, joining CNN and Variety for live coverage of the 78th Emmy Awards on Monday, September 14.  



  • The fashion expert, host and author will join CNN Correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh throughout CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV's Biggest Night, bringing her signature wit and expert eye to the evening's fashion, trends and standout moments.  



  • The return marks a full-circle career moment for Rivers, who helped shape modern red-carpet coverage alongside her mother, Joan Rivers, and now returns to the carpet in a new chapter of her own.  

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Melissa Rivers is returning to where she and her mother were the first ones to turn walking into a building as an event. They helped change the conversation around celebrity fashion, pop culture, and entertainment. For the first time in nearly 20 years, the entertainment host and fashion expert will be back on the red carpet, joining CNN and Variety for live coverage of the 78th Emmy Awards on Monday, September 14.

Rivers will join CNN Correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh throughout CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV's Biggest Night, offering her signature wit, sharp perspective and expert eye on the fashion trends and the moments everyone will be talking about the next day. The special begins at 5 p.m. ET and will stream live at //CNN.com/Watch and on the CNN app for CNN's streaming subscribers. 

"It's a little surreal to think that I'm returning to the red carpet nearly 20 years later," said Melissa Rivers. "I'm excited to be back on the red carpet with CNN and Variety, but to be honest, I'm slightly terrified. Fashion has changed, the red carpet has changed, and I've definitely changed. In my opinion, red carpets have gotten a little too serious over the last few years and I hope to bring some of that fun back."

Q&A for Context 

Why is Melissa Rivers' return to the red carpet significant?

Melissa Rivers became a fixture of awards-season coverage alongside her mother, Joan Rivers, helping bring candid fashion commentary, humor and personality to the red carpet. Her return to the Emmys marks her first time back on the carpet in nearly two decades and a new chapter for Rivers.

What will Melissa Rivers do during CNN and Variety's Emmy coverage? 

Rivers will join Wagmeister and Setoodeh throughout the evening, bringing her perspective to the red-carpet fashion, emerging trends and memorable moments from television's biggest night. Wagmeister and Setoodeh will host the live special, featuring commentary and interviews with the stars and creators behind some of the year's most celebrated television. 

How can audiences watch? 

CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV's Biggest Night will stream live Monday, September 14 beginning at 5 p.m. ET for CNN's streaming and pay TV subscribers via CNN.com, CNN connected TV and mobile apps. CNN subscribers will be able to access additional Emmys content on the CNN app. 

Why is CNN and Variety teaming up for the Emmys? 

The Emmy red-carpet special is the first major activation of CNN and Variety's expanded partnership, combining CNN's global reach and multiplatform audience with Variety's entertainment industry access and expertise.  

About Melissa Rivers 

Melissa Rivers is an award-winning television host, producer, New York Times bestselling author and fashion expert whose career spans decades across entertainment, pop culture and red-carpet coverage. A longtime television personality and commentator, Rivers has built a distinct voice known for her candid humor, sharp perspective and deep knowledge of fashion and entertainment. She continues to appear across national television, digital media and podcasts as a sought-after voice on fashion, pop culture and the entertainment industry.

releases.body:
• New Chrome-based Avid Media Composer video editing and conversational media search built with Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise help creative teams collaborate securely from anywhere
  • Avid research shows editors embracing AI for practical tasks while overwhelmingly calling for technology that empowers creative control and efficiency
  • New advances to be showcased for the first time at global media and entertainment event IBC2026 in Amsterdam (Sept. 11-14)

BURLINGTON, Mass. and SUNNYVALE, Calif., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Avid and Google Cloud today announced the expansion of their strategic partnership, introducing browser-based Avid Media Composer, the company's flagship video editing platform, and an upgraded Avid Content Core, Avid's content data platform. By embedding Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise and Google BigQuery directly into Avid's post-production environment alongside media-specific AI agents and Avid tools, creators can remove the constraints of physical hardware and administrative friction. As a result, editors and directors can collaborate seamlessly from anywhere, automate repetitive tasks, and focus on storytelling.

Today's media production houses face two competing pressures: content demand is soaring, yet creative teams remain bogged down by administrative overhead. Editors often spend substantial portions of their day tagging footage, organizing timelines, and searching through fragmented archives. Furthermore, because professional editing historically required heavy, on-premises workstations, remote global collaboration has remained slow and cost-prohibitive.

New Avid research illustrates how editors are using AI to solve practical post-production challenges, helping tackle time-consuming tasks while preserving creative control. In a survey of professional editors, 79% reported using AI in their workflows, with speech-to-text and transcription cited as the most common use cases (60%). Editors are equally clear on AI's optimal role: 87% agree that AI is most valuable when empowering them to achieve their creative intentions more efficiently, while 76% say its best use is unlocking more time for storytelling. The findings also highlight the importance of integrating AI more seamlessly into established professional environments, with 63% emphasizing that AI tools require tighter workflow integration to be truly useful.

Building on milestones announced at the NAB Show in April 2026, the next phase of the Avid and Google Cloud partnership addresses these industry challenges directly. The expanded collaboration embeds Gemini Enterprise directly into Media Composer and Content Core to accelerate the creative process. By connecting an intelligent, searchable media archive directly to a browser-based timeline, the integrated solutions help streamline the industry's two most time-consuming bottlenecks: media discovery and timeline organization.

The joint announcement highlights four core pillars of technology integration:

  • Browser-based Media Composer and agentic editing: Avid's industry-standard editing platform, now available within the Google Chrome browser, enables creators to edit professional timelines in Avid Content Core. Within Media Composer, agentic AI capabilities in Avid's Ready to Edit allow editors to use natural language prompts to sync media, transcribe and align dialogue, and organize project bins, putting the focus back on editorial storytelling. In addition, an embedded Media Composer Gemini panel allows editors to generate B-roll, find stock footage, and automatically enrich media with tagging, logging, or translation using their existing Gemini accounts.
  • Semantic search in Content Core to speed up media discovery: Utilizing Google Cloud technologies to analyze and enrich media as it is imported, Avid Content Core and Gemini Enterprise automatically generate transcripts and semantic descriptions. This eliminates hours of manual logging and enables production teams to locate the exact media they need through natural language search.
  • Connected workflows from newsroom to timeline: Through Content Core Insights—built with Gemini Enterprise and BigQuery—organizations can bridge the data gap between how content is produced and how it performs. Newsrooms can plan stories and assign teams in Content Core Planning and Rundown—which coordinate assignments, resources, and program rundowns—while editors can pull matching footage into their timelines via natural language search. Final cuts then sync back to broadcast programming, with each step reflected as live production data. Broadcast and studio executives can then query plain-language insights on staffing, resource utilization, production costs, and content performance, providing complete visibility to produce and monetize content.
  • Flexible, secure hybrid cloud deployment: The Avid Content Core Site Engine links customer Google Cloud environments directly to Content Core, ensuring media processing, production intelligence, and agentic workflows are managed centrally, while compute and high-resolution assets remain securely in the customer's own cloud environment.

"Customers are asking for intelligent tools that plug seamlessly into existing workflows and scale with their creativity," said Wellford Dillard, chief executive officer of Avid. "Our expanded partnership with Google Cloud strengthens our ability to deliver secure, AI-driven innovation while keeping Avid open, interoperable, and adaptable. By bringing Media Composer to the browser and integrating Gemini Enterprise into Content Core, we are helping creative teams bypass administrative friction and focus on storytelling."

"Avid has always been a media technology pioneer, and this partnership solidifies its leadership in adopting advanced AI for film and television," said Anil Jain, global managing director of Strategic Industries at Google Cloud. "By integrating Gemini Enterprise with Avid's flagship tools, we are giving editors powerful agentic workflows and intelligent search to handle tedious production logistics. This collaboration ensures creators can stay in their creative flow and work securely from anywhere."

Avid and Google Cloud will demonstrate these end-to-end agentic workflows at IBC2026 in Amsterdam from Sept. 11-14, across the Google Cloud and Avid exhibition spaces.

About the Avid research: Avid surveyed 120 professional editors – users of Avid's post production and editing software, including Media Composer® – among its customer community in Q2 2026.

About Avid Technology, Inc.

Avid is the power behind the content that touches virtually every person on the planet. Every word, every note, every frame – every day. Powering great creators and trusted newsmakers, Avid enables everyone with a story to tell – from Emmy®, Grammy®, and Oscar® winners to rising talent. Avid pushes boundaries with end-to-end solutions that transform how content is created, managed, and monetized.

About Google Cloud

Google Cloud offers a powerful, optimized AI stack—including AI infrastructure, leading models like Gemini, data management capabilities, multicloud security solutions, developer tools and platform, as well as agents and applications—that enables organizations to transform their business for the Agentic Era. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted technology partner.

releases.body:
The Sonic Intelligence Academy unveils the SIQA Verified Registry and the SIQA Verified app, giving artists, industry, and fans a single source of truth for identifying AI music. LOS ANGELES, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SIQA (The Sonic Intelligence Academy Inc.), the independent data and verification platform for the AI music era backed by 1517 Fund, today announced the launch of the SIQA Verified Registry and the SIQA Verified app for iOS, unveiled through the company's Mid-Year AI Music Intelligence Report. The registry allows artists to register their work and gives the industry and the public a way to discover a track's origin and AI involvement.

SIQA operates the industry's first AI music charts, and this new registry extends that work, from ranking what's rising to verifying what's real. The company's guiding principle is simple: Verified, Not Flagged. Rather than policing or labeling tracks as suspect after the fact, SIQA equips artists to establish provenance up front, turning verification into a credential artists carry, not an accusation they have to defend against.

That distinction matters more than ever as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms like Spotify and Deezer faster than the industry can account for it, a shift now tracked by outlets from Billboard to Music Business Worldwide. The prevailing industry response has been reactive: identify AI tracks after release, then flag, dispute, or remove them. SIQA flips that model by verifying at the source, not flagging after the fact. The SIQA Verified Registry lets artists register and verify their work, while giving labels, distributors, DSPs, and everyday listeners a trusted way to check a track's provenance, going beyond the generic 'AI-Generated' label to classify each under the SIQA Classification Framework as Fully AI-Generated, AI-Assisted, or a Human + AI Hybrid (e.g., vocal cloning).

The SIQA Verified app identifies a song much like Shazam, and reveals its AI classification in seconds.

The companion SIQA Verified app puts that trust in your pocket. Much like Shazam identifies a song, SIQA Verified uses audio fingerprinting so anyone can discover a track's AI classification instantly, drawing on the SIQA Verified Registry to show whether a work is Fully AI-Generated, AI-Assisted, or a Human + AI Hybrid.

SIQA will also host the inaugural AI Music Awards (AIMAs) in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026 — a red-carpet celebration featuring celebrity appearances, the presentation of the first-ever SIQA Visionary Award, and live performances directed by the creators behind Xania Monet, Olivia B Moore, Chaisen Hale, EJ Rogers, and more.

The AI Music Awards are sponsored by a collective of music and tech companies including Deepgram, the real time voice infrastructure platform that powers conversational AI experiences for more than 1,300 companies, including Granola, Twilio, and Sierra.

"AI is rapidly expanding what's possible with sound and voice, which makes trust and transparency increasingly important," said Scott Stephenson, CEO of Deepgram. "We're excited to support SIQA in bringing creators, technologists, and the industry together to explore what responsible innovation can look like as this space evolves."

On November 12, the day before the awards, SIQA will host a summit (SIQA Summit) featuring panel discussions from bold, notable industry leaders of AI music, including Romel Murphy (CEO of dai+drm).

The SIQA Verified Registry is now live at registry.thesiqa.com, the Mid-Year AI Music Intelligence Report is available at thesiqa.com; the SIQA Verified app is available on the App Store.

About SIQA

SIQA (The Sonic Intelligence Academy Inc.) is an independent AI music intelligence and infrastructure company building the data, standards, and verification layer for the AI music era. Home to the industry's first AI music charts, SIQA operates on a simple principle: Verified, Not Flagged. The company is backed by 1517 Fund. Learn more at https://thesiqa.com

releases.title: Pocket Entertainment Surpasses $500M ARR as AI Reshapes How Entertainment Is Created and Scaled
releases.body:
Fueled by Pocket FM, AI entertainment ecosystem features 550,000+ creators, doubles customer retention, and generates 2.6 million hours of content annually

CULVER CITY, Calif., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pocket Entertainment, world's leading AI entertainment platform and the parent company of Pocket FM and Pocket Saga, today announced it has surpassed $500 million in Revenue Run Rate (ARR) growing 70% YOY.

The milestone reflects the continued global growth of Pocket FM, its flagship AI audio drama platform, alongside Pocket Entertainment's increasing use of AI across content creation, production, personalization and distribution.

"AI fundamentally changes the economics of entertainment businesses. Crossing $500 million in ARR, with a healthy bottom line, is a testament to that. Interestingly, Pocket FM has scaled while improving retention alongside it. That doesn't happen without having good taste." Harsha Kumar, Partner at Lightspeed.

Pocket FM remains the primary engine of Pocket Entertainment's growth. Revenue retention on the platform has increased from 44% to 76%, reflecting stronger and more sustained listener engagement. Strategic licensing and adaptation partnerships have further expanded its content offering, including a collaboration with Disney Publishing APAC that brought 36 iconic Marvel audio series episodes to Hindi-language listeners.

Over the past year, Pocket FM expanded into the UK, Germany and France, broadened its catalog across genres including Thriller and Fantasy, and launched user-generated content in the U.S., significantly increasing the volume and diversity of stories available to listeners.

This scale is translating into a growing portfolio of breakout franchises: 96 titles have each generated more than $1 million in revenue, including 13 that have surpassed $10 million.

Building an AI Entertainment Engine

Pocket FM brings together a global ecosystem of more than 550,000 creators, a purpose-built AI stack and real-time audience insights across creation, production, localization and distribution.

Real-time audience insights help identify stories that are resonating, enabling promising IP to scale faster across audiences and markets. AI reduces the time required to launch in new markets from approximately 12 months to two, allowing successful stories and IP to travel across languages and geographies far more quickly.

The result is a fundamentally different model for creating and scaling entertainment:

  • Pocket FM's creator ecosystem generates more than 2.6 million annualized hours of content.
  • The platform's library has grown to more than 770,000 titles across eight categories.
  • English-language originals and adaptations including Saving Nora, The Primal Hunter, The Duke's Masked Bride and Shadow Slave generate millions of plays, while My Vampire System surpassed 1.5 billion plays.

AI Is Opening Entertainment Creation to a New Generation of Storytellers

"AI is creating an entirely new era of entertainment, one defined by an abundance of high-quality content, the rise of single-person studios capable of creating blockbusters, and experiences hyper-personalized for every individual," said Rohan Nayak, CEO and Co-Founder of Pocket Entertainment. "We are already seeing creators build stories that generate millions of dollars, something that historically required large studios, big teams, significant budgets and years of production. We believe the next global entertainment phenomenon can come from anywhere, reach millions of people across the world, and still feel uniquely made for each of them. At Pocket Entertainment, we are building the platform for this future, fundamentally expanding who can create, what can be created, and how the world experiences entertainment."



Pocket FM listeners now spend an average of 155 minutes a day on the platform, with 51% of weekly active users engaging daily.

"I struggled to get my stories published, but now I can see them come to life with Pocket FM," said Steven Ade, writer and creator. "Pocket FM's AI creation tools help me develop ideas, build characters and storylines, and turn those ideas into stories much faster. I can spend more time being creative, create more consistently and see my stories reach audiences I never could before."

Pocket FM continues to welcome creators and writers from around the world to bring their stories to life and reach global audiences. To listen or start creating, visit pocketfm.com.

About Pocket FM

Pocket FM is the leading AI audio drama, shaping a new category of serialized entertainment for audiences around the world. With more than 250 million listeners across 20+ countries, Pocket FM combines human creativity and AI with audience insights to help more than 550,000 creators develop stories, produce audio, adapt content across languages and scale successful IP for global audiences. Pocket FM has built a rapidly growing library of more than 770,000 audio series, creating an entertainment ecosystem where creators can bring their ideas to life and reach audiences around the world. Pocket FM is headquartered in Bengaluru and Culver City, California, and is operated by parent company Pocket Entertainment.

About Pocket Entertainment

Pocket Entertainment is the world's leading AI entertainment platform building products that help creators create, produce, distribute and monetize entertainment at global scale. Its portfolio includes Pocket FM, the leading AI audio drama platform, and Pocket Saga, its AI microdrama platform. Founded in India in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Nishanth KS and Prateek Dixit, Pocket Entertainment combines human creativity and AI to make audio and video entertainment creation faster and more accessible, enabling creators to develop high-quality entertainment, reach audiences across languages and geographies, and scale successful IP globally.

Pocket Entertainment is building a future of hyper-personalized entertainment, where individual creators can build global blockbusters that once required large studios, teams and budgets. Pocket Entertainment is headquartered in Bengaluru and Culver City, California, with offices in San Francisco, Berlin and Mumbai.

releases.title: Korean Cultural Center New York presents Yunie's Magical Adventure: A Musical Dreamscape for the Whole Family
releases.body:
Friday, September 25, 2026 at 6 PM

Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 4 PM

Theater at the Korean Cultural Center New York

(North American Premiere) 

NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY), a branch of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea, will present the North American premiere of Yunie's Magical Adventure: A Musical Dreamscape for the Whole Family for two performances on Friday, September 25 at 6 PM and Saturday, September 26 at 4 PM at the theater of the Korean Cultural Center New York as part of the "KCCNY Curates" series. Co-presented by KCCNY and MIRI Opera, the imaginative family music theater production blends live music, multimedia storytelling, and participatory play to create an engaging and interactive experience for young audiences and families.

Timed around Chuseok, often described as Korean Thanksgiving and one of Korea's most important traditional holidays, the production brings beloved Korean children's songs and traditional games to life through the vibrant sounds of Western classical and Korean traditional music. Through music, movement, and imaginative play, the performance celebrates the spirit of togetherness and shared memories while offering children and families a joyful introduction to Korean culture.

The story follows Yunie, a curious young girl who travels with her family to Grandma's house for Chuseok. While the adults are busy preparing the holiday feast, Yunie finds herself without anyone her age to play with. Just as she begins to feel lonely and sleepy, something extraordinary happens: tofu and bean sprouts come to life and become her new friends. Together, they enter a magical world filled with music, games, friendship, and unexpected discoveries.

Featuring a live chamber orchestra (New York Classical Players), colorful visuals, animation, and interactive storytelling, Yunie's Magical Adventure introduces audiences to some of Korea's most beloved traditional songs and games, including Kkomaya Kkomaya (Little Child), Mugunghwa Flower Has Bloomed (Korean Red Light, Green Light), Dong Dong Dongdaemun (Gate Game), Toad, Toad (Sandcastle Game), Hide-and-Seek, and Ganggangsullae (Circle Dance).

At its heart, Yunie's Magical Adventure explores universal themes of family, friendship, imagination, and belonging, creating a playful space where young audiences can discover Korean traditions while sharing the joy of music and play together.

Admission is free and open to the public, but pre-registration is required.

Synopsis

With Chuseok, one of Korea's most important traditional holidays, just around the corner, Yunie's family is busy shopping in a bustling marketplace. It is a cherished Korean tradition to make wishes under the full moon during Chuseok—but oh no, it's raining! Will Yunie and her family be able to see the full moon on Chuseok night?

On the morning of their trip to Grandma's house, cheerful Yunie sets off hand in hand with her loving mom and dad. But once they arrive, all the adults are busy preparing the holiday feast. With no other children her age around, Yunie begins to feel lonely and bored—and maybe even a little sleepy. Then, just as she is about to drift off, something extraordinary happens. Yunie's eyes open wide as a magical world begins to unfold before her!

Creative Team

Storyteller: Sung Yeena

Orchestra: New York Classical Players

Conductor: Kim Dongmin

Production: MIRI Opera

Original Story / Composition / Artistic Direction: Park Sungsun

Script: Yang Inyong & Chung Jooeun

Character Design / Animation / Media Art: Kim Hyeran

Storyteller Sung Yeena is a New York City–based actor, songwriter, and creative whose work spans theater, film, music, writing, and visual storytelling. Originally from South Korea, she is especially interested in stories of belonging and nuanced Korean and Korean American identity. Yeena holds an MFA from Columbia University and a BFA from NYU Tisch School of the Arts.

The production is led musically by New York Classical Players under conductor Kim Dongmin, with original story, composition, and artistic direction by Park Sungsun. The script is by Yang Inyong and Chung Jooeun, with character design, animation, and media art by Kim Hyeran. Together, the creative team combines live music, theatrical storytelling, and visual media to create an immersive world for young audiences.

About MIRI Opera Company

MIRI Opera Company is a creative and performing arts collective founded by artists who share a vision of building a "beautiful community" through the arts. Its parent organization, InterEduArt, was established in 2010, and the group has been active under the name MIRI Opera Company since 2017.

MIRI Opera Company oversees the entire creative process in-house—from performance planning and scriptwriting to composition and production—and has presented more than 200 performances across Korea. The company is also active in arts education through educational content development, teacher training programs, and professional consulting.

About New York Classical Players

New York Classical Players (NYCP) is a dynamic chamber orchestra redefining how classical music lives in our time. Founded in 2010 by music director Kim Dongmin, NYCP brings together exceptional musicians committed to artistic excellence, collaborative music-making, and meaningful engagement with audiences.

Through adventurous programming, commissions, premieres, recordings, and collaborations with leading artists, NYCP connects established repertoire with the music of the present. Based in the New York metropolitan area, the ensemble works closely with cultural institutions, presenters, and community partners to bring exceptional live music to audiences across New York City, northern New Jersey, and beyond.

About the Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY)

The Korean Cultural Center New York (KCCNY), a branch of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea, was established in December 1979 to promote Korean culture and foster cultural exchange in New York. KCCNY presents a wide range of cultural and artistic programs, including exhibitions, performing arts, film, educational workshops, and more. At its home at 122 E 32nd Street in Manhattan, KCCNY serves as a cultural hub where audiences can discover and experience the richness of Korean culture.

About KCCNY Curates

KCCNY Curates is the flagship performance series of the Korean Cultural Center New York, dedicated to showcasing distinctive and innovative works of Korean performing arts in the heart of New York City. Launched in conjunction with KCCNY's theater, the series embodies the Center's curatorial vision by introducing exceptional productions that combine artistic excellence and creative exploration.

Featuring distinguished Korean artists and groundbreaking works across genres, KCCNY Curates offers New York audiences compelling opportunities to experience the dynamic spirit of Korea's performing arts scene and aims to establish itself as a signature platform for world-class Korean performing arts in New York.

For event details and RSVP, visit www.koreanculture.org and follow @kccny on Instagram.

For inquiries: Hyo Han (Program Director of Performing Arts), hhan@koreanculture.org

releases.title: Public Service Announcement - Canadian War Museum launches The Long War, a podcast exploring Canada's role in the Afghanistan war
releases.body:
OTTAWA, ON, Sept. 10, 2026 /CNW/ -- In the wake of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks against the United States, Canada joined the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan to pursue al-Qaeda and unseat the Taliban. More than 40,000 Canadians served. Over the course of the war, more than 1,500 were wounded and a diplomat and 158 Canadian soldiers died. Now, 25 years later, the Canadian War Museum is launching a new podcast that delves into the history and legacy of this overseas mission, which forever marked Canadian military history.

The Long War: Canada in Afghanistan offers a compelling examination of Canada's 13-year mission. Hosted by journalist Anna Maria Tremonti and guided by War Museum historian Andrew Burtch, the series traces the arc of Canada's role in the conflict -- from early victories and attempts to build a democratic state, to the counterinsurgency and the final fall of Kabul. It revisits key moments from the war, while also exploring its complicated legacy.

The series incorporates historical documentary recordings, War Museum oral histories, and original interviews conducted for the podcast. Listeners will hear from military leaders, diplomats, veterans, and policymakers, including former Chief of the Defence Staff General (Ret'd) Wayne Eyre; Major-General (Ret'd) David Fraser; Elissa Golberg, the Representative of Canada in Kandahar in 2009, and current Canadian Ambassador to Italy; and former Cabinet minister and Deputy Prime Minister John Manley. By focusing on the voices of the people who were there, the podcast combines powerful firsthand storytelling with thoughtful reflection upon a defining chapter in Canadian military history.

Eight episodes cover the history and legacy chronologically:

  • The Fall and the Beginning
  • Into Battle (2001–2002)
  • Defence, Diplomacy, Development (2003–2006)
  • Operation Medusa (2006)
  • Home Front (2006–2008)
  • The Grind (2007–2010)
  • A Long Goodbye (2010–2014)
  • Reckoning

Full descriptions and links are available on the Museum website, and on all major podcast platforms. The first episode is available today; the remaining episodes will be released weekly over the next two months.

The Long War: Canada in Afghanistan will be launched September 10 at the War Museum, with a special in-person panel discussion featuring some of the people interviewed for the podcast. Tickets can be purchased from the War Museum website. This event is presented in conjunction with The World at War Speaker Series, an annual program of compelling lectures presented by the War Museum. A list of upcoming events is also available.

This year also marks the fifth anniversary of the collapse of the Afghan government to the Taliban, and the 20th anniversary of Operation Medusa, one of the toughest battles in Afghanistan for both the Canadian Army and NATO.

Many voices heard in The Long War come from the War Museum's oral history project, In Their Own Voices: Stories From Canadian Veterans and Their Loved Ones. Both of these projects have been generously funded by donors including the A. Britton Smith Family; the Azrieli Foundation; Arthur B.C. Drache, C.M., K.C., and Judy Young Drache; The Royal Canadian Legion; The Legion National Foundation; Friends of the Canadian War Museum; the Crabtree Foundation; Robert Stollery, in honour of his service in the Second World War; Colonel (Ret'd) Stanley A. Milner, O.C., A.O.E., M.S.M., C.D., LL.D.; and individuals from across Canada.

The Canadian War Museum is Canada's national museum of military history. Its mission is to promote public understanding of Canada's military history in its personal, national and international dimensions.

For more information, visit warmuseum.ca. Follow us on Twitter, Facebook or Instagram.

If you would like to have your name removed from our distribution list or if this information should be directed to someone else, please send an email to Avra Gibbs Lamey.

releases.title: Response Media launches RE:HEALTH to Address Pharma's $300 Billion Adherence Blind Spot¹
releases.body:
New health and life sciences practice debuts AdherenceIQ, an AI-powered platform that predicts patient adherence risk

ATLANTA, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Medication nonadherence costs the U.S. healthcare system as much as $300 billion annually. Despite significant investments in awareness, patient acquisition, and new prescription generation, life sciences companies struggle to identify which patients will start/discontinue therapy and understand the emotional barriers driving those decisions.

Response Media launches health and life sciences practice to address pharma's $300 billion adherence blind spot

Response Media today announced the launch of RE: HEALTH, a specialized health and life sciences practice built to help pharmaceutical and health brands close that gap.

Backed by decades of healthcare marketing expertise, RE: HEALTH combines behavioral science, privacy-compliant AI and advanced analytics to help brands identify the emotional barriers to treatment and translate that intelligence into engagement strategies that improve adherence, persistence and TRx growth.

"Medicine is an emotional decision but the industry has marketed it as a functional one," said Josh Perlstein, Response Media CEO. "We believe there is a smarter approach, and it begins with focusing on the human behind every treatment."

With the launch, the company is introducing AdherenceIQ, a proprietary, AI-powered behavioral intelligence platform that predicts and addresses therapy adherence risk before drop-off occurs.

Built on published adherence science, AdherenceIQ identifies the emotional and functional barriers preventing patients from starting or continuing therapy, predicts who is most likely to disengage and why, and recommends intervention strategies based on those barriers.

For chronic and rare disease therapies, where adherence and persistence are critical to patient outcomes and commercial performance, AdherenceIQ shifts the focus from measuring attrition to identifying patients at risk of disengaging while there is still an opportunity to intervene.

"Adherence is too often treated as a reminder problem," said Dr. Alvin Glay, chief strategy officer, RE:HEALTH. "But patients don't make decisions based on reminders. Concerns about side effects, necessity, distrust, and stigma all shape their decisions. We can now uncover those barriers early enough to intervene in a relevant, human way that not only improves patient outcomes but accelerates TRx growth."

About Response Media: Ad Age's Data & Insights Small Agency of the Year in 2025, Response Media is a performance marketing agency specializing in data-led CRM/CX strategy and media. First-ever summit, themed "Putting AI to Work", will draw companies from the Fortune AIQ 75 prestige list, and beyond

NEW YORK and SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fortune today announced its first-ever Fortune AIQ Summit, scheduled to take place on Oct. 1 in New York City in partnership with ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW), the AI control tower for business reinvention. The one-day event will convene top executives and industry innovators advancing AI across industries to explore how organizations can deploy it profitably while preparing their people to thrive alongside it.

The invite-only AIQ Summit, hosted at the New York Stock Exchange, will also draw attendees and speakers from the Fortune AIQ 75 list (debuting Sept. 29). The prestigious Fortune AIQ 75 list ranks Fortune 500 companies generating significant, measurable impact from AI adoption.

The event will feature cross-industry conversations offering actionable insights on what separates successful AI implementations from stalled pilots. Participants will explore how to identify the right use cases, redesign workflows, and scale AI across an enterprise to deliver quantifiable business outcomes.

The Fortune AIQ Summit program will span sectors such as finance, technology, energy, healthcare, and industrial manufacturing. The list of early confirmed speakers include:

"AI only matters when it drives real business impact," said ServiceNow's Paul Fipps. "Fortune AIQ 75 leaders put governance and visibility at the center of their strategy. They know exactly what their agents are doing and why it matters. Context and control are the difference between an AI promise and a scalable operation that positions organizations for competitive advantage."

Fortune and ServiceNow created the AIQ initiative to help business leaders navigate AI-driven transformation, grounded in ServiceNow's Enterprise AI Maturity Index, which assesses AI readiness and usage across companies worldwide. The AIQ initiative offers business leaders resources to implement and maximize AI's value and insights into where AI is reshaping industries and driving future innovation. Explore the Fortune AIQ hub presented by ServiceNow here.

Fortune also partnered with ETR to develop a methodology for evaluating Fortune 500 companies on their AI implementation. This methodology is supported by an ETR-designed survey of technology leaders assessing both the value of their organizations' AI investments and their impressions of AI adoption among peer companies in their sector.

The Fortune AIQ Summit expands Fortune's portfolio of premier conferences and convenings, including the Fortune Global Forum, Brainstorm Tech, Brainstorm AI, and the Most Powerful Women Summit, further strengthening its role as a platform for the world's most influential business leaders.
