releases.title: Surfside Names Lars Djuvik Chief Revenue Officer as It Expands Retail Media Platform Beyond Cannabis and Alcohol
releases.body:
Former Crealytics and Pentaleap executive joins as Surfside expands its retail media platform across grocery, convenience and other fragmented retail categories.

NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Surfside, the advertising operating system built for the retail majority, today announced that Lars Djuvik has joined the company as Chief Revenue Officer.

Djuvik joins Surfside as the company expands the infrastructure it built in cannabis and alcohol into grocery, convenience and other retail categories. Together these make up the "retail majority": the thousands of independent, specialty and regional retailers that account for the majority of consumer spending.

As Chief Revenue Officer, Djuvik will lead Surfside's revenue organization across both sides of that network: expanding partnerships with retailers while scaling the demand organization serving agencies, suppliers and advertisers.

"Lars understands something fundamental about retail media: the merchant, the media and the transaction have to work together, all in service of the shopper," said Michael Blanche, co-CEO of Surfside. "He has spent his career on every side of that equation. As we take the infrastructure we built in some of the most complex retail environments and bring it to a much larger market, there are very few people with his combination of retailer, brand, agency and adtech experience."

Djuvik brings more than 25 years of experience across advertising, commerce and retail media. He most recently held leadership roles at Crealytics and Pentaleap, the retail media technology company launched by Crealytics. He also held leadership positions at Shopkick, acquired by SK Planet and now part of Trax Retail; Interactive Media Holdings, which became the publicly traded demand-side platform Viant; and Freeosk, whose in-store sampling platform has operated across major retailers including Sam's Club and Albertsons.

Surfside built its platform in two of the most heavily regulated categories: cannabis and alcohol. Its technology connects onsite, offsite and in-store media activation with transaction data and measurement at the source, allowing retailers and brands to evaluate performance against point-of-sale outcomes while retailers retain ownership of their customer and transaction data.

The company has been extending that infrastructure to regional grocers, convenience stores, liquor retailers, gas stations, specialty retailers and other businesses that have often been excluded from retail media because of fragmented point-of-sale systems, loyalty programs and data environments. Surfside enables these retailers to participate in a unified, addressable network while giving advertisers a more efficient way to reach and measure custom audiences.

While Surfside also partners with the largest retailers, its core mission is this underserved retail set, which accounts for roughly 80% of consumers' everyday shopping.

"Surfside doesn't get paid on impressions or guesses; it gets paid on performance tied directly to point-of-sale data," said Djuvik. "The cash register, not a click, is the source of truth. That is the standard I've chased throughout my career. Surfside has built the infrastructure to give the retail majority access to meaningful advertising demand without requiring them to hand over ownership of their customer relationships."

Djuvik said Surfside's ability to connect advertising with the moments when purchasing decisions are made was another factor in his decision to join.

"The greatest opportunity is often the day or two before an event, when customers are filling their carts or planning their everyday shopping," Djuvik added. "Surfside helps brands, and especially their agencies, understand and act on those high-value moments while giving retailers a direct role in the media economics surrounding their customers. What sealed it for me, though, wasn't just the technology. It's the team. This is a group of retail media and adtech operators who've actually built and scaled this from the ground up."

Surfside has already expanded into grocery and convenience, with additional retail categories to follow.

About Surfside

Surfside is the Advertising OS for the Retail Majority. One platform connects brands, retailers, and shoppers across every channel, built on purchase data from thousands of independent and regional stores that standard retail media fails to activate. Brands get high-intent audiences and inventory they cannot buy anywhere else. Retailers turn transactions they already process into revenue. Every campaign is measured against real sales.

WILMINGTON, Del., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Factor Cybersecurity, Inc. and founder and CEO Jason Thompson have filed a federal lawsuit against SecurityScorecard, Inc. and CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.
releases.title: Factor Cybersecurity Files Federal Lawsuit Against SecurityScorecard and CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy
releases.body:
Lawsuit follows Factor's efforts to expose an alleged competitor hacking operation and alleges a campaign of retaliation intended to silence those who brought the conduct forward

WILMINGTON, Del., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Factor Cybersecurity, Inc. and founder and CEO Jason Thompson have filed a federal lawsuit against SecurityScorecard, Inc. and CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.

Read the complaint and follow the case here: https://factorcyber.com/factor-vs-securityscorecard

The complaint alleges that while Thompson was an executive at SecurityScorecard, he witnessed Yampolskiy and others engage in efforts to improperly obtain competitor technology and information. Thompson reported his concerns internally, including to SecurityScorecard's board, and alleges that Yampolskiy subsequently threatened and retaliated against him.

The complaint alleges that Yampolskiy told Thompson he had relationships with Russian hackers and paid individuals thousands of dollars to obtain nonpublic information about competitors including BitSight, Black Kite and Panorays. It further alleges that Yampolskiy repeatedly accessed competitor systems through a VPN from SecurityScorecard's offices, activity witnessed by multiple employees, and that information obtained from competitors influenced SecurityScorecard's product development and commercial strategy.

"Sunlight is the best disinfectant," said Thompson. "Factor is proud of the work we have done to expose and disrupt what we allege was a sophisticated operation targeting companies in the cybersecurity community. We did what cybersecurity professionals are supposed to do. We investigated, preserved evidence, identified witnesses, reported what we found and stood up for the companies and people being targeted."

Factor maintains that dozens of current and former SecurityScorecard employees witnessed relevant conduct and that substantial documentary and electronic evidence exists.

"The irony of Yampolskiy accusing Factor of stealing data and misappropriating trade secrets while Factor's complaint alleges that SecurityScorecard engaged in efforts to improperly obtain competitor information is impossible to ignore," said Thompson.

The Need for Supply Chain Cybersecurity Solutions is Real

The need for a new approach is increasingly clear. Verizon's DBIR found that breaches involving third parties grew from 15% in 2024 to 48% in 2026, underscoring how quickly supply chain cyber risk is accelerating. Meanwhile, legacy market players are collapsing under high churn, customer dissatisfaction, and notably poor security outcomes. Factor was built to address a need traditional ratings and assessment platforms were never designed to meet, bringing together internal telemetry, outside-in intelligence, assessments, attestations, and secure communications so enterprises can continuously detect and respond to supply chain threats much like they do inside their own SOC.

"While this case is an extreme example, business relationships can create real threats to enterprises and their intellectual property," said Thompson. "Factor is designed to identify and snuff out these risks, moving organizations beyond a compliance-focused approach to lightning-fast detection and response across their supply chain."

About Factor

Factor is the AI-powered operational platform for supply chain cyber risk management. Designed to help enterprises operationalize risk intelligence from best-in-class technology providers, Factor enables organizations to automate workflows, improve supplier engagement, reduce operational costs, and strengthen cyber resilience across their extended enterprise ecosystem. Through its growing Factorverse partner ecosystem, Factor provides customers with the flexibility to integrate the data, intelligence, and services that best meet their needs. releases.body:
LOS ANGELES, Calif., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vision Films announces the worldwide Transactional VOD release of Isolation on September 22, 2026, through a deal with Legacy Distribution. The intense drama was directed and produced by James Drake Coleman and co-produced by Joe Barajas of Regardless Productions. Isolation was filmed in various locations across Texas starting in Austin that crisscrossing the state from Monahans Sandhills State Park in West Texas to the Pineywoods forest region of East Texas.

Originally an award-winning 16-minute short film, this passion project of Coleman's became a full-length feature made possible by angel investors. Coleman, who also stars in, edited and scored the film, credits the support of friends for making his cinematic dream come true.

The dystopian adventure follows Logan, a prisoner aboard a desolate spacecraft, as he undertakes dangerous missions to retrieve alien artifacts in exchange for a chance at freedom. His only companion is the ship's onboard messaging interface, "AMI." As Logan faces isolation and danger, the film explores questions of purpose, survival, and the nature of his own mind. Watch the trailer: HERE

Lise Romanoff, CEO and Managing Director of Vision Films says, "You will never quite know what is real or a trick of the isolated and paranoid mind of this space prisoner. Isolation will keep you riveted and guessing until very last scene."

Filmmaker James Drake Coleman shares, "I feel so blessed to have been able to make this film with such extraordinary people. Though our crew was extremely small, we packed a punch. I wanted to make this film with the psychology of isolation always at the forefront and to draw the audience into that space, even in the quietest moments. Everything was deliberate and I made the film I saw in my head. I couldn't have done it without the support and love from everyone who helped create it."

Isolation stars James Drake Coleman (Divorce Tears from the Alpha, But I Shine Alone), the voice talent of singer, actress, producer and flutist Sheilava (Callbacks), Timothy Banfield (The REAL Thunderbolts Story), Erv Brown (Armstrong: Dark Secrets), Chiara McCarty (LBJ: Triumph and Tragedy).

releases.title: Consumers Want AI Shopping Recommendations to Include Trusted Creator Perspectives, According to IAB
releases.body:
Global study finds 56% of consumers prefer AI-generated shopping recommendations that incorporate creator perspectives, with Gen Z and Millennials leading the shift

NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Artificial intelligence is becoming an everyday shopping companion, helping consumers research products, compare options and make decisions. But as AI plays a larger role in product discovery, with nearly three-quarters (72%) of consumers using general-purpose AI assistants for shopping-related decisions, brands and AI platforms face a growing challenge: delivering recommendations consumers view as credible and trustworthy.

Ahead of the first IAB CreatorFronts, Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade association for the digital advertising industry, released new global research examining how consumers value creator perspectives in AI-generated shopping recommendations. The study surveyed 2,200 consumers who have used AI for shopping-related research in the past three months, spanning the U.S., U.K., Australia, Mexico and India.

The findings reveal a clear opportunity for AI platforms to bring trusted creator perspectives into the shopping experience. More than half of consumers (56%) prefer AI-generated shopping recommendations that incorporate creator or influencer perspectives, while 65% say they are more confident in AI recommendations when those recommendations are informed by credible creator reviews.

"AI is reshaping how consumers discover and evaluate products, but as these tools become a more influential part of the shopping journey, trust will be a critical differentiator," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "Creator perspectives can help strengthen confidence in AI-generated recommendations by bringing credible human voices into the experience. That's an important opportunity for the industry to embrace as AI continues to reshape commerce."

Younger Consumers Are Leading the Shift

The appetite for creator-informed AI is particularly strong among younger generations. About 65% of Gen Z and Millennials prefer AI recommendations that incorporate creator perspectives, compared with 53% of Gen X and 34% of Boomers. Among Gen Z, creator reviews incorporated into AI recommendations are nearly as influential as brand or advertiser information, at 27% versus 29% respectively.

Creators are also increasingly being discovered through AI itself. Half of Gen Z and Millennials have discovered creators through AI, and nearly three in four say creator-backed recommendations increase their confidence in AI shopping advice.

Authenticity and Expertise Matter More Than Popularity

Consumers are not simply looking for AI to surface the biggest names. The research finds that authenticity and expertise are key drivers of creator trust.

The most trusted creator types are:

  • Everyday consumers (52%)
  • Professional reviewers (43%)
  • Subject-matter experts (37%)

The top factors that make a creator trustworthy enough for AI to rely on their content are:

  • Credibility (46%)
  • Consistency (40%)
  • Expertise (36%)
  • Independence from brands/sponsorship transparency (34%)

"What we're seeing is that with AI shopping, consumers don't just want the recommendation. They want real-world experience and expertise behind the guidance," said Jack Koch, SVP, Research & Insights at IAB. "Our research shows that trusted creator perspectives can increase confidence in AI-generated recommendations, creating an opportunity for platforms to bring more authentic human expertise into the shopping experience."

AI Is Already an Established Part of the Shopping Journey

Eighty percent of consumers are comfortable relying on AI recommendations, creating new opportunities for creator content to play a role throughout the shopping journey. Consumers see the greatest value in creator-informed AI recommendations when finding the best value (38%), discovering products (32%), comparing options (31%) and summarizing product information (31%).

Creator-Informed AI Resonates Across Markets

The value consumers place on credible, authentic creator content is evident across the five markets studied, signaling a global opportunity to bring more human experience into AI shopping recommendations.

Among consumers who have used AI tools for shopping research in the past three months, those in India and Mexico place the greatest value on creator-informed shopping experiences. Compared with consumers in the U.S., U.K., and Australia, they are more likely to want creator perspectives incorporated into AI recommendations and to view creator content as a valuable input to shopping guidance. Among Western markets, the U.S. is the most creator-receptive, while the U.K. is generally the most cautious.

Across all markets, however, the foundation of creator value is consistent: expertise, authenticity, and real-world product experience.

These global shifts in AI-assisted shopping and creator influence will be among the themes explored at IAB's inaugural CreatorFronts, part of IAB Global Creator Week, bringing together platforms, creators, agencies and marketers to examine the future of creator-driven marketing.

To access IAB's Global Creator Research, click here: https://www.iab.com/insights/the-creator-signal/ 

About the Research

The IAB Insights Engine study, powered by Attest, was conducted in May 2026 among 2,200 consumers who had used an AI tool for shopping-related research in the previous three months. The study included 1,000 respondents in the U.S. and 300 respondents each in the U.K., Australia, Mexico and India.

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. releases.title: LiveU Offers Starlink for News and Sports Broadcast as Clarus Integrated Reseller
releases.body:
The new offering extends LiveU's connectivity platform, giving field teams access to cellular service and Starlink broadband as a managed service

HACKENSACK, N.J., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LiveU is now a Clarus Integrated Reseller, bringing Starlink's fast, reliable broadband directly into LiveU's cellular bonding EcoSystem through a single plan for broadcast, sports, and field production teams. LiveU Hybrid Data is the first integrated data plan that provides field teams access to cellular and Starlink broadband for the broadcast IP bonding market.

It's a shift that reflects how Starlink is being used as a primary connectivity solution across live production: not as a fallback for extreme scenarios but bonded alongside cellular to keep broadcast operations online in remote areas and through outages and disruptions.

With Hybrid Data, LiveU delivers and invoices for cellular data and Starlink in one managed service. Both connections sit side by side in the same workflow, so your broadcast can use cellular and Starlink together in the moment. LiveU serves as the single source for support.

LiveU Hybrid Data will be available for LiveU's LU300S, LU800, and LU900Q field units, across the United States and United Kingdom.

At the heart of LiveU's resilient connectivity solutions are two core technologies. LiveU Reliable Transport (LRT™) bonds cellular, Starlink, and other IP connections into a single reliable stream, trusted by more than 5,000 customers worldwide for their day-to-day live transmission. LiveU IQ (LIQ™) continuously analyzes network conditions to dynamically select the best-performing cellular operators for any given location.

"LiveU has always been focused on keeping customers live from anywhere," said Gideon Gilboa, Chief Business Officer, LiveU. "Crews get a connection that adapts to whatever the field throws at them, a congested stadium, a rural dead zone, a remote shoot with no cell tower in range. But beyond the connection itself, what our customers increasingly want is simplicity: all their connectivity solutions under a single pane of glass – cellular and Starlink broadband as a packaged service – managed and supported by LiveU, through one plan and one point of contact. That's what Hybrid Data gives them."

LiveU will showcase its full connectivity portfolio at IBC2026, Stand 7.C24. To arrange a meeting or demonstration, visit https://get.liveu.tv/ibc-2026/.

About LiveU 

LiveU is the global leader in live IP-video solutions, transforming live video into real value. From breaking news and major sports events to enterprise communications and public safety, LiveU enables reliable and efficient live production and visual intelligence at scale. LiveU offers a comprehensive, modular IP-video EcoSystem spanning the entire live production workflow. Our solutions are powered by the resilient, low-latency LRT™ (LiveU Reliable Transport) protocol and further strengthened by LiveU IQ (LIQ™), which leverages AI–driven connectivity for optimal performance. With a strong focus on automation, LiveU reduces manual processes to help organizations deliver innovative, story-centric live productions – streamlining scheduling, content creation, ingest and orchestration. Supporting digital–first, hybrid and cloud–based workflows, LiveU provides flexible, scalable and future-proof solutions that support remote productions, on-premises/cloud integration, and multi-platform distribution. Actus Digital, a LiveU company, and the value leader in its space, combines quality assurance monitoring and compliance logging in a unified, affordable Actus X platform. Trusted by over 5,000 customers in more than 150 countries, LiveU is an American company, headquartered in Hackensack, New Jersey, and a multi-award winner. For more information, visit www.liveu.tv, or follow us on X, Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn or Instagram.

releases.title: Centrus and Radiant Announce Long-Term Partnership for Domestic HALEU to Supply Kaleidos Microreactors
releases.body:
Agreement adds another domestic, U.S.-origin source of HALEU to support commercial and national security deployments of Radiant's Kaleidos microreactors

Adds another HALEU customer to Centrus' backlog and includes prepayments to Centrus that advance its build-out of domestic enrichment capacity

BETHESDA, Md., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Centrus Energy Corp. [NYSE: LEU] ("Centrus"), a trusted supplier of nuclear fuel and services, and Radiant, a leading developer of transportable plug-in ready nuclear microreactors, today announced a definitive multi-year contract to supply high-assay, low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel needed to deploy multiple Kaleidos microreactors. Under the agreement, Centrus will begin delivering HALEU before the end of the decade, adding another domestic source of fuel to support commercial scale-up of Radiant's Kaleidos fleet.

The contract further strengthens Centrus' position as a leading fuel supplier for next generation nuclear technologies while expanding its role in the emerging microreactor market. The agreement includes Radiant prepayments to Centrus to support its domestic commercial enrichment capacity program. For Radiant, the contract adds another domestic source of HALEU as the company moves from its first Kaleidos test toward commercial and national security deployments, reinforcing the fuel supply it continues to build in parallel with the reactor itself. 

"The contract with Radiant marks another important step in building the domestic fuel supply chain needed to support the next generation of nuclear energy," said Amir Vexler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Centrus. "By expanding our work to include innovative microreactor developers like Radiant, we are strengthening the U.S.-based fuel supply network. This will help ensure that emerging nuclear technologies have access to the reliable fuel they need to reach commercialization and meet growing demand for clean, secure, and dependable energy."

"You can't deploy nuclear reactors without fuel, so we have approached our fuel supply the same way we have approached the reactor: build it in parallel, and don't depend on any single path," said Dr. Rita Baranwal, Chief Nuclear Officer of Radiant. "This agreement gives Kaleidos a continued source of HALEU for commercial and national security applications and removes one of the biggest constraints facing advanced nuclear deployment. We're securing the fuel supply chain alongside the reactor so that when Kaleidos is ready to deploy at scale, the infrastructure behind it is ready too."

Because Centrus' technology is U.S.-origin and relies upon a U.S. manufacturing supply chain, the enrichment that Centrus provides to Radiant will be "unobligated" – meaning that it can be used for national security applications. Centrus' AC100 centrifuge design is the only deployment-ready U.S.-origin technology available for unobligated enrichment today. Radiant is developing transportable microreactors designed to provide reliable power for remote locations, data centers, defense applications, and/or other commercial and industrial uses, representing a broad potential market for Centrus' domestic HALEU supply.

About Centrus

Centrus Energy is a trusted American supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry, helping meet the growing need for clean, affordable, carbon-free energy. Since 1998, the Company has provided its utility customers with more than 1,850 reactor years of fuel, which is equivalent to more than 7 billion tons of coal. With world-class technical and engineering capabilities, Centrus is pioneering production of High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium and is leading the effort to restore America's uranium enrichment capabilities at scale so that we can meet our clean energy, energy security, and national security needs. Find out more at www.centrusenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

About Radiant

Radiant is a leading developer of advanced nuclear technologies focused on delivering reliable, resilient, and scalable energy solutions that are transportable by land, sea and air. Radiant is committed to enabling a new generation of nuclear applications for commercial, industrial, and defense customers.

NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As educators, students, and families begin a new academic year, the Planet Classroom Network is celebrating a major milestone: more than 1,000 educational films showcasing the ideas, creativity, and leadership of the next generation of storytellers, scientists, artists, innovators, and changemakers from around the world.
releases.title: Planet Classroom Network Surpasses 1,000 Global Films, Showcasing the Next Generation of Storytellers, Scientists, and Changemakers
releases.body:
As students return to classrooms worldwide, Planet Classroom launches its September Back-to-School Collection—ten inspiring new films exploring artificial intelligence, climate resilience, healthcare innovation, creativity, culture, and human connection.

NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As educators, students, and families begin a new academic year, the Planet Classroom Network is celebrating a major milestone: more than 1,000 educational films showcasing the ideas, creativity, and leadership of the next generation of storytellers, scientists, artists, innovators, and changemakers from around the world.

To mark the start of the school year, Planet Classroom today announced its September Back-to-School Collection—six new premieres and four Spotlight selections curated to inspire classroom discussion, critical thinking, creativity, and global citizenship.

Produced by CMRubinWorld, Planet Classroom has grown into one of the world's leading free educational streaming platforms, connecting learners with filmmakers, educators, scientists, entrepreneurs, healthcare innovators, climate experts, artists, and youth leaders through original films and conversations that make today's biggest global challenges accessible to audiences everywhere.

"What Harry and I hoped to create was never simply a place to watch films," said C. M. (Cathy) Rubin, Founder and CEO of the Planet Classroom Network. "We wanted Planet Classroom to become a place where curiosity leads learning, where young people meet extraordinary thinkers and creators, and where every story opens the door to a larger conversation about the future we are building together."

Launched during the COVID-19 pandemic, Planet Classroom has evolved into a global learning community featuring more than 1,000 films created by over 400 filmmakers and curators from across six continents. Today, its growing collection explores the defining issues shaping the twenty-first century—from artificial intelligence and climate change to healthcare, education, sustainability, culture, creativity, and social innovation.

A Global Classroom Without Borders

Planet Classroom believes that some of the world's most meaningful learning happens through storytelling.

Its original series—including AI for a Better World, Net Zero Speaks, Problem Solvers, Earth's Champions—and collaborations with organizations including Protect Our Planet (POP), KIDS FIRST! Film Festival, and Actuality Abroad, bring together students with internationally recognized scientists, entrepreneurs, artists, educators, physicians, engineers, environmental leaders, and filmmakers.

Every film is designed to encourage inquiry, discussion, and action while supporting educators seeking engaging, real-world learning experiences for their classrooms.

The September Back-to-School Collection

This month's collection explores some of the most important questions facing today's students.

Artificial Intelligence & The Future of Humanity

The September collection opens with AI for a Better World: What Does It Mean to Be Human in the Age of AI?, featuring internationally acclaimed artist, futurist, and "Bionic Pop Artist" Viktoria Modesta in conversation with C. M. (Cathy) Rubin. Together they explore creativity, identity, human augmentation, and why our uniquely human imagination may become our greatest strength in the age of intelligent machines.

Students can also explore AI through two new Problem Solvers films: Could AI Replace Colonoscopies For Cancer?, examining how artificial intelligence may improve early colorectal cancer detection, and David at Davos, an original fictional animated short imagining how a young climate entrepreneur works alongside Gemini AI to transform complex climate research into a compelling presentation for world leaders.

Climate Resilience Begins Locally

In Net Zero Speaks with David W. DuBois, host Ivan Ransom speaks with New Mexico State Climatologist David W. DuBois about how extreme heat, prolonged drought, water scarcity, dust storms, declining snowpack, and air quality are reshaping everyday life across the American Southwest—and why trusted local climate information is becoming essential for building resilient communities.

Stories That Build Empathy

Award-winning director Jaime Torres brings audiences to Hoi An, Vietnam, in Hearing & Beyond, the inspiring story of a young deaf woman whose life is transformed through education, friendship, and community.

Meanwhile, creator Cameran Small explores one of popular culture's most beloved franchises in Do Fans Like Disney-Era Muppets?, examining how audience engagement, nostalgia, and storytelling continue to shape entertainment.

September Spotlight: Timeless Stories Worth Discovering

Planet Classroom's September Spotlight also celebrates four remarkable films from its growing archive.

Viewers can experience AIKĀNE, a visually breathtaking animated short inspired by Hawaiian history, mythology, and Indigenous storytelling, directed by Academy Award® nominee Daniel Sousa with Dean Hamer and Joe Wilson; Eternal Illusion, Daniel Gomez Sancho's visually stunning animated art film that transforms personal grief into a moving meditation on healing through sculpture, 3D printing, animation, and movement; Lori Belilove's The Revolutionary at NYFW, an unforgettable New York Fashion Week performance honoring the enduring legacy of dance pioneer Isadora Duncan; and Jesus Thief, Kyle Wyborski's heartfelt coming-of-age comedy about friendship, faith, forgiveness, and finding the courage to do the right thing.

Together, these ten films reflect Planet Classroom's belief that education extends far beyond textbooks—that stories have the power to spark curiosity, build empathy, encourage critical thinking, and prepare young people to navigate an increasingly interconnected world.

Supporting Educators Worldwide

Every Planet Classroom film is available free through the Planet Classroom Network and is designed to support educators, schools, universities, libraries, museums, and youth organizations seeking engaging resources that encourage inquiry, creativity, collaboration, global awareness, and meaningful classroom discussion.

As classrooms reopen around the world this September, Planet Classroom invites educators everywhere to discover new voices, new perspectives, and new conversations that inspire lifelong learning.

Watch the September Back-to-School Collection

The complete September collection premieres throughout September on the Planet Classroom Network YouTube Channel.

releases.title: WLRN PUBLIC MEDIA NAMES TOM HUDSON CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER FOLLOWING NATIONWIDE SEARCH
releases.body:
Veteran journalist and public media leader takes permanent helm of WLRN; Carlton Gillespie to succeed Hudson as host of The Florida Roundup as Hudson prepares to relaunch The Sunshine Economy this fall

MIAMI, Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- WLRN Public Media today announced that Tom Hudson has been named Chief Executive Officer, following a nationwide search for the organization's next permanent leader. Hudson, who has been serving as Interim CEO, will now officially take the helm of one of South Florida's leading public media organizations.

The appointment marks a new chapter for WLRN — and a return to familiar territory for Hudson, whose career at the organization has spanned newsroom leadership, award-winning journalism, statewide public affairs programming and some of WLRN's most ambitious coverage of South Florida's economy.

"This is a critical time for public media and Tom has the right mix of journalistic integrity, collaboration and innovation to take WLRN into the future," said South Florida Public Media Group Board of Directors Chair Cheryl Wilke. 

As CEO, Hudson will lead WLRN's television, radio, digital, journalism and community engagement operations while helping shape the organization's strategy for reaching and serving audiences across a rapidly changing South Florida.

"WLRN has an extraordinary opportunity to build on the trust we have earned in South Florida while finding new ways to be essential to the communities we serve," said Hudson. "That means Florida-focused journalism, compelling local programming, meaningful community engagement and creating more opportunities for South Floridians to understand and participate in the issues shaping this region. I am incredibly proud of this organization, the community which supports it and excited about what we can build together."

Hudson has spent much of his career at the intersection of journalism, economics and public media. He previously served as WLRN's Vice President of News and later returned to the organization as Senior Economics Editor and Special Correspondent. Earlier in his career, he was managing editor and co-anchor of PBS' Nightly Business Report. At WLRN, he also helped create and host programs that became fixtures for audiences across South Florida and the state.

With his move into the permanent CEO role, Hudson will step down as host of The Florida Roundup, WLRN's weekly statewide public affairs program covering the politics, economy, environment, culture and news shaping Florida.

WLRN Broward County Bureau Reporter Carlton Gillespie will take over as host of The Florida Roundup. Gillespie began his career at WLRN as an intern and has grown into one of the newsroom's recognizable voices, most recently covering Broward County and regularly contributing to The Florida Roundup as a reporter, expert guest and fill-in host. His appointment represents another important step in WLRN's commitment to developing journalistic talent from within the organization. Gillespie's journalism recently was recognized with a national Edward R. Murrow award.

Hudson, however, will not be leaving the microphone entirely.

This fall, he plans to bring back The Sunshine Economy, the signature WLRN program he created and hosted for a decade exploring the people, businesses, industries and economic forces transforming South Florida.

The program, which originally ran from 2013 to 2023, took listeners beyond economic statistics to tell the stories of the people behind them — from entrepreneurs and CEOs to workers, policymakers and community leaders — while examining issues ranging from housing and tourism to technology, climate change, employment and the region's evolving business landscape.

Hudson will once again serve as host when The Sunshine Economy returns to WLRN radio and podcast audiences this fall.

And its return will begin with a live conversation about where South Florida's economy is headed next.

On September 23, Hudson will host and moderate the WLRN Sunshine Economy Summit 2026, a major gathering of business leaders, policymakers, community experts and other key stakeholders examining the opportunities and challenges defining South Florida's economic future. Gillespie and WLRN Palm Beach County Reporter Wilkine Brutus will also serve as panel moderators.

Hudson hopes to use the Summit as a launching point for the next chapter of The Sunshine Economy, turning the conversations taking place on stage into the beginning of a renewed, ongoing dialogue with South Florida audiences.

"The economy touches virtually every part of our lives — where we live, how we work, what we earn, how our communities grow and what kind of South Florida we are building for the future," Hudson said. "There has never been a more interesting or important time to tell those stories. The Sunshine Economy Summit gives us an opportunity to bring people together around those questions, and I'm looking forward to carrying that conversation back to our listeners this fall."

Hudson's appointment comes at a pivotal moment for WLRN as the organization continues to expand its reach, deepen its local journalism and strengthen its connection with audiences and communities throughout South Florida.

His new role brings together the different chapters of his WLRN career — journalist, host, newsroom leader and executive — around a single mission: ensuring WLRN remains the beacon of trusted journalism, storytelling, culture and public service for the region it calls home.

About WLRN Public Media

WLRN Public Media is an award-winning public media organization serving South Florida through radio, television and digital platforms. Through independent journalism, educational programming, original storytelling, arts and cultural content and community engagement, WLRN connects audiences throughout Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Monroe counties and beyond with the information and programming that help them better understand their communities and the world.

releases.title: A Journey into the Unconscious: New Book Offers an Approachable Introduction to Carl Jung
releases.body:
Clinical psychologist Claire Hillenbrand Sherman pairs Jungian theory with reflection, journaling, active imagination and creative exercises

OLDENBURG, Ind., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "Discover Wholeness with Carl Jung and His Red Book," by clinical psychologist Claire Hillenbrand Sherman, translates Carl Jung's analytical psychology into an approachable guide to self-awareness, personal growth and psychological wholeness.

Aimed at readers who may be curious about Jung but find his original writings challenging, Sherman explains the relationship between the conscious and unconscious mind through clear descriptions of his central ideas.

Jung's personal experiences, particularly those documented in "The Red Book," provide a foundation for the discussion. After separating professionally from Sigmund Freud, Jung began an extended period of introspection in which he explored dreams, symbolic images and imagined inner figures. He recorded conversations with these figures and created artwork and mandalas as part of his effort to better understand the unconscious. Those experiences helped shape the analytical psychology for which he later became known.

Sherman connects that history to concepts including the ego, persona, shadow, collective unconscious, archetypes, complexes, projection, and anima and animus. At the center of the book is individuation, Jung's term for the process of recognizing and integrating the many conscious and unconscious aspects of the personality. The goal is not to eliminate conflicting qualities, but to develop a fuller understanding of how they influence behavior, relationships and a person's sense of identity.

The book also gives readers opportunities to apply the ideas through reflection questions, writing activities and creative exercises. Among the practices Sherman presents are active imagination, a method Jung used to engage with images and voices from the unconscious, as well as journaling, dream exploration, mindfulness and mandala-making. The exercises are designed to help readers identify patterns, consider overlooked parts of themselves and connect abstract psychological concepts with personal experience.

Throughout the book, Sherman distinguishes psychological wholeness from perfection. Instead, she presents it as a continuing process of becoming more aware of the full range of one's personality, including qualities that may have been ignored, rejected or left undeveloped. By combining explanations of Jung's theories with practical opportunities for reflection, "Discover Wholeness with Carl Jung and His Red Book" offers readers a framework for examining identity, relationships, creativity, spirituality and the unconscious forces that can shape everyday life.

releases.title: GeeLark Advances Cloud Phone Infrastructure for Scalable Social Media Operations
releases.body:
SINGAPORE, Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Social media work is increasingly mobile-first. From publishing short-form video to managing content across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and other platforms, many everyday workflows still depend on native mobile apps.

For agencies, brands, and content teams managing multiple clients, campaigns, or regional operations, that creates a practical challenge: as mobile workloads grow, so does the number of Android environments a team needs to manage.

Traditionally, adding more mobile capacity meant adding more physical devices. Cloud phone technology offers a different approach by turning Android environments into remotely accessible, software-managed infrastructure.

The Hidden Cost of Managing More Physical Phones

Physical smartphones work well when a team only needs a few devices. At a larger scale, however, the work around those devices can become a burden of its own.

Teams need to purchase and replace hardware, keep devices charged, manage operating system and app updates, maintain network settings, provide remote access, and keep track of which device belongs to which client or project.

Large collections of physical smartphones are sometimes loosely described as a "phone farm," but for legitimate social media teams, the more practical issue is often much simpler: every additional device adds another piece of hardware that needs to be stored, maintained, accessed, and organized.

The challenge is not the smartphone itself. It is the operational complexity that comes with managing physical hardware as mobile workloads grow.

Turning Android Devices Into Cloud-Managed Infrastructure

A cloud phone changes that model.

Instead of tying an Android environment to a physical phone sitting on a desk, a cloud phone runs remotely and can be accessed through a computer. Teams can create mobile environments when they need them, organize them by project, and manage them from a central workspace.

In this model, the Android environment becomes a software-managed resource rather than a piece of hardware that must always be physically available.

That distinction matters for distributed teams. A device no longer has to be passed from one employee to another or remain plugged in at a particular office. Team members can access the mobile environment remotely while keeping project resources organized in one place.

The shift is less about replacing smartphones entirely and more about giving businesses another way to manage mobile capacity.

How GeeLark Makes Cloud Phones Easier to Manage

GeeLark brings cloud phones into a centralized workspace designed for mobile-first social media operations.

Each GeeLark cloud phone operates as a separate Android environment with its own storage, app data, login sessions, and network configuration. This allows teams to keep different projects and mobile workflows organized without relying on a growing collection of physical devices.

Teams can also configure cloud phone environments based on project requirements, including Android versions, device models, language, location, and network or proxy settings.

For an agency managing different brands or regional campaigns, for example, cloud phone profiles can be grouped and organized by client or project. Access can be managed across team members, while the environments themselves remain available remotely through the same workspace.

This centralized approach makes it easier to answer basic operational questions that become harder as a team grows: Which environment belongs to which project? Who needs access to it? What configuration does it use? And how can the team manage more mobile workflows without adding the same amount of physical hardware?

From Remote Access to Automated Mobile Workflows

Moving Android environments to the cloud reduces hardware-management work. The next efficiency gain comes from reducing repetitive actions inside those environments.

GeeLark combines cloud phones with automation tools for mobile workflows. Teams can use ready-made automation templates for common tasks, build custom in-app workflows with RPA, or use APIs to connect cloud phones and automation tasks with their own internal systems.

For content teams, this can mean preparing content in advance, assigning workflows to different cloud phone environments, scheduling repetitive publishing tasks, and reviewing execution results without manually operating every device one by one.

For teams with more specialized processes, RPA provides a way to turn repeated Android app actions into reusable workflows. Technical teams can go further by using APIs to connect cloud phone operations with existing content systems, scheduling tools, scripts, or internal dashboards.

The result is a more flexible approach to mobile operations: instead of scaling workloads by continually adding physical devices and manual steps, teams can manage Android environments and repeatable workflows through software.

For agencies, brands, and other teams whose social media work depends heavily on mobile apps, cloud phones provide a practical way to reduce device-management overhead while keeping mobile workflows accessible, organized, and easier to scale.

About GeeLark

GeeLark provides cloud phone and automation tools for teams managing mobile-first social media workflows. Its platform combines cloud-based Android environments, team management, automation templates, RPA, and API capabilities in a single workspace.

Learn more about GeeLark and its cloud phone platform at GeeLark.com.

releases.title: SiriusXM Names Sean Gibbons Chief Product and Technology Officer
releases.body:
Longtime SiriusXM leader will advance the Company's product experiences and technology strategy 

NEW YORK, Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SiriusXM (NASDAQ: SIRI) today announced that Sean Gibbons has been promoted to Senior Vice President, Chief Product and Technology Officer, reporting to Chief Executive Officer Jennifer Witz and joining the Company's Executive Leadership Team. In this role, Gibbons will lead product and technology across SiriusXM and Pandora, with responsibility for product strategy and development, technology platforms and engineering, automotive and streaming distribution partnerships, and advertising technology.

"Sean has helped shape SiriusXM through some of our most important product and technology transformations, including the development and successful rollout of SiriusXM with 360L," said Jennifer Witz, Chief Executive Officer, SiriusXM. "He brings more than two decades of experience, deep knowledge of our business and a strong track record of bringing together teams, technology and partnerships to deliver for consumers. Sean is a highly respected leader and the right person to help us accelerate innovation, improve the customer experience and advance the products, platforms and partnerships that will support our growth."

Gibbons' key priorities will include advancing SiriusXM with 360L and the Company's next generation of in-car experiences; shaping the long-term technology roadmap supporting SiriusXM's satellite, broadcast and streaming platforms; applying AI to improve personalization, discovery and customer service; and creating more dynamic, connected and participatory experiences across SiriusXM's in-vehicle and streaming platforms.

"SiriusXM has a unique set of assets and a tremendous opportunity to make them work together even more powerfully for listeners," said Gibbons. "We can pair the reach and reliability of satellite with the flexibility of streaming and the intelligence of AI to make it easier for people to discover what they love, stay connected wherever they listen and participate more deeply in the content and moments that matter to them. I'm excited to take on this role and help shape the next generation of the SiriusXM experience."

Gibbons joined Sirius in 2000, before the company's first satellite launch, and has held leadership roles spanning product management, engineering, automotive, streaming, content technology and strategic partnerships. During his tenure, he established SiriusXM's first formal Product Management organization and later founded and led its first Streaming organization, expanding the SiriusXM experience across mobile, web and connected-home platforms.

Most recently, Gibbons led SiriusXM's Automotive organization, bringing together product, user experience, engineering and automotive partnerships to advance the company's in-vehicle experiences and relationships with leading automakers. Across more than two decades at SiriusXM, he has played a central role in many of the Company's most significant product and technology transformations, including its evolution toward connected, software-defined vehicle experiences and hybrid satellite-and-IP services.

About Sirius XM Holdings Inc.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a complete ecosystem of advertising solutions through SiriusXM Media and AdsWizz. SiriusXM offers live, on-demand, and human-curated programming across music, talk, news, sports, and podcasts, and the company reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its platforms. With deep automotive manufacturer relationships and unique spectrum assets, SiriusXM is built to reach listeners wherever they are. The company connects fans to the voices, creators, and moments they love - creating communities where listeners engage, participate, and belong. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: https://www.siriusxm.com/

releases.title: Factor4 Announces New Integration Partnership with Tri-City Retail Systems
releases.body:
Bringing Omnichannel Gift Card Solutions to MyPOS Connect Retailers

BROOMALL, Pa., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Factor4, a leading provider of omnichannel gift card and loyalty solutions, today announced a new integration partnership with Tri-City Retail Systems, provider of MyPOS Connect, a cloud-based retail point-of-sale platform designed to help specialty retailers manage their businesses across stores, online channels, and multiple locations.

The new integration connects Factor4's gift card and loyalty technology with MyPOS Connect, enabling retailers to offer and manage physical and digital gift cards through their retail environment. The integration supports gift card sales, balance inquiries, and redemptions, including online redemption, giving retailers the ability to provide customers with a seamless gift card experience across in-store and digital channels.

MyPOS Connect is designed to support retailers ranging from independent single-store businesses to multi-location and enterprise retailers. The platform provides point-of-sale, omnichannel sales, inventory management, purchasing, customer engagement, and reporting capabilities, while allowing retailers to connect their POS environment with ecommerce platforms and other third-party applications.

Through the integration with Factor4, MyPOS Connect retailers can leverage Factor4's omnichannel gift card capabilities to create new revenue opportunities, increase customer engagement, and provide customers with a convenient way to purchase and redeem gift cards wherever they shop.

"Partnering with Tri-City Retail Systems and integrating with MyPOS Connect allows Factor4 to bring our gift card and loyalty technology to a strong network of specialty retailers," said Dan Battista, CEO of Factor4. "MyPOS Connect is designed around the needs of retailers that want a flexible and scalable platform, and our integration gives those merchants the ability to offer physical and digital gift cards, balance inquiries, and redemption across both their in-store and online channels."

"Gift cards have become an important part of the customer experience for retailers, and we wanted to provide our MyPOS Connect customers with a solution that could support both their in-store and online needs," said Michael Steg, Managing Director of Tri-City Retail Systems. "Our integration with Factor4 gives retailers a flexible way to offer physical and digital gift cards while maintaining a connected experience through MyPOS Connect. We are excited about the opportunity to provide our customers with another valuable tool to increase customer engagement and drive repeat business."

About Factor4

Factor4 provides comprehensive gift card and loyalty solutions designed to help merchants increase sales, strengthen customer relationships, and grow their brands through physical and digital gift card programs.

Factor4's RewardOS™ API enables integrations with point-of-sale systems, ecommerce websites, payment terminals, tablets, and other platforms, providing merchants with flexible solutions for managing gift card and loyalty programs across multiple sales channels.

For more information, visit www.factor4gift.com.

We're looking forward to bringing the show to an even wider audience and introducing new advertising partners to such an engaged fan base."

Rather than simply revisiting memorable moments from pop culture, The McBride Rewind focuses on the careers behind them. Guests reflect on the successes, challenges and turning points that shaped their lives, offering listeners a perspective that's both nostalgic and relevant to today's entertainment landscape.

With support from WME and Acast, the podcast will continue to expand its guest lineup while exploring new opportunities across audio, video and live programming.

releases.body:
Joins other honorees such as Anthropic, Chipotle, American Express, and many others

SAN FRANCISCO and NEW YORK, Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fast Company today announced its eighth annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list, recognizing businesses that are creating cultures where innovation can thrive at every level. Mission North earned a spot as a winner for Advertising, Marketing, and PR for a culture that puts curiosity and experimentation first.

The 2026 Best Workplaces for Innovators list recognizes 100 companies across industries such as entertainment, biotech, consumer packaged goods, marketing, education, and healthcare. To be considered, applicants detailed their investment in innovation, internal programs, and company culture. Fast Company's editors evaluated each application and conducted extensive research to develop a score for each company. A distinguished panel of judges then reviewed the top-rated companies to determine the final honorees.

"Innovation only flourishes when everyone at every level genuinely feels like they have the license to challenge assumptions, experiment with new ideas, and get the senior support to do it. Building that kind of culture makes us a better partner to our clients and a better place to work," said Tyler Perry and Bill Bourdon, co-CEOs of Mission North. "This recognition celebrates the people who make that possible every day."

Mission North reinforces its culture of innovation through close partnerships between senior and junior employees, performance incentives and recognition programs including its monthly Values Awards and Trailblazer Awards which celebrate employees who set new standards through creative solutions, novel approaches, and deeper problem-solving.

For two-time Trailblazer Award winner and Mission North communications associate Ale Orozco, that culture means "having the space to explore an idea and the support to see where it can go. We're encouraged to experiment, build on what works, and ultimately find better ways to deliver for our clients."

"The most innovative workplaces don't simply ask their employees to come up with great ideas; they create the conditions that make great ideas possible," says Brendan Vaughan, editor-in-chief of Fast Company. "This year's honorees understand that innovation is ultimately a cultural commitment that requires empowering people to think differently, take risks, and turn ideas into actions. We're proud to recognize the companies and executives who are leading by example."

Mission North is hiring communications professionals across the agency. Open roles can be found on Mission North's careers page.

releases.body:
The winner receives a $25,000 grant and will represent Canada's Francophone music scene at MaMA Music & Convention in Paris this fall

MONTRÉAL, Sept. 8, 2026 /CNW/ -- SiriusXM Canada today announced Hawa B as the inaugural winner of Nouvelles Ondes SiriusXM, a national program dedicated to discovering and showcasing emerging Francophone artists. The announcement was made at the Festival de musique émergente en Abitibi-Témiscamingue (FME) on Saturday night, following standout performances by the three finalists, Grand Eugène, Hawa B and N Nao.

Hawa B takes home a $25,000 grant and will bring her music to the international stage this October with a performance at MaMA Music & Convention in Paris. The two other finalists each receive a $10,000 grant, along with mentorship opportunities and increased visibility across SiriusXM platforms.

"It's a great honor to be the very first recipient of Nouvelles Ondes SiriusXM. I'm receiving this award at a truly perfect moment in my career. The support from SiriusXM will allow me to give my career a real boost, but above all, to bring my upcoming projects to life with the resources to match my ambitions. I'm extremely grateful and can't wait to show you what's next", said Hawa B. "This experience has given me so many opportunities to share my music, connect with new audiences and be part of an amazing community of Francophone artists. I'm so grateful to everyone who supported me along the way, and I can't wait to represent French Canadian artists in Paris this fall."

"This inaugural edition of Nouvelles Ondes SiriusXM showcased the tremendous richness and diversity of Canada's next generation of Francophone music talent," said Michelle Mearns, Senior Vice President, Programming and Operations, SiriusXM Canada. "Grand Eugène, Hawa B and N Nao each brought a distinct sound and perspective to the program and gave audiences an exciting look at the future of Francophone music in Canada. We are incredibly proud to name Hawa B as this year's winner, and to support the next stage of her career."

A national platform for emerging Francophone talent

Launched in spring 2026, Nouvelles Ondes SiriusXM was created to discover, support and showcase emerging Francophone artists from across Canada. Following a national call for submissions, Grand Eugène, Hawa B and N Nao were selected as finalists by a jury of music industry professionals.

Over the summer, the three finalists each recorded an exclusive studio performance and music video, introducing audiences across the country to their music and artistry ahead of a nationwide public vote. The finalists also performed at the Festival d'été de Québec (FEQ) in July before reuniting at the FME for the final stage of the competition.

Throughout the program, acclaimed singer-songwriter Ariane Moffatt served as the official mentor, providing guidance and support to the artists along the way.

Nouvelles Ondes SiriusXM is part of SiriusXM's ongoing tradition of supporting and elevating the best emerging Canadian music. SiriusXM continues to offer a leading platform for Canadian artists through its significant financial contributions and North American-wide reach. Through this program, the company aims to further strengthen its commitment to Francophone creativity and actively support the discovery of new talent.

Listeners can enjoy 24/7 Francophone artists on SiriusXM channels: Attitude Franco, Influence Franco, Racines Musicales, Les Tubes 80s-90s and Les Tubes Franco.

releases.title: NETWORK MEDIA GROUP ANNOUNCES LAUNCH OF NETWORK VERTICALS
releases.body:
New division launches in Fall 2026 to develop premium vertical short-form content; one of the fastest-growing new formats in global entertainment

VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 8, 2026 /CNW/ -- Network Media Group Inc. (TSXV: NTE) (OTC: NETWF) ("Network" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the launch of Network Verticals, a new division of Network Entertainment dedicated to developing, producing, and distributing premium vertical content.

Verticals are feature-length stories serialized into short episodes, typically 50 to 100 episodes, each 60 to 90 seconds. The stories are filmed in a 9:16 aspect ratio designed specifically for smartphone viewing. The genre is known for its scripted dramas and soap opera-like content and is now expanding into other genres, including unscripted true crime, comedy, music, horror, and sports.

Network Verticals marks the Company's entry into one of the fastest-growing formats in digital entertainment. Omdia, a global technology, media, and telecommunications research firm, estimates that the global vertical content market generated US$11 billion in revenue in 2025 and will reach US$14 billion by the end of 2026, with Variety projecting US$26 billion by 2030.

"Verticals are exploding because they meet the evolving needs of today's audiences, delivering short-form content to their cell phones," said Network's Chief Operating Officer, Paul Gertz. "What makes the opportunity particularly compelling is the format's strong monetization potential, with subscription and transactional revenue already growing at an exponential rate. As the business evolves to include advertising, franchises, and new distribution models, we see significant potential for premium storytelling and new revenue opportunities in this space."

Network's Vice President of Studios, Eric MacDonald, said, "Network has a long history of adapting premium storytelling to new platforms and emerging formats. We were one of a select group of production companies chosen to create original content for the innovative but short-lived mobile platform Quibi, conceived by Jeffrey Katzenberg and launched at the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic, which gave us an early opportunity to leverage our premium production experience to short-form, mobile-first storytelling."

Industry leaders are moving quickly into the space. Fox Entertainment has taken an equity stake in Holywater, the company behind the My Drama app, and committed to more than 200 shows for the platform. Disney+ has launched Verts, a dedicated vertical video feed inside its mobile app, while Netflix, Peacock, YouTube, Amazon, and TikTok are all investing in vertical storytelling as both a standalone content category and a tool for audience engagement.

Hollywood talent is following the momentum. Academy Award nominee James Franco, Jimmy Fallon, Kevin Hart, Issa Rae, and Kim Kardashian are among the high-profile talent who have entered the vertical space as producers, developers, on-screen talent, and investors.

"Verticals represent one of the most significant shifts we've seen in how audiences now regularly discover and consume content," said Derik Murray, Network's Founder and CEO. "We've consistently earned the trust of the world's A-list talent, high-profile IP holders, and global distributors, streamers, and broadcasters, and Network Verticals gives us the opportunity to bring that expertise to an evolving format and a new generation of audiences."

Network Verticals will operate as a dedicated content pipeline within the Company. Additional details will be announced in the coming weeks.

About Network Entertainment

Network Media Group is the parent company of Network Entertainment Inc.

Network Entertainment is a creatively driven production company that creates, finances, and produces award-winning film, television and digital content for audiences around the world. For more than two decades, Network has built a reputation for telling the stories of extraordinary and iconic international figures. 

Network has earned international recognition for productions including Facing Ali, which was shortlisted for an Academy Award for Best Feature Documentary; Sidney, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival, was produced in partnership with Oprah Winfrey and was released globally on Apple TV+, earning a Critics' Choice Documentary Award for Best Biographical Documentary, and a Black Reel Award for Outstanding Documentary Feature; and Sly Lives! (aka The Burden of Black Genius), a Peabody Award-winning and Emmy Award-nominated feature documentary, directed by Academy Award winner Ahmir "Questlove" Thompson. The film debuted at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival and premiered shortly after on Hulu/Disney+. Another recent release, BRATS, a feature documentary directed by Brat Pack member Andrew McCarthy in partnership with NEON and ABC News Studios, had its world premiere at the 2024 Tribeca Film Festival, went straight to #1 on Hulu upon its release, and won the 2025 ASCAP Award in the Top Streaming Film category.

Benefit concert at Nashville Palace featuring Collin Raye, Allie Colleen and more will support ARC's work

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Animal Rescue Corps (ARC), a national nonprofit animal protection organization, is inviting animal advocates and country music fans out for a night of live music Sept. 27 at the Nashville Palace, with every ticket sold helping ARC save another life.

ARC's Night at the Palace will feature performances by country music artists Collin Raye, Allie Colleen, Natalie Murphy, Angie K and Bobby Messano. Doors open at 6 p.m., and music begins at 6:30 p.m.

Proceeds from the evening will help ARC respond when animals are in need, whether that means getting a rescue team on the road, covering veterinary care or providing food and shelter for animals recovering at ARC's Rescue Center outside Nashville.

"When animals need us, we go," said Tim Woodward, executive director of Animal Rescue Corps. "That's the promise we've made. This event gives people a chance to have fun while raising critical funds, and help us keep saying 'yes' when animals have nowhere else to turn. Every person who comes out to enjoy these amazing artists is helping make another rescue possible."

ARC often steps in when local communities are facing cruelty cases or animal emergencies that are simply too large to handle alone. The organization provides the additional support and expertise needed to bring animals to safety and begin their recovery.

"There's a lot of heart in Music City," Woodward said. "You see it in the people who show up for animals, and you see it in the artists who are willing to lend their time and talent to a cause they believe in. This night is really about bringing all of those gifts together. We spend so much time focused on the work in front of us that it's nice to have a night where we celebrate what this community makes possible."

ARC's Night at the Palace will be held at the Nashville Palace, 2611 McGavock Pike in Nashville.

General admission tickets are $65 in advance and $75 the day of the show. Rail seat tickets are $75 in advance and $85 the day of the show. VIP table seat tickets are $150 and include seating on the dance floor and a swag bag. To purchase tickets, visit outhousetickets.com/events/nashville-palace-arc-09272026/tickets.

More information about ARC's work and how to support its ongoing rescue efforts is available at animalrescuecorps.org/.

About Animal Rescue Corps

Since 2010, Animal Rescue Corps (ARC), a national animal protection nonprofit organization, has provided large-scale animal rescue for communities that lack resources to address abuse. In addition to emergency rescue, ARC offers education and shelter relief. ARC's mission is to end animal suffering through direct and compassionate action and to inspire the highest ethical standards of humanity towards animals. In 2025, ARC Executive Director Tim Woodward was honored as a CNN Hero and selected as one of five finalists for the CNN Hero of the Year award. To learn more about Animal Rescue Corps, visit animalrescuecorps.org/.

releases.title: Poynter, Public Media Company Launch National Initiative on the Future of Public Media
releases.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A year after the federal government upended public radio and television stations by defunding public media, a partnership of the Poynter Institute and Public Media Company is launching the Future of Public Media Initiative — a national effort to reimagine a public media system built to serve communities for the next 50 years and beyond.

Poynter and Public Media Company will guide a process based on community needs that leads to a full set of recommendations — focused on renewing public media's purpose, definition and design principles — during early 2027. The initiative will build on groundbreaking research that offers the most comprehensive analysis available of how communities across America want media to serve them.

"We're living in an era of enormous change, where technology has connected us in new ways — but also has often isolated us from each other and from reliable information," said Sitara Nieves, Poynter's vice president of teaching and organizational strategy, who leads the effort for Poynter, a nonprofit that works to strengthen journalism.

"This is an opportunity to think expansively about a reimagined public media system that can serve the needs of our country and our communities into the future," said Tim Isgitt, CEO of Public Media Company, which seeks to cultivate vibrant local media that informs, connects and inspires communities. "Our goal is to establish a clear framework for a robust public media system that helps connect communities and provide trusted information and inspiration to all Americans for free."

The Future of Public Media Initiative will work to define the purpose of public media and what it means to serve the public interest, and propose a definition, structure, funding models and design principles for a reimagined system.

It has been a year since Congress voted to rescind more than $1 billion in future funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. CPB had distributed funding to a network of 1,500 public media stations for over 50 years, providing support for essential news, educational and cultural programming.

The Future of Public Media Initiative will engage a wide coalition – of civic leaders, public media station leaders and staff, nonprofit media and concerned citizens – in the creation of a shared framework to answer key questions about public media's future. They will use this work "to drive a recommendation for where a public media system could go and what it could look like – how it might serve the real needs of communities in this country at scale," Nieves said.

The initiative will work with a research partner, City Square Associates, which has conducted research on the needs, sentiments and opinions of over 100,000 U.S. adults.

The public sign up at futureofpublicmedia.org for regular updates.

The initiative has received initial funding from the Arthur Vining Davis Foundations and Knight Foundation. Individuals who wish to support the effort can donate through Poynter's website.

Poynter is the gold-standard for journalist professional development, and works extensively with media companies to help improve skills, ethics, editorial strategy, leadership, and sustainability. Poynter has a longstanding relationship with public media, and has worked with more than 300 public media stations — including guiding a digital transformation to increase revenue and audience. Public Media Company has worked with over 450 local media organizations in all 50 states, facilitating mergers, acquisitions, operating agreements and content partnerships that have expanded service to millions of people — work that includes launching the Public Media Bridge Fund to help at-risk stations navigate the post-CPB landscape.

releases.title: Cartwheel Launches Specialized Screens & Social Media Program for Students Struggling With Digital Stress
releases.body:
Innovative mental health program helps students, K-12 schools, and families address the impact of screens and social media on sleep, mental health, relationships, and school.

  • The program addresses growing concerns from school districts and parents about the impact of screens and social media on youth
  • Care includes targeted assessment, evidence-based clinical care, and skill building for parents and caregivers
  • The launch coincides with new state and federal investments in youth mental health and online safety

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cartwheel, the nation's largest school-centered telehealth provider, today unveiled its Screens & Social Media Program, a specialized clinical program that has been under development since last spring. The program addresses how technology affects students' sleep, mental health, relationships, and engagement at school.

Digital stress has concerned schools, families, and clinicians for years, but it has recently become a national policy priority. Across nearly 400 districts, Cartwheel clinicians have seen troubling patterns escalate: students losing sleep to their phones, conflict with parents over screen time, and social media shaping how kids see themselves and each other.

Rather than treating technology use as a problem in isolation, the program helps mental health clinicians understand its role in each student's life and build the skills for healthier boundaries.

Students receive individual and family therapy from licensed therapists and child psychiatrists on Cartwheel's care team, plus specialized assessments and family support tailored to digital-use challenges. All services require parent or guardian consent and can include:

  • Targeted screening and assessment related to screen use and digital stress
  • Individual and family therapy to build healthier digital habits
  • Optional psychiatric evaluation or medication support for students with more acute anxiety
  • Optional caregiver groups offering strategies for reducing conflict and building healthier routines at home

"During my years at Boston Public Schools, I saw how phones and social media could disrupt a student's sleep, their friendships, their ability to sit through a class," said Jillian Kelton, Senior Director at Cartwheel. "What's different about this program is that we don't just tell families to cut back — we assess what's actually happening for that student and build a real treatment plan around it. That's the kind of care schools have been asking for."

The launch comes as youth mental health and online safety draw growing national attention, including a multistate settlement with Meta worth up to $17.1 billion, with states weighing how proceeds can fund related work.

Cartwheel has made social media and screen time a core focus for years. In 2025, it convened a national conversation on phone-free schools with The Anxious Generation author Jonathan Haidt, Governor Kathy Hochul, and Indiana Secretary Katie Jenner, and this spring launched the "My Amazing Summer" Challenge to get students spending more time offline.

"Technology is part of all of our lives, and helping kids develop a healthy relationship with it takes more than simply limiting screen time," said Juliana Chen, MD, Chief Medical Officer at Cartwheel. "We want to understand how screens and social media are affecting each student and help students and families make realistic changes now while building healthier habits."

Screens & Social Media joins Cartwheel's growing portfolio of Care Programs, including School Avoidance and Big Behaviors, Big Feelings.

Across Cartwheel's care model, 58% of students with anxiety achieve full remission, moderate-to-severe depression drops threefold, absences fall 62%, and suspensions among students with prior disciplinary history fall 68%.

Learn more at www.cartwheel.org.

About Cartwheel

Cartwheel is the nation's largest school-centered telehealth provider, partnering with nearly 400 K-12 districts across 16 states. Founded in 2022 by educators and clinicians, Cartwheel provides evidence-based clinical care, including therapy, parent guidance, and psychiatry, and accepts all major insurance, including Medicaid, with free care for uninsured families.
